jobs.title: PhD Student in Philosophy with a Focus on Applied Ethics
jobs.department: IKOS - Department of Culture and Society
jobs.description_html:
Your work assignments

The doctoral project addresses ethical questions about age as a basis for priority setting in health care, with a particular focus on the challenges posed by an ageing population. The project should have a clear ethical focus but may also include empirical approaches.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20 per cent of full-time.

Your main task as a PhD student is to work on your thesis under the supervision of our staff. As a PhD student, you will take courses corresponding to 60 higher education credits. These courses aim to deepen your expertise in your specialist areas and strengthen your overall competence in philosophy. Courses are normally taught in English.

This doctoral position is a collaboration between the Division of Philosophy and Applied Ethics (Faculty of Arts and Sciences) and the National Centre for Priorities in Health (Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences). The PhD student is therefore expected to spend approximately half of their time at each division. A workspace will be provided at both units.

As a PhD student, you are expected to contribute to the research environments at both units. You will actively participate in their research seminars and relevant research activities. Your duties may also include teaching, course development and other teaching-related tasks. As a PhD student, you are expected to be present on site on a daily basis.

The doctoral project is also linked to an interdisciplinary research group comprising several PhD students and senior researchers in ethics, health economics and law, including the supervisors. The group consists of researchers from the Division of Philosophy and Applied Ethics and the National Centre for Priorities in Health at Linköping University, and the Centre for Research Ethics & Bioethics and the Department of Law at Uppsala University.

Your qualifications

You have graduated at Master’s level or completed courses with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be in advanced courses. Alternatively, you have gained essentially corresponding knowledge in another way.

At least 30 higher education credits, or the equivalent, must consist of second-cycle courses in philosophy, practical philosophy, applied ethics, bioethics, medical ethics or theoretical philosophy, or equivalent subjects, including a thesis of at least 15 credits.

Important personal skills include good collaboration and organisational skills, as well as the ability to work under supervision, independently and in a team. You take responsibility for your tasks, organise your work independently and take initiative to make progress. Great importance will be attached to personal suitability for the position.

Selection will be based on the above criteria and the documents submitted with the application. The selection process also includes interviews and reference checks.

Your ability to conduct independent research will be assessed primarily on the basis of published research (including articles) or course papers. These may be submitted as 1–2 writing samples. Evidence of the ability to plan, carry out and coordinate research projects, as well as to obtain research funding, may be advantageous but is not required. 

Fluency in English is a prerequisite for participating in the research activities and other duties described above. Knowledge of Swedish is an advantage.

Your workplace

The Division of Philosophy and Applied Ethics (see also https://liu.se/artikel/filosofi) offers courses in philosophy at first-cycle, second-cycle and doctoral levels. The division has eight permanent members of staff. Our teaching covers all major branches of philosophy: logic, epistemology, philosophy of science, history of philosophy, ethics, aesthetics, philosophy of religion and more. We also offer courses in other areas of the university, for example at the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences and the Faculty of Science and Engineering. We hold an advanced research seminar that meets on average twice a month, featuring invited Swedish and international speakers or our own academic staff. In our many interdisciplinary collaborations, we use a variety of methodological approaches and work actively with several other departments at Linköping University.

One such interdisciplinary collaboration is with the National Centre for Priorities in Health, within the Health Care Analysis Unit, Division of Society and Health, Department of Health, Medicine and Caring Sciences at Linköping University. The National Centre for Priorities in Health, the second workplace, is a national knowledge centre focusing on how limited health care resources should be prioritised. The centre is multiprofessional and, in addition to its research remit, has a strong external engagement profile, with staff advising government agencies, regions, municipalities and other actors in health and social care. The centre and its sister centre (the Centre for Medical Technology Assessment, CMT) have a combined staff of around thirty, including approximately ten doctoral students. There is an active doctoral seminar, as well as other seminars and meetings that provide opportunities for an active exchange of knowledge on issues relating to resource allocation in health and social care. The centre organises a national conference on priority setting in health and social care every two years.

The employment

When taking up the post, you will be admitted to the program for doctoral studies. More information about the doctoral studies at each faculty is available at Doctoral studies at Linköping University

The position is fixed-term and corresponds to four years of full-time employment. You will initially be employed for one year, after which your employment will be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time, based on progress against your individual study plan. The employment period may be extended to up to five years depending on the extent of teaching and departmental duties. Further extensions may be granted under special circumstances.

Starting date by agreement, no earlier than 31 January 2027.

Salary and employment benefits

The salary of PhD students is determined according to a locally negotiated salary progression.

More information about employment benefits at Linköping University is available here.

jobs.description_html:
We are now looking for a PhD student in communication systems at the Department of Electrical Engineering (ISY).

Your work assignments

The PhD project will investigate distributed and cooperative computing, learning and inference over satellite networks. The research will focus on developing communication-efficient distributed algorithms that account for dynamic network topologies, intermittent connectivity, and limited communication and computing resources.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20 per cent of full-time.

Your qualifications

You have graduated at Master’s level in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or Applied Mathematics, with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be in advanced courses in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or Applied Mathematics. Alternatively, you have gained essentially corresponding knowledge in another way. The requirement for a degree must be met no later than the time the employment decision is finalized, which occurs when the employment contract is signed.

Applicants must demonstrate strong mathematical maturity, possess excellent programming skills, and have an excellent ability to communicate in English, both orally and in writing.

Furthermore, you must be able to work independently, be goal-oriented, and have strong problem-solving skills. You must also be clear in your communication and able to collaborate effectively with others.

jobs.title: PhD student in Communication-Efficient Distributed Inference
jobs.description_html:
We are looking for a highly talented and motivated Ph.D. candidate to join our research team in scalable and secure distributed inference. This project, “Communication-Efficient Synchronization of Predictions for Distributed Intellient Systems (CESP)”, is funded by the Swedish Research Council (VR).

Your work assignments

The project aims to establish a theory for communication-efficient cooperation among distributed predictive agents, with a focus on synchronization of predictions under mismatched local contexts and models for robust decisionmaking. The project will combine tools from information and communication theory, signal processing, and statistical learning. It is suitable for a candidate who is interested in developing rigorous foundations while also validating ideas through modern distributed generative and agentic AI systems.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20 per cent of full-time.

Your qualifications

You have graduated at Master’s level in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or Applied Mathematics with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be in advanced courses in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or Applied Mathematics. Alternatively, you have gained essentially corresponding knowledge in another way. The requirement for a degree must be met no later than the time the employment decision is finalized, which occurs when the employment contract is signed.

Applicants must demonstrate strong mathematical maturity, solid programming skills, and an excellent ability to communicate in English, both orally and in writing. You must also be able to work independently, be goal-oriented, communicate clearly, and collaborate effectively with others.

We especially welcome strong applicants from backgrounds such as information theory, communication theory, signal processing, optimization and learning, applied probability and statistics, and distributed systems.

Your workplace

You will be based in the Division for Communication Systems (KS), Department of Electrical Engineering (ISY), Linköping University. The Division for Communication Systems carries out research, undergraduate and postgraduate education in communications engineering, statistical signal processing, network science, and decentralized machine learning. Welcome to read more about us at: https://liu.se/en/organisation/liu/isy/ks.

For more information about working at ISY, please visit: https://liu.se/en/article/open-positions-at-isy.

You will become a key member of a dynamic and ambitious research team led by Asst. Prof. Khac-Hoang Ngo. The team currently consists of 4 PhD students working on massive connectivity, point-cloud transmission, distributed inference, and AI security. Check the website https://khachoang1412.github.io/ and our recent relevant work, including:

• Prediction-Based Compression Using Large Language Models, IEEE BITS Inf. Theory Mag., 2026.
• Type-Based Unsourced Federated Learning With Client Self-Selection, IEEE ICC 2026.
• Type-Based Unsourced Multiple Access Over Fading Channels in Distributed MIMOWith Application
to Multi-Target Localization, IEEE Trans. Wireless Commun., 2026.

Linköping University is ranked 43rd globally in AI research, 12th in Europe, and is recognized as a leading university in Sweden in this field, according to Vinnova’s report on strategic technologies for Sweden. In addition, Linköping has been awarded “Student City of the Year” in Sweden three times.

The employment

The employment has a duration of normally four years’ full-time equivalent. Extension of employment up to five years is based on the degree of teaching and institutional assignment. Further extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances. You will initially be employed for one year, after which your employment will be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time, depending on your progress through the study plan.

jobs.title: PhD Student in Technology and Social Change
jobs.description_html:
We are now looking to recruit a doctoral student in Technology and Social Change.

Your work assignments

As a Phd student, you will devote your time to your doctoral studies and the research project of which you will be part. Your duties may also include teaching or participation in other departmental assignments, up to a maximum of 20% of full-time working hours.

You will collaborate with other researchers, while also being expected to carry out independent research in line with the project's focus. The position involves writing academic articles that will form part of your doctoral thesis, as well as presenting research findings at conferences and project meetings.

The aim of the project is to investigate how socio-technical systems change when biogas, which has previously been legitimized primarily through its function as an energy technology, is increasingly valued for several potentially competing functions. The Phd student will study how the multifunctionality of biogas affects socio-technical configurations, policy and institutional relations, and governance processes, with a particular focus on how different interests and values are negotiated across sectors and policy areas.

The research will focus on the Swedish biogas sector and will involve analysing the connections between biogas and areas such as agriculture, waste management and the circular economy, environmental governance, energy, and preparedness and resilience. The research findings will shed light on how emerging functions interact with established structures, and how new forms of governance and institutional relations develop as the role of biogas changes.

The successful candidate will be part of the national interdisciplinary competence centre Biogas Solutions Research Center (BSRC). The centre generates new and relevant knowledge through co-creation and collaboration across different academic disciplines, as well as between researchers and practitioners from the private and public sectors. BSRC brings together researchers and support resources from two universities, Linköping University and the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU), as well as around 50 private and public organisations representing all parts of the biogas system. The centre also receives funding from the Swedish Energy Agency.

The position includes completing the coursework component of the doctoral programme, comprising 66 credits, equivalent to approximately two semesters of full-time study. You will also participate in one of the weekly seminars at tema T – Technology and Social Change.

A central part of the work will involve writing academic texts in English, both independently and potentially in collaboration with others. Your doctoral thesis may take the form of a monograph or a compilation thesis based on a number of academic articles.

Your qualifications

To meet the general entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must have been awarded a second-cycle (Master's) degree, completed courses corresponding to at least 240 credits, of which at least 60 credits are at second-cycle level, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

The specific entry requirements are met by applicants who have knowledge corresponding to 90 credits in a subject of central relevance to the theme.

Documented research experience and proficiency in qualitative methods is considered a particular merit. Documented experience of interdisciplinary research is also considered a merit. A good command of spoken and written Swedish is considered a particular merit. A good command of spoken and written English is a requirement for the position. Experience of collaborating with stakeholders outside academia is considered a merit.

Relevant academic backgrounds for this position include human geography, environmental science, urban and regional planning, political science, sociology, or related fields.

We are looking for someone with good interpersonal skills who is attentive and communicative, and able to build and maintain professional relationships. You work independently, take responsibility and drive your work forward with commitment and energy. You can organize your work and manage processes in a structured and goal-oriented manner. You are committed to the objectives of the research project and contribute to its development. In addition, you are creative and innovative – you recognise opportunities, think outside the box and translate ideas into practice.

In addition to the documents you wish to submit in support of your application, you must also include a statement of intent (explaining why you wish to pursue doctoral studies), of no more than one page, together with a research proposal of no more than three pages.

The research proposal should outline a possible research project within the scope of the position and should primarily provide an insight into your research interests and the direction you might wish to pursue. The proposal is not intended to constitute a definitive doctoral project; the final research project will be developed and refined as part of your doctoral studies.

The research proposal may, for example, address the following questions: What questions are relevant to ask, and why? What theoretical approaches could inform and inspire the research? What types of material or empirical data could be studied?

Your workplace

Technology and Social Change (tema T) is a nationally and internationally leading research and educational environment, where social science, humanities and interdisciplinary perspectives on technology, science, medicine and social change are central.

Research and teaching focus on how people create and use technology, and how technological change is intertwined with knowledge, politics, practice and ethics.

Tema T offers doctoral studies as well as undergraduate and Master's-level education, focusing on issues relating to technology and social change. At undergraduate level, tema T offers Bachelor's and Master's programmes in Urban and Regional Planning, as well as courses in areas such as philosophy of science and the history of technology.

Technology and Social Change is part of the Department of Thematic Studies. Read more about the department here.

The employment

Upon taking up the position, you will be admitted to doctoral studies. Read more about doctoral studies at the respective faculties here.

The position is a temporary full-time employment, normally corresponding to four years. The employment may be extended to a maximum of five years, depending on the extent of teaching and departmental assignments. Further extensions may be granted in special circumstances.

Initially, you will be employed for a maximum of one year. The employment will then be renewed for periods of no more than two years at a time, based on progress in accordance with your individual study plan.

Starting date by agreement.

Salary and employment benefits

The salary of PhD students is determined according to a locally negotiated salary progression.

jobs.title: PhD student in Computer Science with focus on cybersecurity and privacy
jobs.department: IDA - Department of Computer and Information Science
jobs.description_html:
We are looking for a PhD student to conduct research on cybersecurity and privacy in next-generation immersive and networked systems. The position is part of SENSE-VR, an international research collaboration involving Linköping University and partners in the United States, aimed at developing efficient, secure, and privacy-preserving multi-user virtual reality (VR) systems.

Modern VR systems continuously collect and exchange sensitive information, including head movements, eye gaze, hand gestures, and other user interactions. Such information can reveal user identities and sensitive personal attributes, even when communications are encrypted. Furthermore, observable communication patterns may reveal information about user behavior. Protecting against these privacy risks while preserving responsiveness, functionality, and user experience presents important research challenges.

The research will focus on developing and evaluating novel privacy-enhancing mechanisms for networked and immersive systems, combining techniques from cybersecurity, machine learning, networking, and performance-aware system design.

Your work assignments

As a PhD student, you will develop and evaluate novel privacy-enhancing methods for immersive and networked systems. Depending on your background and interests, potential research directions include:

  • Privacy leakage and client-side defenses: Investigating privacy risks associated with motion, gaze, and other user data, and developing defenses that preserve application functionality and user experience.
  • Traffic analysis and privacy-preserving communication: Investigating information leakage through observable communication patterns and developing practical defenses that balance privacy, overhead, and performance.
  • Secure and encrypted processing: Exploring techniques such as homomorphic encryption for processing sensitive data on edge and cloud servers without exposing its contents.
  • Privacy-aware resource optimization: Optimizing privacy, latency, and resource usage across devices, edge servers, and cloud infrastructure.

Your research will combine the design and analysis of novel methods with practical implementation and experimental evaluation. You will collaborate with researchers in Sweden and internationally, including partners in the United States, and publish your findings at leading international conferences and journals.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20 per cent of full-time.

Your qualifications

You have graduated at Master’s level in computer science, computer engineering, information technology, software engineering, electrical engineering, or a closely related field, or completed courses with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be in advanced courses in a relevant field. Alternatively, you have gained essentially corresponding knowledge in another way.

We also welcome applications from students who are currently completing their Master's studies, including their Master's thesis. The eligibility requirements above must be fulfilled no later than the time when Linköping University makes its decision to employ you.

You should have a solid technical background, good analytical and programming skills, and an interest in cybersecurity and privacy research. We value candidates who enjoy exploring new ideas, solving challenging problems, and combining analytical thinking with practical implementation and experimentation. Good proficiency in written and spoken English is required.

Experience or knowledge in one or more of the following areas is considered an advantage:

  • Cybersecurity, privacy, or network security.
  • Machine learning, data analysis, statistical modeling, or algorithm design.
  • Computer networks, distributed systems, or performance evaluation.
  • Practical system development, experimental measurements, or research-oriented programming.
  • Privacy-enhancing technologies, such as traffic analysis defenses, homomorphic encryption, or privacy-preserving machine learning.

We are looking for a curious and motivated person with a genuine interest in learning and conducting research. You should enjoy working both independently and collaboratively, and have an ambition to develop your research skills and contribute to high-quality scientific research.

Your application should include a brief statement of motivation (approximately one page) describing your interest in the position, relevant technical experience, and which aspects of the proposed research you find most interesting. We encourage you to highlight your main strengths and interests, including relevant experience from coursework, projects, or your Master's thesis.

Your workplace

The Department of Computer and Information Science was founded in 1983 but its roots go back to the early 1970s. It is one of the largest computer science departments in northern Europe. Our research covers a broad spectrum of fields, from core to applied computer sciences. Its vast scope also benefits our undergraduate and graduate programmes, and we now teach courses in several engineering programmes at bachelor’s and master’s levels, as well as the programmes in statistics, cognitive science and innovative programming. Read more at  https://liu.se/en/organisation/liu/ida

You will join the Cybersecurity Division (CYBER) at Linköping University, working under the supervision of Professor Niklas Carlsson and alongside a team of PhD students, postdoctoral researchers, and senior researchers. Our research spans cybersecurity, privacy, computer networking, performance evaluation, multimedia systems, and applied data analytics. We combine theoretical and experimental approaches to address challenging research problems and regularly publish our findings at leading international conferences and journals.

You will be part of a positive, supportive, and internationally recognized research environment, with opportunities to develop into an independent researcher, publish at leading international conferences and journals, and collaborate with academic and industrial partners in Sweden and internationally.

The employment

When taking up the post, you will be admitted to the program for doctoral studies. More information about the doctoral studies at each faculty is available at Doctoral studies at Linköping University

The employment has a duration of normally four years’ full-time equivalent. Extension of employment up to five years is based on the degree of teaching and institutional assignment. Further extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances. You will initially be employed for one year, after which your employment will be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time, depending on your progress through the study plan.

jobs.title: PhD Position in Cybersecurity for Decentralised Energy Systems
jobs.department: IDA - Department of Computer and Information Science
jobs.description_html:
We are announcing a PhD student position in Computer Science at the Division of Cybersecurity (CYBER), Department of Computer and Information Science (IDA), Linköping University. Your research will make decentralised critical infrastructure such as the power grid more secure and resilient using trustworthy AI-supported methods.

Your work assignments

Power grids and other critical infrastructure are becoming decentralised and digitalised with thousands of remotely controlled distributed energy resources (DER) and assets such as solar panels, batteries and EV chargers. This adds a new entry point for attackers and attacks can spread across many systems at once. Your doctoral research will develop trustworthy AI-supported methods that help such critical infrastructure assess these risks and their consequences, detect potential attacks, reason about response, and keep operating safely.

Within this area, your thesis can build on the following research directions:

  • threat modelling, attack-path analysis and risk reasoning for critical infrastructure
  • AI-supported, robust, and privacy-preserving (for example federated) intrusion and anomaly detection for distributed and cyber-physical systems
  • cyber resilience and decision support that turn security insight into indicators and actions operators can use

The work is carried out in national and European research projects together with academic and industrial partners. You will work closely with researchers and engineers in Sweden and Europe, publish in leading security and energy-systems venues, and make research visits to partner organisations. Over the four years you will shape your own research questions within the directions above.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20 per cent of full-time.

Your qualifications

You hold a master's degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering or a closely related field, or you have completed courses with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be advanced courses in computer science, computer engineering, or electrical engineering. Alternatively, you have gained corresponding knowledge in another way.

For this position you are required to have:

  • good knowledge of cybersecurity
  • knowledge or experience of machine learning, for example for anomaly detection
  • programming skills, for example in Python
  • excellent oral and written communication skills in English

It is a merit if you also have knowledge or experience of:

  • research, for example through a Master’s thesis or scientific publications
  • intrusion detection or network security monitoring
  • basic electrical engineering, power systems or smart grids
  • large language models (LLMs) and agentic AI
  • threat modelling, attack graphs or frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK
  • privacy-preserving, federated, explainable, and trustworthy machine learning

Scientific curiosity and the ability to think independently are essential personal qualities. You should enjoy working in a team and together with researchers and industry partners in several countries. Motivate in your personal letter why you are interested in this position and why you are especially qualified for it.

Your workplace

You will be working in the Division of Cybersecurity (CYBER) at the Department of Computer and Information Science. At CYBER, the research focuses on securing the most critical functions of digital society. Through numerous national and European projects, methods are developed for areas such as verification, trustworthy AI, and AI-based cybersecurity. More about cybersecurity research at LiU can be found at: https://liu.se/en/research/cybersecurity

jobs.title: PhD Student in Biogas Solutions for a Flexible, Resilient and Sustainable Energy System
jobs.department: IEI - Department of Management and Engineering
jobs.description_html:
We are now recruiting a PhD student for a research project on biogas solutions in a flexible, resilient and sustainable energy system. The holder of this position will be a part of a national transdisciplinary center of excellence called Biogas Solutions Research Center (BSRC). Here, co-production of new and relevant knowledge is generated through collaboration between different scientific disciplines as well as between researchers and practitioners from industry and public organizations. The BSRC includes researchers and support from two universities, Linköping University and Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, as well as about 50 private and public organizations involving all parts of the biogas system. It also has support from the Swedish Energy Agency.

Your work assignments

You will conduct research in collaboration with senior researchers and other PhD students. The research will primarily focus on biogas solutions and their role in developing a flexible, resilient, and sustainable energy system. The work will involve techno-economic analyses, mathematical modelling, and case studies focusing on the value of flexible biogas production, as well as the contribution of biogas to self-sufficiency and regional resilience. The analyses will account for uncertainties related to, among other things, policy instruments and market conditions. The work will be carried out in close collaboration with industry and public-sector organizations.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work will also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20% of full-time. As a PhD student, you will have the opportunity to shape your doctoral research within the framework of the project’s research agenda, with support from your supervisors.

Your qualifications

We are looking for a motivated individual with a genuine passion for research and development.

You have graduated at Master’s level in a subject of central relevance to the field of Sustainable Systems or completed courses with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be in advanced courses of relevance for the subject.

Your degree must be completed no later than the date when the employment decision is made.

The ability to write and communicate in English is a requirement. The work will be conducted in collaboration with other researchers and industry partners, making the ability to collaborate with others essential. You should also enjoy sharing your work and results with both internal and external stakeholders.

Previous experience with energy systems analysis, mathematical modelling, techno-economic analysis, case studies, and scenario analysis is considered a merit.

Your workplace

The Division of Energy Systems is one of the leading research and educational organizations in its field, conducting research from a systems perspective with an interdisciplinary approach. This means that the focus is not only on developing technical solutions but also on understanding decision-making processes within industry and the public sector.  Both education and research are largely interdisciplinary and are conducted in close cooperation with other academic institutions, industry, and public administration. Read more at Energy Systems.

We are looking for a PhD student in flexible X-ray detectors.

Your work assignments

Flexible X-ray detectors represent a future technology that can benefit applications spanning several scientific, medical, and technological fields. Our joint project funded by the Knut and Alice Wallenberg foundation aims to realize flexible X-ray detectors by developing new organic semiconductors that can fulfil the critical requirements on flexibility, X-ray absorption, and charge transport simultaneously. jobs.description_html:
The Division of Automatic Control is now seeking a PhD student to work in the new national Center for Heterogeneous Adaptive Swarm Systems (CHASS) funded by the Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research (SSF) at the Department of Electrical Engineering (ISY).

Your work assignments

The multidisciplinary center for heterogeneous adaptive swarm systems (CHASS) is a national effort funded by the Swedish Strategic Research Foundation (SSF) to bring together leading researchers in AI, autonomous systems, robotics, and swarm intelligence to develop novel solutions for autonomous heterogeneous swarm systems for the benefit of Swedish industry and society. The vision is to make Sweden a leader in intelligent, adaptive, and trustworthy swarm systems by pioneering autonomous heterogeneous collectives of space, aerial, ground, surface, and underwater platforms that can operate as a unified intelligent entity with minimal human intervention. The research program focuses on six key themes: Drone Design, Adaptation, & Production; Perception, Sensing, & Communication; Autonomy, Localization, Mapping & Navigation; Coordination, Self-Governance, & Self-Improvement; Human Swarm Interaction; and Swarm-based Services & Socio-Technical Aspects. The PhD position in this announcement focuses on the research theme Autonomy, Localization, Mapping & Navigation.

CHASS will drive world-class research in autonomous swarm systems through a strong, stimulating, and well-connected international research environment. Research outcomes will be validated in real-world scenarios with industry and public-sector partners. CHASS will also serve as a national hub for autonomous swarm systems, promoting education, knowledge sharing, innovation, and policy development.

The position focuses on uncertainty-aware, optimization-based motion planning at the control and planning layer. You will develop scalable trajectory optimization and real-time Model Predictive Control (MPC) strategies that use the swarm’s belief state to ensure safety, maximizing information gain, and achieving reliable goal completion. Working within a collaborative and cross-disciplinary consortium, you will help bridge the gap between high-level swarm autonomy and robust physical motion execution in demanding GNSS-denied environments, such as those encountered in search-and-rescue and environmental surveillance.

Collaboration across areas within the center is strongly encouraged. As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20 per cent of full-time.

Research at the division is characterized by close integration of methodological development and practical applications. We maintain extensive collaborations with industrial partners as well as with leading research groups worldwide, providing doctoral students with excellent opportunities for international exposure and impactful research.

As a PhD student, you will join an open, collaborative, and intellectually stimulating environment that values scientific curiosity, independence, and teamwork. More information about the division is available at: https://liu.se/en/organisation/liu/isy/rt.

Department of Molecular Biology at Umeå University is seeking a PhD student in Molecular Biology, attached to national DDLS Research school in Data driven epidemiology and biology of infection. The future of life science is data-driven. Would you like to be part of this transformation? We warmly welcome your application to this unique PhD programme, with a planned start in January 2027, or as agreed. Application deadline: 19 November 2026.

Data-driven life science (DDLS) uses data, computational methods and artificial intelligence to study biological systems and processes at all levels, from molecular structures and cellular processes to human health and global ecosystems. The SciLifeLab and Wallenberg National Program for Data Driven Life Science (DDLS) aims to recruit and train the next generation of data-driven life scientists and to create globally leading computational and data science capabilities in Sweden. The program is funded with a total of 3.3 billion SEK over 12 years from the Knut and Alice Wallenberg (KAW) Foundation.

In 2026 the DDLS Research School will be expanded with the recruitment of 25 academic and 7 industrial PhD students. During the course of the DDLS program more than 260 PhD students and 200 postdocs will be part of the Research School. The DDLS program has four strategic research areas: cell and molecular biology, evolution and biodiversity, precision medicine and diagnostics, epidemiology and biology of infection. For more information, please see

https://www.scilifelab.se/data-driven/ddls-research-school/   

Data driven epidemiology and biology of infection covers research that will transform our understanding of pathogens, their interactions with hosts and the environment, and how they are transmitted through populations. Research will have a strong focus on computational analysis or predictive modelling of pathogen biology or host-microbe systems for which multidimensional, genome-scale experimental data are now available or it may use population-scale genetic, clinical, or public health data from pathogen surveillance efforts and biobanks.

This interdisciplinary PhD project lies at the intersection of molecular biology, bioinformatics, and computer science. The doctoral student will develop innovative computational methods for the analysis and interpretation of complex biological data, while pursuing doctoral studies in Molecular Biology at Umeå University.

We are looking for a PhD student in Molecular Biology with an interest in algorithms, data structures, and high-performance computing. The position at the Department of Molecular Biology at Umeå University is temporary for four years to start immediately or as agreed. The student will be enrolled in the Umeå university Technical Faculty PhD school for Molecular Biology, as well as the national DDLS PhD school for Data driven epidemiology and biology of infection. However, no prior knowledge of biology is required and the ideal candidate has a Computing Science background or similar.

Description of work

The PhD student will participate in activities provided by the Department of Molecular Biology, the Laboratory for Molecular Infection Medicine Sweden (MIMS), and the Umeå Centrum for Microbial Research (UCMR). Furthermore, the student will take part in Data-driven Life Science (DDLS) national activities and have access to the Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program (WASP). This enables interaction with researchers from different research fields and access to various scientific and technical expertise. 

Data-driven life science (DDLS) uses data, computational methods and artificial intelligence to study biological systems and processes at all levels, from molecular structures and cellular processes to human health and global ecosystems. The SciLifeLab and Wallenberg National Program for Data-Driven Life Science (DDLS) aims to recruit and train the next generation of data-driven life scientists and to create globally leading computational and data science capabilities in Sweden. The program is funded with a total of 3.3 billion SEK over 12 years from the Knut and Alice Wallenberg (KAW) Foundation.

In 2026 the DDLS Research School will be expanded with the recruitment of 25 academic and 7 industrial PhD students. During the course of the DDLS program more than 260 PhD students and 200 postdocs will be part of the Research School. The DDLS program has four strategic research areas: cell and molecular biology, evolution and biodiversity, precision medicine and diagnostics, epidemiology and biology of infection. For more information, please see https://www.scilifelab.se/data-driven/ddls-research-school/ 

The future of life science is data-driven. Will you be part of that change? Then join us in this unique program!

Background and description of tasks

Our group develops new single-cell multiomic methods to characterize microbial genomes, resulting in vast (terabyte-petabyte) amounts of data. Using this technology, we aim to characterize complex bacterial communities across different environments, to be stored for deeper analysis and visualization in a Microbial Cell Atlas. This position aims to develop key software components to enable this mission. The results of this project will be used to track new pathogens, combat antimicrobial resistance and biological threats, and find new enzymes of broad interest (e.g., CRISPR gene editing). It will also reduce environmental impact of bioinformatics and promote safe computing standards.

Our software is built primarily in Rust, with minor parts in R and Python to support bioinformaticians. Our web frontend is also developed in Rust (web assembly) – all to support fast computing and handling of complex single-cell data. The software is designed from the ground up for a new type of data (single-cell whole-genome sequencing/metagenomics), and how to best analyze the data is an open research problem. Analysis covers preprocessing, assembly of DNA fragments into complete genomes, imputation of missing data, filtering of bad data, prediction of the meaning of the DNA in individual cells, compression for archiving, indexing and visualization. Our hardware encompasses CPU and GPU-nodes, and software will be designed for both multithreading and horizontal scaling.

The PhD student will become part of an interdisciplinary team of researchers and engineers, covering chemistry, microbiology, computing science, mathematics and data science. As a major team effort, the PhD student is not expected to carry out all tasks, but rather identify and tackle suitable subproblems. Experience of a statically typed programming language is however a must. We encourage independent thinking, from problem definition to solution, and projects are flexible.

A person who is employed as a PhD student shall primarily devote his-/or herself to his/her own education. The project and research environment will give the dedicated student the opportunity to train as a first-class researcher.

Qualifications

Applicants must hold a University degree equivalent to a European University Master degree or completed course requirements of at least 240 credit points, of which at least 60 credit points should be at second-cycle level. 

To fulfil the general entry requirements, the applicant must have qualifications equivalent to either a completed degree at advanced level (second-cycle), or completed course requirements of at least 240 ECTS, including at least 60 ECTS at advanced level, or has otherwise acquired essentially equivalent knowledge within Sweden or abroad. The faculty board may, in the case of a specific applicant, consent to an exemption from the general entry requirements if there are special reasons to do so. (Higher Education Ordinance, Chapter 7, Section 39).

To meet the specific entry requirements for doctoral education in molecular biology, the applicant must have completed higher education studies comprising at least 90 credits in a relevant subject area. 

The requirements for prior knowledge as described above are also considered to be met by those who have otherwise acquired essentially equivalent knowledge. You must be proficient in both oral and written communication in English. 

Requirements

  • Background in Computing Science, Bioinformatics or otherwise combines interest in Biology with strong programming experience. 
  • Have experience of a statically typed language
  • Have knowledge of algorithm design and common data structures

Advantageous qualifications

  • Has experience of Rust
  • Has experience of bioinformatics (especially of de novo assembly, single-cell analysis, and microbial bioinformatics)
  • Has experience of web development and dynamic websites
  • Has basic knowledge of mathematics (e.g. linear algebra, probability, statistics, stochastic processes)
  • Has experience of  in program development

Additional desirable qualifications

  • Has experience of R and Python
  • Has experience of machine learning
  • Has any knowledge of biology

While we don’t expect applicants to have a background in biology, applicants are expected to learn a sufficient amount during the course of the PhD, as to be able to effectively communicate with others, and formulate solutions to bioinformatics problems in terms of algorithms. The PhD course package will be adapted to the needs of the student.

You should be highly motivated and able to work productively in a team as well as independently. Excellent communication skills for interacting effectively with senior colleagues and peers are required. Great emphasis will be placed on personal suitability.

As an employee with us, you contribute to fostering an inclusive culture and a positive work environment. This involves communicating effectively across differences, demonstrating a collaborative spirit and the ability to work well with others. You maintain openness and a welcoming attitude, showing respect, compassion, and empathy. You engage with and support colleagues from diverse backgrounds and perspectives, and promote a healthy work-life balance for both yourself and others.

Basis of assessment

The evaluation of the ability and potential to assimilate the education is mainly based on:

1. Knowledge and skills relevant to doctoral studies within the research area,

2. The ability to formulate and solve scientific questions.

3. Skills in written and oral communication in English.

4. Other experience relevant to doctoral studies, such as professional experience.

Good collaborative skills, drive and independent work ability are considered as positive merits.

A selection will be made among qualified applicants on the basis of their qualifications and their ability to benefit from studies at the doctoral level. After the selection of the suitable candidate, the process for the admission to doctoral studies will commence. An admission decision will be taken by the prefect.

About the employment

The position is intendent to result in a doctoral degree and is limited to four years full time. If part-time teaching (max. 20%) can be offered, the employment period can be extended. Wage placement takes place according to the established salary ladder for doctoral student employment. According to the Higher Education Ordinance (Chapter 12, Section 2), the decision on employment cannot be appealed.

How to apply

You apply through our recruitment system at the latest 2026-11-19. Your application must contain the following documents written in English or Swedish:

  • A CV with information on education, a list of previous and current employments, and a list of publications.
  • Copies of relevant degrees, including a list of courses and grades.
  • A cover letter describing research experience and interests, motivation for applying for the position, and a link to previously produced code on GitHub or equivalent. If previous code cannot be disclosed, provide a motivation.
  • Contact details of two to three references.

For questions regarding the position contact johan.henriksson@umu.se or laura.carroll@umu.se 

More about us

You can find more information at www.umu.se/en/department-of-molecular-biology/ www.ucmr.umu.se,and www.scilifelab.se/data-driven/ddls-research-school/.

Our labs are described at www.henlab.org/ and www.microbe.dev/.

 Welcome with your application!

The Department of Physics at Umeå University (https://www.umu.se/en/department-of-physics/) conducts strong research in condensed matter physics, nanotechnology, photonics, ultrafast spectroscopy, and theoretical and computational physics. We announce a PhD position within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network SPARK for the doctoral project ‘Spatiotemporal Information Processing’. 

Last day to apply is November 30, 2026.
The earliest starting date is February 2027, or by agreement.

Project description 

The project will develop ultrafast optical logic and memory concepts using spatiotemporal metamaterials. The doctoral candidate will design metamaterial structures coupled to quantum emitters for ultrafast information processing and investigate how structured ultrashort light pulses can control optical and magnetic properties on femtosecond timescales.

The research will focus on developing sub-10 fs protocols for all-optical logic operations, data processing, and spatiotemporal magnetic memories. The work combines nanophotonics, metamaterials, quantum emitters, ultrafast optics, and light–matter interaction, with the aim of creating new routes for information processing beyond conventional electronic approaches.

The doctoral candidate position is funded by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network SPARK. The network offers a structured international training environment with research-specific and transferable-skills courses, workshops, conferences, and network-wide events. The project includes a 3-month industrial secondment at NKT Photonics in Denmark, focusing on vectorial ultrashort pulses, and a 6-month research secondment at Imperial College London in the United Kingdom, focusing on nanofabrication and characterization.

The doctoral project will be carried out at Umeå University under the supervision of Associate Professor Nicolò Maccaferri. The candidate will also benefit from co-supervision and mentoring by Professor Riccardo Sapienza at Imperial College London and from an industrial mentor at NKT Photonics. The position provides the opportunity to work in a stimulating, multidisciplinary, and international research environment within a prestigious European training network.

To be admitted for studies at third-cycle level, applicants are required to have completed a second-cycle level degree or completed course requirements of at least 240 ECTS credits. The recruitment procedure will follow the Higher Education Ordinance (Högskoleförordningen). Fluency in English is mandatory. A documented background in photonics, nanophotonics, ultrafast optics, condensed matter physics, quantum optics, metamaterials, magnetism, or related experimental or theoretical methods is meritorious.

Willingness to work in an inter-cultural, international, and diverse group, and the ability to work independently or as part of a team, are fundamental.

The applicant must meet the MSCA eligibility and mobility requirements: the candidate must not hold a doctoral degree at the time of recruitment and must not have resided or carried out their main activity, such as work or studies, in Sweden for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before recruitment.

Terms of employment

The employment is expected to result in a doctoral degree, and the main assignment for the doctoral student is to take part in research education, including participation in the described research project and relevant courses. Teaching and other departmental work, up to a maximum of 20%, may be included. 

The salary follows the established salary level for doctoral students at Umeå University. The position is funded for 36 months through the MSCA Doctoral Network SPARK, with a salary corresponding to at least the MSCA level (approximately 33 100 SEK gross per month), with the possibility of additional MSCA allowances for mobility and accompanying family members. Funding for the remainder of the employment period is provided from other sources. Employment conditions and additional benefits for employees according to applicable regulations.

The employment is limited to four years at full-time or up to five years if teaching and other departmental work is performed. The employment starts in February 2027 or according to agreement.

Umeå University is offering a PhD position in Computing Science with a focus on machine learning for graph transformations. The project investigates a hybrid approach that combines deep learning with grammatical inference to develop models that are interpretable, efficient, and mathematically verifiable while leveraging the flexibility of neural methods. If successful, the work has the potential to advance applications such as automated theorem proving, knowledge-graph inference, and causal analysis.

The Department of Computing Science has experienced rapid growth in recent years, with a strong emphasis on fostering an inclusive, collaborative, and bottom-up-driven research environment. Our workplace brings together a diverse community of individuals from a wide range of nationalities.

As a PhD student with us, you benefit from comprehensive career development support, opportunities for networking, and access to robust administrative and technical services—all within a setting that offers attractive employment conditions.

To learn more about the department, please visit: https://www.umu.se/en/department-of-computing-science/

Project description

Graphs are a fundamental way of representing structured information from sentences and computer programs to social networks and they are becoming increasingly important as generative AI systems move beyond text. To keep such systems safe and reliable, we need mechanisms that can ensure their outputs follow the right rules, much like guardrails that prevent language models from producing harmful content or incorrect code. This project introduces a new idea: instead of relying on opaque, heavy machine-learning models, it learns transparent, rule-based rewriting systems that can transform graphs, check the correctness of AI-generated structures, and even guide neural networks during inference. By combining techniques from grammatical inference, reinforcement learning, and efficient search algorithms, the method can automatically discover both the rules and probabilities needed to model complex graph behaviors, offering a more interpretable and verifiable alternative for future AI systems.

The student will collaborate closely with the PI and her research group at Umeå University to investigate the proposed learning approach. The PhD student is expected to produce research outputs relevant to the fields of theoretical computer science and symbolic machine learning.

Admission requirements

The general admission requirements for doctoral studies are a second- cycle level degree, or completed course requirements of at least 240 ECTS credits, of which at least 60 ECTS credits are at second-cycle level, or have an equivalent education from abroad, or equivalent qualifications.

To be admitted to doctoral studies in the field of computer science, the applicant must have completed courses totaling at least 90 higher education credits in computer science or in subjects directly relevant to the specific specialization.

We are looking for candidates who have:

Solid analytical and mathematical abilities Experience with machine learning Experience with formal language theory or automata theory Strong communication skills and proficiency in English The ability to work independently as well as collaboratively

Meritorious Qualifications

It is considered an advantage if you have:

Experience with academic writing Strong programming skills, particularly in Python Familiarity with knowledge graphs Experience with graph neural network

Personal Qualities

We value candidates who are:

Intellectually curious Self-motivated and well-organized Eager to engage with the scientific community

About the position

The position provides you with the opportunity to pursue PhD studies in Computing Science for four years, with the goal of achieving the degree of Doctor in Computing Science. While the position is mainly devoted to PhD studies (at least 80% of the time), it may include up to 20% department service (usually teaching). If so, the total time for the position is extended accordingly, resulting in a maximum of five years.

The procedure for recruitment for the position is in accordance with the Higher Education Ordinance (chapter 12, 2§) and the decision regarding the position cannot be appealed.

The expected starting date is January 12, 2027 or as otherwise agreed.

Application

A cover letter including a description of your research interests, your reasons to apply for the position, and your contact information A curriculum vitae Reprints / copies of completed BSc and/or MSc theses and other relevant publications, if any Copies of degree certificates, including documentation of completed academic courses and obtained grades Documentation and description of other relevant experiences or competences.

Umeå University is one of Sweden’s largest higher education institutions with over 41,500 students and about 4,600 employees. The University offers a diversity of high-quality education and world-leading research in several fields. Notably, the groundbreaking discovery of the CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing tool, which was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, was made here. At Umeå University, everything is close. For Umeå University, conducting research about – and in the middle of – a society in transition is key. We also take pride in delivering education to enable regions to expand quickly and sustainably. In fact, the future is made here.

Are you interested in learning more? Read about Umeå university as a workplace

The Department of Physics at Umeå University (https://www.umu.se/en/department-of-physics/) conducts strong research in condensed matter physics, nanotechnology, photonics, ultrafast spectroscopy, and theoretical and computational physics. We announce a PhD position within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network SPARK for the doctoral project ‘Spatiotemporal Hybrid Light–Matter States’. 

Last day to apply is November 30, 2026. 
The earliest starting date is February 2027, or by agreement.

Project description

The project will create spatiotemporal polaritons through ultrafast light–matter interactions in engineered metamaterial systems. The doctoral candidate will explore wide-bandgap semiconductors and high-quality excitonic or molecular emitters coupled to time-modulated gratings, with the goal of realizing hybrid light–matter states whose properties can be controlled on femtosecond timescales.

The research will combine ultrafast pump–push–probe experiments with sub-10 fs resolution, finite-element simulations, and quantum models extending the Tavis–Cummings Hamiltonian. The aim is to demonstrate coherent control of spatiotemporal polaritons and to design spatiotemporal metamaterial platforms supporting new forms of hybrid light–matter dynamics. The work combines nanophotonics, metamaterials, ultrafast optics, condensed matter physics, and quantum optics.

The doctoral candidate position is funded by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network SPARK. The network offers a structured international training environment with research-specific and transferable-skills courses, workshops, conferences, and network-wide events. The project includes a 6-month research secondment at Universidad Autónoma de Madrid in Spain, where theoretical skills will be developed, and a 3-month industrial secondment at Ultrafast Innovations GmbH in Germany.

The doctoral project will be carried out at Umeå University under the supervision of Associate Professor Nicolò Maccaferri. The candidate will also benefit from co-supervision and mentoring by Associate Professor Paloma Arroyo Huidobro at Universidad Autónoma de Madrid and from an industrial mentor at Ultrafast Innovations GmbH. The position provides the opportunity to work in a stimulating, multidisciplinary, and international research environment within a prestigious European training network.

Competence requirements

To fulfil the general entry requirements, the applicant must have qualifications equivalent to a completed degree at advanced level (second-cycle), or completed course requirements of at least 240 ECTS credits including at least 60 ECTS credits at advanced level. To fulfil the specific entry requirements to be admitted to doctoral studies in experimental physics, the applicant is required to have completed courses within the field of physics comprising at least 120 credits. 

Applicants should have a Master’s degree, or equivalent, in physics, applied physics, optics/photonics, materials science, nanoscience, electrical engineering, or a closely related field. 

English fluency, both written and spoken, is mandatory. A documented background in photonics, nanophotonics, ultrafast optics, condensed matter physics, quantum optics, exciton–polaritons, light–matter interaction, numerical simulations, or quantum modelling is meritorious.

Willingness to work in an inter-cultural, international, and diverse group, and the ability to work independently or as part of a team, are fundamental.

The applicant must meet the MSCA eligibility and mobility requirements: the candidate must not hold a doctoral degree at the time of recruitment and must not have resided or carried out their main activity, such as work or studies, in Sweden for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before recruitment.

Terms of employment

The employment is expected to result in a doctoral degree, and the main assignment for the doctoral student is to take part in research education, including participation in the described research project and relevant courses. Teaching and other departmental work, up to a maximum of 20%, may be included. 

The salary follows the established salary level for doctoral students at Umeå University. The position is funded for 36 months through the MSCA Doctoral Network SPARK, with a salary corresponding to at least the MSCA level (approximately 33 100 SEK gross per month), with the possibility of additional MSCA allowances for mobility and accompanying family members. Funding for the remainder of the employment period is provided from other sources. Employment conditions and additional benefits for employees according to applicable regulations. 

The employment is limited to four years at full-time or up to five years if teaching and other departmental work is performed. The employment starts in February 2027 or according to agreement.

The application 

The application should contain:

  1. A cover letter with a summary of research interests and motivation (max. 1 page)
  2. Curriculum Vitae.
  3. Certified copies of relevant degree certificate(s) translated to English or Swedish.
  4. Transcripts with grades, with English or Swedish translation. Note that for international applicants the grading system should be explained in brief.
  5. Copies of student theses and publications (if any).
  6. Names and contact information of at least one reference person.

You apply via our e-recruitment system Varbi.
The deadline for applications is November 30, 2026. 

Log in and submit your application via the button at the bottom of the page. All application documents must be uploaded in PDF format and should be written in English (preferred) or Swedish.

More information

For further information, contact the Principal Investigator of the project, Associate Professor Nicolò Maccaferri, nicolo.maccaferri@umu.se.

We look forward to receiving your application!

jobs.title: Doctoral researcher in Adaptive Grid-Interactive Edge Datacenter Fleets (MSCA Doctoral Network)
jobs.description_html:
We are recruiting one doctoral researcher (3 years) to the AEGIS network


AEGIS — Adaptive Grid-Interactive Edge Datacenter Fleets — is a European research and training network. It is funded by the EU through a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network, runs from 2026 to 2030, and trains 15 Doctoral Candidates (PhD students). The DN targets developing software-defined technologies that turn edge data centers from passive electrical loads into active, carbon-efficient and grid-interactive resources. The project has three layers:

  • A programmable infrastructure layer gives safe, runtime-verified control of a site’s power electronics, cooling, and AI hardware.
  • An intelligence layer reads real-time grid signals and turns a request such as “reduce power by 20%” into the detailed actions that hardware and facilities must take, without breaking service.
  • A fleet orchestration layer coordinates many sites, even when they have different owners, using trusted and privacy-preserving methods, so the whole fleet can act as one Virtual Power Plant.

Read more about the project and other participants here: https://aegis-dn.eu/

 

Your role:

You will be working on “End-to-End Energy Modeling for Distributed AI Services”. To make carbon-aware decisions, both orchestrators and developers need to see the real energy cost of an AI workload. In this project you build analytical models and systems that make energy and carbon metrics visible. You will create compositional energy models that span the radio network, the transport network, and the datacenter hardware, and expose them through a fast query interface so any tool can ask, “what does this AI service cost in energy?”


You will be responsible for:

  • Developing compositional energy models for disaggregated radio (RAN) components, transport networks, and datacenter hardware.
  • Building a low-latency query API that returns the end-to-end energy cost of an AI service.

What you will deliver:

  • Validated models with less than 10% prediction error on the Aalto and Ericsson testbeds.
  • A query API that returns end-to-end energy-cost estimates in under 100 milliseconds.
  • A doctoral dissertation that you will defend.

Secondments:

You will spend two research visits with partners in the network:

  • Ericsson (Finland) — 3 months from around May 2028 (industry), with Tomas Mecklin: test the energy models on Ericsson’s infrastructure testbeds.
  • TU Wien (Vienna, Austria) — 3 months from around May 2029 (academic), with Ivona Brandić: combine the digital-twin models with the end-to-end energy models.

The position requires:

  • Master's degree in computer science, communications engineering, telecommunications, or a related field (with a CGPA of at least 4/5)
  • Experience (e.g. coursework, projects, etc.) in AI and machine learning, including understanding of various DNN architectures, training models, and applying them for different tasks
  • Understanding of computer and telecom networks (for example RAN)
  • Experience with empirical measurements (Prior work on energy or power measurement is strongly preferred)
  • Data analysis and analytical modeling — identifying the features that drive system behaviour and building compositional or analytical models from measured data (an interest or aptitude here is enough; we don’t expect prior demonstrated experience)
  • Good programming skills – you are required to provide a sample of your code during the recruitment process
  • Fluency in written and spoken English. See https://www.aalto.fi/en/study-options/aalto-doctoral-programme-in-electrical-engineering#8-required-language-proficiency for information on how you can demonstrate proficiency in English. This is required when officially applying for doctoral studies at the School of Electrical Engineering in Aalto University (within 6 months after starting in the job). Please note that you do not need official proof when applying for this job.

If you are chosen for this position, you will apply for the study right in doctoral studies at Aalto University School of Electrical Engineering. Thus, please see the student information and admission criteria at https://www.aalto.fi/en/study-options/aalto-doctoral-programme-in-electrical-engineering.


MSCA eligibility

You must meet the following requirements:

  • No doctoral degree. At the date of recruitment, you must not yet hold a PhD.
  • Mobility rule. You must not have lived or done your main activity (work or studies) in Finland for more than 12 months in the 36 months just before you are recruited, unless as part of a compulsory national service or a procedure for obtaining EU temporary protection or refugee status under the Geneva Convention. Short stays such as holidays do not count.
  • All nationalities welcome. The positions are open to applicants of any nationality.

What we offer:

You will become a part of the Cloud and Network Computing group, headed by assistant professor Gopika Premsankar. You will be advised by Riku Jäntti, full professor in Communications Engineering. Both groups are based in the Department of Information and Communications Engineering in the School of Electrical Engineering.


The position starts in March 2027 or as mutually agreed. The start date cannot be later than June 2027. The employment contract will be made for three years.


Application documents

To apply, please share the following application materials (as PDFs) with us through our recruitment site ("Apply now!” at the bottom of the page):

  • A CV
  • A short letter of motivation, at most 1 page, which describes your interest and motivation (please try to include details that are not part of your CV and emphasize how you address the position-specific requirements listed above)
  • Sample code, preferably on a code repository (Provide a URL and describe in one paragraph your role in developing the software)
  • Names and email addresses of two reference providers. They will be contacted directly at a later stage in the application process.
  • Transcript of grades for your Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees

Please note that our recruitment system allows maximum of 5 attachments, so please combine e.g. the copies of transcripts in one PDF, if necessary.


Application process

The application deadline is December 15, 2026 23.59pm (EET). We will go through the applications in batches, and we may invite suitable candidates to interview already during the application period. The call will be closed early, if the position is filled before the application deadline.

jobs.title: Doctoral Researcher, sustainability of Power-to-X (PtX) value chains
jobs.description_html:
Aalto University is where science and art meet technology and business. We shape a sustainable future by making research breakthroughs in and across our disciplines, sparking the game changers of tomorrow and creating novel solutions to major global challenges. Our community is made up of 16 000 students and 5 200 employees, including 446 professors. Our campus is in Espoo, Greater Helsinki, Finland.  Diversity is part of who we are, and we actively work to ensure our community’s diversity and inclusiveness. This is why we warmly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to join our community.


The Sustainable Systems research group in the Department of Chemical and Metallurgical Engineering at Aalto University is seeking a highly motivated


DOCTORAL RESEARCHER


to focus on the sustainability of Power-to-X (PtX) value chains.

Are you passionate about advancing renewable energy technologies? Do you want to develop cutting-edge computational frameworks that shape the future of sustainable energy? Join us in solving key challenges in decarbonizing hard-to-abate sectors.


Project Overview

This PhD project aims to develop decision-making models and optimization strategies for the cross-sector integration and operation of PtX technologies. You will work on ensuring these pathways operate within planetary boundaries while meeting stringent criteria for cost-effectiveness, safety, and operational resilience.


Key Research Questions:

  • How can the intermittent nature of renewable electricity production be economically decoupled from further chemical processing of eFuels and eChemicals?
  • How can the technical, economic, and environmental feasibility of the PtX value chain be maximized under operational and market uncertainty?
  • How can an efficient and intelligent computational framework be developed to optimally design and operate low-carbon energy transition pathways for the industrial sectors in Finland and beyond?

Your Role and Responsibilities

  • Push the flexibility limits of energy transition pathways by modeling operational dynamics, intermediate storage, and variable feedstocks.
  • Formulate Techno-Economic and Life Cycle-driven Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) models to optimize full PtX value chains.
  • Engage with internal group members, academic collaborators, and external industry stakeholders.
  • Present research outcomes at international academic conferences and publish in high-impact, peer-reviewed journals.

To support your research, you will have access to our group’s comprehensive model library covering PtX technologies, unit operations, training materials, and sustainability assessment frameworks.


Your network and team

You will join the Sustainable Systems group, led by Prof. Rofice Dickson. Our group focuses on developing mathematical models, algorithms, and computer-aided software tools to explore circular and sustainable solutions for energy systems.


You will be directly supervised by Prof. Rofice Dickson and work alongside a vibrant, multidisciplinary team of PhD students, postdoctoral researchers, and industrial partners.


The unique competitive edge of the Department of Chemical and Metallurgical Engineering in the School of Chemical Engineering is based on sustainable utilization of raw materials, designing more efficient processes, and developing new materials and products. Our department’s areas of expertise enable a sustainable future with high-performance products and processes in the circular economy and bioeconomy. The department is in a key position in research of chemical engineering, materials technology, metals processing, efficient energy technologies and digitalization of these. Our core competences include unit operations and processes in chemical engineering, hydro- and pyro-metallurgy, catalyst and polymeric materials, novel catalytic process, process control and process systems engineering.


Your Experience and Ambitions

We are seeking highly motivated candidates with a strong research background in Process Systems Engineering of energy systems.


Required:

  • Master’s Degree: In Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Energy Systems Engineering, or a closely related field.
  • Optimization background: Solid experience applying mathematical programming (e.g., MILP, MINLP) to energy or process systems.
  • Programming proficiency: Demonstrated skills in optimization or modeling environments (e.g., GAMS, Python, Julia, or MATLAB).

Desirable (Considered an Advantage):

  • Assessment Methodologies: Knowledge of TEA and LCA methodologies.
  • Software tools: Familiarity with process simulation tools (Aspen Plus/Hysys, PRO/II) and LCA software (SimaPro, openLCA).
  • Research focus: Strong interest in renewable energy pathways, cross-sectoral integration, and decision-making under uncertainty.

What we offer

The starting date is January 1, 2027, or as mutually agreed. We offer a fixed term contract initially for 2 years. During the first 6 months you must apply and receive a right to study in the Doctoral Programme in Chemical Engineering. After a successful evaluation by the end of the first 2 year contract, the contract can be extended. Extension contract is typically based on the progress evaluation, revised project plan and available funding.


The starting salary for a Doctoral Researcher is about 3140 €/month (gross). The contract includes Aalto University occupational healthcare benefits.


Please check the student information and admission criteria at https://www.aalto.fi/en/study-options/aalto-doctoral-programme-in-chemical-engineering. Please pay attention to the mandatory skill level in English.
