jobs.title: Doctoral Researcher – Heterogeneous Integration for Power Electronics
jobs.description_html:
Electronics Integration and Reliability (EILB) (Electronics Integration and Reliability | Aalto University) is a research group at Aalto University School of Electrical Engineering. We advance next‑generation electronics through innovative materials, device design, and bonding technologies. By leveraging high‑quality AlN and high‑Al‑content AlGaN, distributed polarization doping, and advanced packaging and interconnection concepts, we develop solutions for cutting‑edge power electronics based on wide‑bandgap (WBG) and ultra‑wide‑bandgap (UWBG) semiconductors, as well as for RF applications and smart sensors. Our mission is to enable miniaturized, sustainable, and energy-efficient systems with superior power handling, higher breakdown voltages, and enhanced high temperature performance.


We are looking for a doctoral researcher to advance miniaturised, high‑density heterogeneous integration of WBG and UWBG power electronics through novel high‑temperature interconnects—including solid–liquid interdiffusion (SLID), hybrid and diffusion bonding, and sintering technologies—in collaboration with our international research partners. The research will investigate how interconnect interfacial compatibility, metallurgy and microstructures, and local interface states and defects influence electrical and thermal performance, and long‑term reliability of power electronic modules. These innovative solutions necessitate profound requirement specifications and co-design of thermal, thermomechanical, and microstructural aspects, based on a deep understanding of the electrical requirements of WBG/UWBG semiconductors. The goal is to design, manufacture, and characterise reliable, highly integrated, ultra‑high‑power‑density power modules [~50 kW/L (or kg)] or “power chiplets”. These power modules incorporate innovative control and sensing functions by utilising novel interconnection technologies, which are developed by utilizing advanced materials characterisation methods, electrical and thermal measurements, and multiphysics modelling.


Requirements

  • M.Sc. or equivalent degree in a suitable area (e.g. electrical engineering, physics or materials science)
  • good knowledge and understanding of WBG and UWBG power semiconductor technologies
  • experience in multiphysics simulation tools such as COMSOL, ANSYS and circuit design tools like SPICE or PLEX
  • experience of working in a cleanroom  
  • experience or genuine interest in advanced microfabrication, novel interconnection and material characterization methods
  • experience or genuine interest in electronics reliability assessment and failure analysis tools
  • strong analytical and writing skills

If you are chosen for this position, you will then apply for the study right in doctoral studies at Aalto University School of Electrical Engineering. Thus, please see the student information and admission criteria at https://www.aalto.fi/en/study-options/aalto-doctoral-programme-in-electrical-engineering.

  • The position is fixed term and follows the school’s standard 2+2 model for doctoral researchers. It will be made initially for two years, with a six-month probationary period, and extended by two further years after a successful mid-term review, giving a total duration of four years
  • opportunity to conduct independent research in a cutting-edge OtaNano infrastructure of Micronova (https://www.aalto.fi/en/otanano/micronova) and Nanomicroscopy Center (https://www.aalto.fi/en/otanano/nanomicroscopy-center)
  • possibility of building international industrial and academic networks within large national and pan-European public-private-partnership projects, in which the EILB team is participating
  • multidisciplinary course curriculum of Aalto University
  • starting salary of 3143 €/month
  • occupational health and social security benefits

The position is available immediately

jobs.title: Doctoral Researcher (Human-Centered Security and Digital Deception)
jobs.description_html:
Aalto University is a community of bold thinkers where science and art meet technology and business. We are committed to identifying and solving grand societal challenges and building an innovative future. Aalto has six schools with 16 000 students and a staff of 5200, of which more than 440 are professors. Our main campus is located in Espoo, Finland. Diversity is part of who we are, and we actively work to ensure our community’s diversity and inclusiveness. This is why we warmly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to join our community.


The Department of Computer Science is an internationally-oriented community and home to world-class research in modern computer science, combining research on foundations and innovative applications. With over 40 professors and more than 550 employees from 50+ countries, it is the largest department at Aalto University and the leading computer science research unit in northern Europe. Computer science research at Aalto University ranks high in several international surveys (7th in Europe and 1st in the Nordics (NTU 2023); and 88th worldwide in Times Higher Education subject ranking 2025).


We are now looking for a

Doctoral researcher

 

How can technology users judge whether a digital request is genuine when convincing messages, voices and images can be fabricated?


The research group Humans, Security and Privacy at the Computer Science Department at Aalto University is looking to hire one Doctoral Researcher in Human-Centered Security and Digital Deception (PhD student). You will be supervised by Assistant Professor Verena Distler.  


Our interdisciplinary research brings together human–computer interaction, psychology, and human-centered security to understand how people experience security and privacy online, and how they respond to digital deception, including social engineering. We combine empirical research with the design and evaluation of user-centered technologies to support critical judgment, informed decision-making, and user autonomy. Please familiarize yourself with the group’s work before applying.


Your network and team

You will work closely with your supervisor and the research group. The department also provides an international research environment and opportunities to connect with other doctoral researchers. While strong independent working skills are essential, the ability to collaborate effectively with fellow researchers is equally important.

 

Your role and goals

The focus will be social engineering in everyday digital interactions. You will investigate how people assess whether requests are genuine, and how interface interventions may support them in their judgments. The precise doctoral research questions will be developed together with your supervisor, taking your interests into account.


Your tasks will include:

  • Reviewing and synthesizing relevant scientific literature.
  • Developing realistic research scenarios and measurement protocols with your supervisor.
  • Designing and conducting studies with human participants, with appropriate ethical safeguards.
  • Collecting and analyzing quantitative and qualitative data, including statistical analysis where appropriate.
  • Writing research articles and presenting findings at leading scientific venues.
  • Collaborating with researchers within the group and its wider network.

In addition to research work, persons hired are expected to participate in teaching following the standard practices at the department.


Your experience and ambitions

  • A relevant master’s degree completed by the employment start date, for example in human–computer interaction, computer science, psychology, social sciences, or a related discipline.
  • A strong interest in the psychological and social aspects of human-centered security and privacy.
  • Strong English communication skills, including the ability to write scientific texts and discuss research.
  • Experience in at least one of the following: experimental design and analysis, questionnaire development, qualitative interviewing and analysis, or interactive prototyping.
    • Experience in all these areas is not required; willingness to develop complementary methodological skills is essential.

jobs.title: Doctoral Researcher in condensed matter physics and two-dimensional (2D) Quantum Devices
jobs.description_html:
Aalto University is where science and art meet technology and business. We shape a sustainable future by making research breakthroughs in and across our disciplines, sparking the game changers of tomorrow and creating novel solutions to major global challenges. Our community is made up of 120 nationalities, 16 000 students, 446 professors and close to 5000 other faculty and staff working on our dynamic campus in Espoo, Greater Helsinki, Finland. Diversity is part of who we are, and we actively work to ensure our community’s diversity and inclusiveness. This is why we warmly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to join our community.

 

At the Department of Applied Physics, our pioneering research in physical sciences creates important industrial applications that hold great technological potential. Our research focuses on Materials physics; Quantum technology; Soft & living matter; and Advanced energy solutions. Topics extend from fundamental research to important applications. We educate future generations of research and development professionals; data specialists; technology experts; inventors; and scientists for industry and society.

 

The Atomic Scale Physics group at the Department of Applied Physics is looking for a Doctoral Researcher (PhD student) in 2D quantum devices and condensed matter physics. The research focuses on correlated electron systems, topological systems and superconductivity.

 

Gate-tunable 2D devices are at the cutting edge of condensed matter physics today. This is where many of the most exciting discoveries are being made, and the field is moving fast. You will work at the frontier of this research, combining nanofabricated devices made from 2D layered materials with low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy (STM). Our group has long experience with both the techniques and the materials.

 

Your role and goals

Your goal is to study emergent electronic phenomena in gate-tunable van der Waals materials using STM. A gate voltage lets you add or remove electrons in a device, so you can tune one sample through many different quantum phases, including exotic ones that are hard to reach in any other way. With STM, you can see these phases at the atomic scale and learn how they form and behave.


Your tasks will include:

  • Fabrication of quantum devices in cleanroom facilities, including lithography, deposition, exfoliation and transfer of 2D materials
  • Running low-temperature STM experiments on these devices
  • Collaboration with leading theoretical physicists
  • Analysis of measured data and writing scientific articles

Your experience and ambitions

Required:

  • A Master's degree in condensed matter physics or a closely related field (completion latest end of 2027)
  • A genuine interest in experimental condensed matter physics
  • Good command of English (Finnish is not required)

A plus:

  • Experience with nanofabrication and cleanroom processing of 2D materials
  • Hands-on experience with low-temperature and ultra-high vacuum systems
  • Experience with scanning tunneling microscopy
  • Knowledge of 2D quantum materials and related physics

The selected candidate needs to apply for the study right in doctoral studies at Aalto University School of Science. Please check the student information and admission criteria at Aalto Doctoral Programme in Science | Aalto University.


What we offer

We offer a fully funded PhD project for one talented Doctoral Researcher under the guidance of Dr. Viliam Vaňo in the Atomic Scale Physics group led by Prof. Peter Liljeroth. The group consists currently of 3 Academy Research Fellows, 1 Postdoctoral Researcher and 6 Doctoral Researchers. The group focuses studying physical phenomena in atomically precise materials characterized using scanning tunneling microscopy in a wide array of systems such as heterostructures of two-dimensional van der Waals materials, atomically well-defined graphene nanoribbons, and artificial lattices on surfaces.


The position of the Doctoral Researcher is initially filled for 2 years. The contract is continued for another 2 years after a successful midterm review. The annual workload of research and teaching staff at Aalto University is 1612 hours. Aalto University follows the salary system of Finnish universities. The starting salary is approximately 3142 €/month (gross), and it increases as the Doctoral Researcher progresses in the research and studies. The contract includes Aalto University occupational healthcare.


Our vast array of professional development opportunities means you will grow and learn, having the chance to participate actively in staff trainings and development projects based on your interests and needs. There is great freedom in your role, and we have a flexible modern working culture. We value work-life balance and well-being in all aspects of life.

We work in a hybrid way, and the primary workplace is Otaniemi, Espoo. Life at the transformed Otaniemi campus is vibrant and filled with amazing architecture, calming nature, and a variety of cafes, restaurants, services and good connections along the recently opened metro line.

jobs.title: Doctoral Researcher in Physics-Enhanced Machine Learning for Floating Offshore Wind Digital Twins
jobs.description_html:
At Aalto University, curiosity moves across disciplines, roles and communities. We bring people together to ask new questions, challenge familiar thinking and turn ideas into impact.

Our work is rooted in responsibility, courage and collaboration, and in a shared commitment to shaping a more sustainable future.


The School of Engineering is inviting applications for a Doctoral Researcher in Physics-Enhanced Machine Learning for Floating Offshore Wind Digital Twins


Floating offshore wind turbines will be central to the clean-energy transition, but their behaviour at sea is difficult to predict and monitor. They move in six degrees of freedom under irregular waves and turbulent wind. The mooring lines that keep them in position are located deep underwater, where permanent sensing is costly and difficult to maintain. Operators therefore need digital twins that combine hydrodynamic knowledge with sensor data to estimate quantities that cannot be measured directly.


In this full-time, salaried Doctoral Researcher position, you will help develop the next generation of these digital twins: models that capture the wave-driven dynamics of floating turbines, update as new data arrive, detect early signs of degradation, and quantify the uncertainty of their estimates.


The position is funded by the Research Council of Finland. It is based at Aalto University's Otaniemi campus in Espoo, Finland, and starts on 28 January 2027 or as agreed.


Research environment and duties

At the Department of Energy and Mechanical Engineering, our Marine and Arctic Technology research group studies how ships and offshore structures move and are loaded in waves, wind and ice. We combine machine learning and data-driven methods with hydrodynamic theory, numerical simulation and model-scale experiments. In this role, you will help us build digital twins that track the wave-induced motions, mooring loads and structural condition of floating offshore wind turbines in real time using only a small number of sensors.


Your work will contribute to safer and more cost-effective floating wind farms, where wave loads and mooring tensions can be monitored continuously, degradation can be detected early, and maintenance can be planned before failures occur.


Your work will include:

  • Developing physics-enhanced machine-learning models that learn the coupled hydrodynamic and structural dynamics of floating wind turbines from measured data and update in real time. These methods will build on, among other approaches, Koopman operator theory and dynamic mode decomposition (DMD).
  • Embedding hydrodynamic knowledge into these models so that they remain physically consistent across sea states, including wave excitation, radiation-memory effects, slow-drift motions and mooring-line dynamics.
  • Estimating wave-induced motions and mooring loads that cannot be measured directly.
  • Detecting early mooring-system or structural degradation and distinguishing it from normal changes in waves, wind and turbine operating conditions.
  • Quantifying the uncertainty of these estimates using Bayesian filtering and probabilistic machine learning.
  • Generating and analysing data from: hydrodynamic simulations, including potential-flow methods and, where needed, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and coupled simulation tools such as OpenFAST
  • Publishing results in leading international journals and presenting them at conferences.

You will work closely with researchers in the Marine and Arctic Technology group and with our international academic collaborators.


This is an exciting time to join us. Floating offshore wind is scaling up rapidly, and industry guidance increasingly favours indirect monitoring of hard-to-access components, such as mooring lines, using sensors located elsewhere on the structure.


Our group has recently shown that digital twins learned directly from measurements can estimate unmeasured responses and loads from only a few sensors, including verification using wave-basin test data. In this role, you will take these methods a step further by embedding hydrodynamics into the learning process and moving from accurate estimation toward reliable, self-updating condition monitoring.


What you bring

To thrive in this role, you will need:

  • A Master's degree completed by the start of the position. Suitable backgrounds include naval architecture, marine or ocean engineering, offshore engineering, mechanical, civil or aerospace engineering, applied mathematics, physics, computer science, or a related field.
  • A strong foundation in linear algebra and in at least one of the following areas: hydrodynamics or fluid mechanics, structural dynamics, dynamical systems, or signal processing.
  • Good programming skills in Python or a similar language, together with a genuine interest in machine learning.
  • Curiosity, independence, and the ability to communicate clearly and work well in a team.


We also value:

  • Knowledge of marine or offshore hydrodynamics, such as wave-structure interaction, potential-flow or boundary-element methods, or computational fluid dynamics (e.g. OpenFOAM or REEF3D).
  • Experience with OpenFAST, MoorDyn or WAMIT, or similar software.
  • Experience with dynamic mode decomposition, Koopman operator methods, system identification or operational modal analysis.
  • Experience with Kalman filtering, Bayesian inference, Gaussian processes or uncertainty quantification.
  • Experience with deep learning for time series, such as Transformers or graph neural networks, using PyTorch or JAX.
  • Scientific publications or a strong Master's thesis in a related area.

Language requirements:

  • English: Excellent English-language skills are required.
  • Finnish: Finnish-language skills are not required.

We know that meaningful work is built by people with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. If you recognise yourself in the purpose of this role, we encourage you to apply and tell us what you would bring to our community.


What we offer

At Aalto, you can expect:

  • The opportunity to work in a growing research team at the intersection of marine hydrodynamics, machine learning and offshore structural dynamics.
  • Work with purpose in a community where research, education, creativity and services support meaningful change.
  • A multidisciplinary environment where collaboration, curiosity and new thinking are part of everyday work.
  • Extensive occupational health-care services.
  • Staff-priced sports-centre services on campus and at other UniSport locations.
  • A workplace at Aalto University's Otaniemi campus, with excellent public transport connections and a wide range of services.

If you are selected for this position, you will apply for the right to pursue doctoral studies at Aalto University School of Engineering. Doctoral studies at Aalto University typically take approximately four years. The position will initially be filled with a two-year fixed-term contract, with the possibility of extension based on progress in research and studies and on performance. We support your professional growth with varied training and development opportunities shaped around your interests and aspirations.


The expected starting salary for a Doctoral Researcher is approximately EUR 3,000 per month (gross), and it increases as the Doctoral Researcher progresses in research and studies. Work-life balance and well-being in all aspects of life are important to us at Aalto.


Curious to make a difference?

Please submit your application through our recruitment system by 28 December 2026 at 23:59 Finnish time (UTC +2). If you are already working at Aalto University, please apply through our internal Workday system. If you are a student or visitor at Aalto University, please apply using your personal email address.


We reserve the right to fill the position before the application period closes should a suitable candidate be found, to appoint a candidate outside of this recruitment process, or to leave the position unfilled.


All applications must include the following materials:

  • Cover letter / motivation letter with your contact information and preferred starting date (maximum 1 page).
  • CV including details of all academic outputs.
  • Contact details of two referees.
  • Description of your Master's thesis project (maximum 1 page).
  • Course transcripts for your Bachelor's and Master's degrees, including grades and a clear explanation of the grading scale.
  • Research statement (maximum 2 pages) answering the question below.
  • Research statement question: How could early degradation of a mooring line, such as a gradual loss of stiffness, be detected in a floating offshore wind turbine using only a few sensors on the tower and platform while wind and wave conditions keep changing?

In your statement, outline:

  • the methods you would use
  • the data you would need
  • how you would validate your approach
  • what could cause the approach to fail.

We do not expect a complete solution; we want to see how you think. You are welcome to draw on any relevant background, including hydrodynamics, structural dynamics, signal processing or machine learning.


All materials should be submitted in English as a single PDF file, compiled in the order specified above. Applications submitted by email will not be accepted. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interviews and may be asked to complete a short technical task. Aalto University reserves the right to leave the position open, extend the application period, and consider candidates who have not applied during the application period.


For more information about the role, please contact:

  • Dr. Mohammad Mahdi Abaei, Academy Research Fellow, mohammad.abaei(at)aalto.fi
  • For questions related to the application process, please contact HR Advisor Anna-Maija Harju, anna-maija.harju(at)Aalto.fi or hr-eng(at)aalto.fi.

About Aalto University

Aalto University builds on the legacy of three leading Finnish universities: Helsinki University of Technology, Helsinki School of Economics and the University of Art and Design Helsinki. Since 2010, we have brought science, art, technology and business together in new ways.


Today, the Aalto community consists of more than 16,000 students and 5,200 employees, including 446 professors. Half of our teaching and research staff have an international background. Our campus in Espoo is a vibrant cluster of research and innovation with striking architecture, peaceful nature, open spaces for collaboration and a wide range of services, all with excellent public transport connections.


Diversity is part of who we are. We work actively to build a community where people can belong, contribute and grow.

jobs.title: PhD Student in Robotics and Artificial Intelligence
jobs.description_html:
Offer Description

Are you ready to take the next step in your academic journey? As a doctoral student with us, you will work closely with leading researchers in a strong, international research environment, with access to advanced laboratory equipment and solid funding opportunities. You will be offered secure employment, high-quality supervision, and room to grow, both as a researcher and as a person.

Robotics and Artificial Intelligence, RAI, at the Deaprtment of Computer Science, Electrical and Space Engineeering at Luleå University of Technology is now looking for a PhD student to contribute to our growing activities. The RAI team conducts basic and fundamental research into all aspects of robotics, with a specific focus on aerial, space and bio-inspired robotics.

Subject description
Robotics and artificial intelligence aim to develop novel robotic systems that are characterised by advanced autonomy for improving the ability of robots to interact with the surrounding environment and humans during the execution of specific tasks.

Project description
RAI’s fundamental vision is to bridge the gap between theory and reality, and the team has a strong background in field robotics. Specific application areas we focus on include long-term autonomous missions in large and uncertain environments, semantic mission planning using foundation models, agentic task decomposition and event-driven replanning, and autonomous, semantically aware inspection of complex infrastructure. The RAI team has strong European and national participation in several research, development and innovation projects.

Duties
As a PhD student, you will conduct research with substantial theoretical and experimental components, to be published in peer-reviewed, internationally recognized journals and at major conferences. The position includes supervising degree projects and providing support with applications for funding from research funding agencies or councils, EU framework programmes or industry. The position may also include teaching assistance, seminars and presentations. You will work in the field of robot autonomy, and all activities will be linked to national, European and global research and development projects. The PhD position will involve intensive research activities in field experimentation and theoretical development. Research areas:

Long-term autonomy in uncertain environments
a. Agentic planning and reasoning
- Semantic mission planning using foundation models
- Task decomposition based on foundation models
- Event-driven task replanning

b. Autonomous inspection planning
- Uncertainty aware planning
- Multi-agent systems for inspection planning

Qualifications
To qualify for the position, you must hold a master’s degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, computer science or another relevant subject. Good knowledge of C++, Python and ROS 2 is required. Good scientific skills, with demonstrated proficiency in experimental research, and very good communication skills are an advantage. You will represent the group in various contexts, both in Sweden and abroad, so very good knowledge of English is required.

For further information about a specific subject see General syllabus for the Board of the faculty of science and technology.

Employment as a PhD student is limited to four years. Teaching and other departmental duties may be added, up to 20% of full-time working hours. The place of work is Luleå, and the starting date is by agreement.

jobs.title: PhD student in phosphorus-based photoswitches
jobs.description_html:
Offer Description

The Department of Chemistry - Ångström conducts research and education in the chemistry field. The department has more than 270 employees and has a turnover of 300 million SEK. At the department's five programs, we conduct very successful research of a high international standard. We have a large number of externally funded research projects, often with international cooperation and we see continued good growth in our subject area. The department has education assignments in engineering programs and master's programs. More information is available on our website Department of Chemistry Ångström Laboratory. 

Duties
We are recruiting a PhD student to the Crespi group at the Department of Chemistry - Ångström Laboratory for the Swedish Research Council-funded project “Hemiphosphaindigos: New Gears for Molecular Machines” (2026-04728). The project explores how phosphorus can be used to control light-induced structural changes in organic molecules and to develop new photoswitches and molecular motors.

The PhD student will primarily design and synthesize new phosphorus-containing indigoid chromophores, purify and characterize the products using techniques including NMR and mass spectrometry, and investigate their photochemical properties. Experiments will include UV-Vis spectroscopy, irradiation studies, photostationary-state analysis, quantum-yield measurements and thermal kinetics. A central goal is to connect molecular structure and phosphorus functionalization with isomerization efficiency and stability.

In later stages, the student will contribute to studies of directional molecular motion and the effects of supramolecular confinement on photochemistry. Advanced time-resolved spectroscopy and computational chemistry will be integrated through expertise within the group and international collaborations, with opportunities for training in complementary methods. Duties also include doctoral coursework, publication and presentation of results. Teaching may be included according to departmental arrangements.

Requirements
To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must

  • have been awarded a second-cycle degree in chemistry or a closely related discipline, or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • acquired essentially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

The candidate must have:

  • very good oral and written proficiency in English.
  • practical experience of organic synthesis, purification and structural characterization from a degree project or research project, and the ability to plan, document and interpret laboratory experiments carefully and safely.

Consideration will also be given to good collaborative skills, drive and independence, and how the applicant’s experience and skills complement and strengthen ongoing research within the department, and how they stand to contribute to its future development.

Additional qualifications
Experience in organophosphorus or other main-group chemistry, photochemistry or photochromism, UV-Vis or NMR spectroscopy, reaction kinetics or supramolecular chemistry is an advantage. Previous work with photosensitive or chiral molecules or quantum-chemical calculations is also relevant. Applicants are not expected to have expertise in all these areas.

About the employment

The employment is a temporary position according to the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5 § 7. Scope of employment 100 %. Starting 1 February 2027 or as agreed. Placement: Uppsala.

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines.

The application should include a cover letter explaining your motivation and relevant laboratory experience, a CV, degree certificates and transcripts, a Master’s thesis or equivalent written research work, and contact details for two referees.

jobs.title: PhD Position Improving Symbolic AI through Learning and Reasoning
jobs.institution: Delft University of Technology via AcademicTransfer
jobs.description_html:
Offer Description

Join TU Delft in developing AI that thinks like a scientist

Job description
While all the headlines are full of AI learning from massivve datasets, in this position you will investigate how can we teach machines to learn from tiny amounts of data. You will investigate how how can we achieve this goal by making AI think like a scientist -- reason about which models and plausible and should be explored. We will build this new approach upon the combination of program synthesis and automated reasoning, and apply it to actual problems from scientific discovery and robotics.

You will join the Algorithmics Group in the Department of Software Technology, Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS). You will collaborate with PhD students and postdocs working on program synthesis and automated reasoning, and will have opportunities to co-supervise students. You will be supervised by Prof. Sebastijan Dumancic.

Job requirements
The ideal candidate will be an ambitious, proactive, reflective, and results-driven researcher. We are looking for the following:

  • MSc degree in Computer Science and/or Artificial Intelligence (essential)
  • prior experience in automated reasoning (essential)
  • prior experinece with symbolic machine learning approaches (essential)
  • prior experience in applying automated reasoning or machine learning in biology, chemistry, or other naturla sciences (desirable)
  • good communication, organisation, and writing skills
  • good programming skills and desire to produce usable open-source software


TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.

For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.

At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.

Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science
The Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) brings together three scientific disciplines. Combined, they reinforce each other and are the driving force behind the technology we all use in our daily lives. Technology such as the electricity grid, which our faculty is helping to make completely sustainable and future-proof. At the same time, we are developing the chips and sensors of the future, whilst also setting the foundations for the software technologies to run on this new generation of equipment – which of course includes AI. Meanwhile we are pushing the limits of applied mathematics, for example mapping out disease processes using single cell data, and using mathematics to simulate gigantic ash plumes after a volcanic eruption. In other words: there is plenty of room at the faculty for ground-breaking research. We educate innovative engineers and have excellent labs and facilities that underline our strong international position. In total, more than 1000 employees and 4,000 students work and study in this innovative environment.

Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science.

Conditions of employment
Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met.

Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%.

As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills.

The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged.

Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. jobs.title: PhD Position: Ecology of Waterway Management
jobs.description_html:
Offer Description

We have five positions available on the new BALANS project in the Netherlands: three PhD positions (at Radboud University (RU), the University of Groningen (RUG) and FLORON/RAVON respectively), one 4-year postdoctoral position (RU) and one two-year position for a research assistant that will become available later in 2027 (RUG).

These positions are part of a larger project funded by LVVN (Dutch Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Food Security and Nature) dedicated to the management of waterways. Waterways, such as ditches, are maintained to ensure sufficient water flow capacity, but also harbour important biodiversity. BALANS will generate knowledge on best practices for future management of waterways, searching for a balance between their practical functionality and their biodiversity. The results will be used for the revision of the new code of conduct for waterway management in the Netherlands (2029) and will be obtained by a consortium including RU, RUG, FLORON, RAVON, and Wageningen Environmental Research (WEnR), with project management by STOWA (Foundation for Applied Water Research), and guided by a committee including representatives from the Dutch water boards and species conservation NGOs.

Key topics that will be investigated are the timing, frequency and spatial scales of mowing activities, and the type of machinery applied. Methodological approaches will include the analysis of available data from water boards, field monitoring, field experiments that manipulate mowing and lab-based experiments for a mechanistic understanding. Research will be carried out across different types of landscapes and waterway dimensions, and will include impacts on different species groups (fish, plants, birds, macrofauna, amphibians, mammals) for which we will apply different monitoring techniques (e.g. camera trapping, tracking, surveys).

As a PhD candidate, you will combine data analyses with setting up and running ecological experiments to examine the effects of various types of waterway management on aquatic and terrestrial plant and animal species. The focus will be on field monitoring, field experiments and targeted lab experiments to unravel general mechanisms in the response of species to mowing activity and other stressors. Work will include comparing the effectiveness of sampling techniques on a diverse range of species groups. You will work at the Department of Ecology at Radboud University, collaborating with the other two PhD candidates in this project.

PhD candidates will receive varied, cutting-edge research training, with ample opportunities to attend advanced courses, workshops and conferences, complemented by training in transferable skills and teaching - as standard at Radboud University. As a PhD candidate at Radboud University, you will be expected to be committed to conducting independent and original scientific research, reporting it in international publications and presentations, and presenting the results in a PhD thesis to be completed within four years. PhD candidates will be expected to contribute 10% of their overall workload to teaching.

Would you like to learn more about what it’s like to pursue a PhD at Radboud University? Visit the page about working as a PhD candidate.

The other positions in the BALANS project can be found here:

Postdoctoral Researcher at Radboud University
PhD position at the University of Groningen
PhD position at FLORON/RAVON

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Galactic archaeology with 4MOST
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

Lund University has been involved in preparing for 4MOST for more than ten years. Several researchers hold leading roles, directing surveys and the working groups that analyse the raw data. We are now seeking a PhD student to work with data that will be released continuously over the next five years. The research focuses on Galactic archaeology based on spectroscopic observations of stars in the Milky Way.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at the Faculty of Science at naturvetenskap.se Doctoral studies | Faculty of Science

Subject and project description

We are seeking a PhD student in observational astronomy. The student will analyse spectroscopic data from 4MOST to understand the origins of the Milky Way and how its stellar populations formed and evolved. The thesis may also include opportunities to develop new observational projects.

  • General syllabys NAASFY02

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral education, which mainly consists of writing a doctoral thesis.

  • Conduct research in the subject area
  • Publish in high-quality journals
  • Participate inproject meetings at Lund University and within the 4MOST consortium
  • Present results at national and international conferences

In addition to studies, a maximum of 20% of working time may be spent on teaching and other departmental work.

Qualifications

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

Specific admission requirements

To be admitted to the third-cycle programme in Astronomy and Astrophysics the student must have earned credits in first and second-cycle programmes in which physics, mathematics and/or corresponding engineering subjects have been substantial elements. In addition to 60 credits in basic physics, there is a requirement for at least 30 credits in subjects of relevance to Astronomy and Astrophysics, e.g., courses in astronomy or other physics subjects, or engineering subjects such as space technology and automatic control. The 90 credits must include at least 45 second-cycle credits.

Equivalent knowledge acquired through corresponding programmes will be assessed individually.

In order to enable interdisciplinary initiatives and important specialisations in certain areas, students with qualifications in subjects other than Astronomy and Astrophysics may be considered for admission.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:  

  • good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems.
  • good written and oral communication skills
  • good ability to cooperate
  • very good knowledge of English, spoken and written

Merits

  • Strong numerical and analytical problem-solving skills, and experience with programming languages, particularly Python
  • Experience working with and analysing stellar spectra
  • Experience with statistical analys of large datasets

Selection criteria

The selection of eligible applicants will be made taking into account the ability to benefit from the training based on the following criteria:

  • knowledge that is an advantage (see reuirements and merits above)
  • demonstrated ability to tackle complex research problems, work both collaborately and independently, and complete taskson time
  • consideration will be given to the applicant’s ability to collaborate, initiative, and independence, as well as how their experience and skills indicate they have the qualities needed to successfully complete the doctoral education

We offer

Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme.

More about working at Lund University on lu.se. 

About the employment

The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, starting as soon as possible. Third cycle studies at Faculty of Science consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§.

More about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staffpages.  

Other

Interviews will be conducted online via Zoom

How to apply

The application should be written in English and you must attach to your application:

  • CV and personal letter with a justification of why you are interested in the training place/employment and in what way the research project matches your interests and your educational background.
  •  Copies of issued study certificates and/or diplomas. These should prove your basic and special eligibility for the doctoral education subject and show that you have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral education project.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Physics with focus on attosecond Physics
jobs.description_html:
The research at the Division of Atomic Physics is centered on different applications of optics and lasers, including atomic and molecular physics with ultrashort light pulses, high-intensity laser-plasma physics, quantum information, and biophotonics. The Division operates the High-Power Laser Facility, including several advanced femtosecond laser systems and collaborate with several free electron laser facilities. It is a central part of a major interdisciplinary research environment within the Lund University, the Lund Laser Centre, LLC. The division is also heavily involved in undergraduate education, especially within the Photonics programme.

Work duties

At the division, research is performed on the generation and application of extremely short light pulses, in the attosecond and extreme ultraviolet range. The activities span from ultrafast laser technology and extreme nonlinear optics to studies of the electron dynamics in atoms and molecules as well as more complex systems using attosecond light pulses. The division of Atomic Physics is now looking for one PhD student for the project described below.

The project is funded through a Marie Sklodowska-Curie doctoral network:

Quantum information science and ultrafast nonlinear control at the attosecond timescale – QU-ATTO

This means that the positions come with some additional constraints and possibilities. The candidates recruited for these positions cannot have worked in Sweden for the last 5 years to be eligible. The positions come with a training network in Europe together with 15 PhD students in different countries.

The project focuses on using a technique for the tomographic reconstruction of entangled states in photoionization. The goal is to improve the technique that has been developed in Lund for the reconstruction of the density matrix of photoelectron originating from the absorption of ultrashort XUV pulses by atoms and molecules.

The main duties of doctoral students are to devote themselves to their research studies which includes participating in research projects and third cycle courses. The work duties can also include teaching and other departmental duties (no more than 20%).

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if he or she:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third-cycle studies in Physics if he or she has:

  • at least 30 second-cycle credits of relevance to the subject, of which at least 15 credits shall comprise a second-cycle degree project, or
  • an MSc in engineering physics or an associated field, or a Master’s degree in physics or an associated field.

 Equivalent knowledge acquired through corresponding programmes will be assessed individually. In order to enable interdisciplinary initiatives and important specialisations in certain areas, students with qualifications in subjects other than Physics may be considered for admission.

Finally, the student must be judged to have the potential to complete the programme.

Additional requirements:

  • Very good oral and written proficiency in English.
  • The student should have a background in optics/photonics and/or atomic physics/quantum mechanics.

Other assessment criteria

Experience in some of the following areas is a qualification for all the projects:

  • Femtosecond lasers and ultrafast optics
  • Quantum optics
  • High-order harmonic generation and attosecond physics
  • Photoelectron and photoion spectroscopy
  • Data analysis, vacuum technique, and mechanical design

Basis of assessment

Selection to postgraduate studies is based on the expected ability to perform well in the studies. The evaluation of the ability to perform well is based primarily on the results of studies at the basic and advanced levels, in particular:

  1. Knowledge and skills relevant to the thesis project and the subject of the study.

  4. Other experience relevant to postgraduate studies, such as professional experience.

Consideration will also be given to good collaborative skills, drive and independence, and how the applicant, through his or her experience and skills, is deemed to have the abilities necessary for successfully completing the third cycle programme.

Only those admitted to third cycle studies may be appointed to a doctoral studentship. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. A doctoral studentship is a fixed-term employment of a maximum of 5 years (including 20% departmental duties). Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§.

Applications may be written in English or Swedish and include a cover letter stating the reasons why you are interested in the position and in what way the research project corresponds to your interests and educational background. The application must also contain a CV, degree certificate or equivalent, and other documents you wish to be considered (grade transcripts, contact information for your references, letters of recommendation, etc.).

jobs.title: Doctoral student in computer science with focus on program transformation
jobs.department: Lund University, LTH, Department of Computer Science
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The position is within the Software Development and Environments division, part of the Department of Computer Science.  The division is exploring novel tools, languages, and methods for supporting software development, and conducts research in a variety of topics that include refactoring, program analysis, compiler construction, declarative specification languages, distributed development environments, and automatic program repair. Its research involves strong collaborations both locally within Lund University, internationally with other universities, and with industrial partners, such as ABB and Ericsson, including research driven by industrial PhD students. The division currently has twelve members, and regularly organises group activities to foster a positive working environment.

The division is actively developing the JastAdd metacompilation framework, which is the foundation for several compilers and software tools, including the division's ExtendJ extensible Java compiler and the static analysis tools IntraJ and MetaDL.

More about the Software Development and Environments group (sde.cs.lth.se/)
More about JastAdd (jastadd.cs.lth.se/web/)
More about ExtendJ (extendj.org)
More about MetaDL (github.com/lu-cs-sde/metadl)

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will learn to approach questions and challenges scientifically. In short, this means that you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se. 

Subject and project description

This research project aims to develop novel tools and techniques that enforce rigid guard-rails during software refactoring and other forms of software evolution. We assume an unreliable source of program transformations, such as a human developer or a large language model.  The guard-rail mechanism will then inspect, steer, and augment any sequence of program transformations to detect and recover from unintended behavioural change.
The position is funded by the Excellence Center at Linköping – Lund in Information Technology (ELLIIT), and it is a collaboration with the Natural Language Processing group at Linköping University, part of the division of Artificial Intelligence and Integrated Computer Systems.

More about ELLIIT (elliit.se)
More about the Division of Artificial Intelligence and Integrated Computer Systems at Linköping University (liu.se/en/organisation/liu/ida/aiics)

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme, which includes participation in research projects as well as third cycle courses, seminars and conferences.

The work duties include:

  • Research on automatic program analysis and program transformation applied to preventing unintended behavioural change during refactoring and similar program evolution tasks. You will work towards exploring approaches that can aid real-world software evolution, and examine qualitative aspects of these approaches.
  • Applying appropriate research methods: depending on the trajectory of this research, different and possibly novel methodologies may be required to provide robust answers to the underlying research questions. You will learn, apply, and possibly support the development of suitable methods.
  • Artefact-oriented activity: You will develop software tools, algorithms, and other software components. These should be evaluated in realistic scenarios and integrated with, as well as shared within, the project team.
  • Presentation and collaboration: You will present your research findings at the annual ELLIIT workshop in southern Sweden and discuss your work at meetings with academic project partners, including personal meetings with our collaboration partners in Linköping.
  • Interaction with the industry: You will have opportunities to discuss your work and collaborate with industrial researchers, especially in Lund.
  • The duties also include participation in teaching and other departmental work (limited to a maximum of 20% of working hours).

Qualifications

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in computer science if the applicant has:

  • at least 60 second-cycle credits at an advanced level with relevance for the research topic, or
  • an MSc in Engineering in Computer Science and Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Information and Communication Technology, Engineering Physics or Engineering Mathematics.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • Knowledge or experience in at least one of the following areas (demonstrated e.g. in the form of a university course, or through professional experiences or contributions to relevant open source projects):
    • o compiler construction, or
    • o the foundations of static program analysis.
  • good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems.
  • good written and oral communication skills.
  • good ability to cooperate.
  • very good knowledge of English, in speech and writing.
  • very good programming experience (demonstrated e.g. in the form of professional experiences, contributions to open source projects, or outstanding results in university courses).
  • persistence and the ability to plan and structure your own work
  • curiosity and willingness to learn and adopt new techniques, especially within the cross-disciplinary scope of the project

Other qualifications (advantages)

For the doctoral programme in question, it is advantageous if you can demonstrate experience or knowledge in one or more of the following subjects:

  • developing automatic program transformation tools, such as
    • o refactoring tools, or
    • o meta-programming tools.
  • software development in teams, especially in the context of:
    • o professional software engineering,
    • o open source projects, or
    • o legacy software engineering projects.
  • dynamic program analysis.
  • programming in Java.
  • functional or declarative programming (logic programming, reference attribute grammars etc.).
  • natural language processing, machine learning, and/or applying large language models, such as
    • o working with the underlying machine learning techniques, such as latent/embedding spaces, representation learning, or transformers,
    • o training or fine-tuning such models, or
    • o applying them to software development / software engineering tasks.
  • systematic evaluation of software systems and relevant statistical methods.
  • systems programming.
  • areas of discrete mathematics with relation to program analysis (lattice theory, type theory, Galois connections etc.).

We offer

Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme.  This project additionally offers collaboration opportunities with Linköping University via its joint supervision structure, and industrial outreach opportunities via ELLIIT, such as the annual ELLIIT workshop.

More about working at Lund University on lu.se. 

About the employment

The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, with intended start date in the spring of 2027 or according to agreement, but no later than 2027-12-31. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§.

More about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staffpages. 

How to apply

Applications shall be written in English and include:

  • CV and a cover letter stating the reasons why you are interested in the doctoral programme/employment and in what way the research project corresponds to your interests and educational background.
  • Copies of issued study certificates and/or awarded degree certificates. These must confirm that you meet the general and specific admission requirements for the doctoral programme and show that you have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral programme project.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Biology (Invertebrate colour vision)
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

For your doctoral research, you will be a part of the Bok lab, which uses a wide range of techniques to study the evolution and ecology of vision in diverse invertebrates. Or lab is embedded within in the Lund Vision Group, a highly collaborative cluster of eight labs, internationally recognised as one of the leading centres in comparative visual science in the world. With 35-40 academics at all education and career stages, our vision research stretches across the entire animal kingdom, from jellyfishes, insects, and crustaceans, to squids and vertebrates. Our speciality is the design and evolution of eyes, how eyes are adapted to different lifestyles and habitats, and how vision is used for navigation and for controlling behaviour. Our techniques range from optics, electrophysiology and theoretical modelling, to microscopy, molecular biology and behavioural experiments. This thriving research environment offers broad support for doctoral education and research.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at the Faculty of Science at naturvetenskap.se Doctoral studies | Faculty of Science

Subject and project description

Aims: Colour vision has only to date been conclusively shown to exist in two of Earth’s approximately 32 animal phyla – vertebrates and arthropods. However, there are two additional known examples where colour vision may be possible – the firefly squid, a mollusc, and the alciopid worm, an annelid. Both are midwater marine species that are night active and live in deep water, yet they have astonishing retinal specializations that may contribute to colour vision. The aims of this PhD thesis will be to discover if these marine invertebrates have convergently evolved colour vision. Further, what behaviours are controlled by colour vision, and do they use the same visual processing circuits and principles to interpret colour information as we see in arthropods and vertebrates? This project will answer these questions using molecular, neurological, electrophysiological, and behavioural techniques in the field and lab.

Project background: This project grows naturally from ongoing research in the Bok Lab and contributes directly to our overall projects regarding the evolution of complex eyes and visual capabilities in crustaceans (water fleas and mantis shrimp) cephalopods (firefly squid), and polychaetes (alciopids and fan worms). The student will benefit from mentorship from the Bok lab's existing postdoctoral researchers who have completed preliminary work for this project. Further, the project synergises well with other research in Sensory Biology and Aquatic Ecology units. The Bok lab has recently been awarded several large grants from the ERC, Swedish Research Council, and the Human Frontiers Science Program, so the PhD student will benefit from a growing and dynamic academic environment.

  • Link to the general syllabus for third-cycle studies in Biology: General syllabus

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral education, which mainly consists of writing a doctoral thesis. You are expected to participate in a research project, doctoral courses, seminars and conferences. In the research project, you will use cutting edge behavioural, molecular, and neuroanatomical techniques to explore the function and evolution of possible colour receptors and their role in the visual ecology of polychaetes and cephalopods:

  1. ) Behaviour: At field stations in Italy and Japan, we will perform behavioural experiments testing the response of both species to colour and polarization stimuli. This will be based on custom light sources and projection screen setups that can vary the two light modalities independently.   
  2. ) Molecules: Alongside postdocs in the Bok Lab (Vanessa Stenvers and Alida Avola), the PhD student will use the results of single-nucleolus transcriptomic data to localize distinct photoreceptor and visual interneuron classes in the retina and optic lobe of both species. 
  3. ) Circuits: SBEM will be used to create connectomic resolution volume data for the retina and optic lobe of both species. Photoreceptor and interneuron synaptic connections and projections will be mapped to decipher the visual circuits. These data, along with the results from the molecular section will then be used to inform electrophysiology recordings to discover putative colour and polarisation opponent neurons in the optic lobe.

In addition to studies, a maximum of 20% of working time may be spent on teaching and other departmental work. You are expected to gain pedagogical experience as lab instructors for undergradate courses run by the Sensory Biology unit, and there are ample opportunities to gain experience in outreach and academic activities. You will be provided ample opportunities to present your work at local and international research conferences.

Qualifications

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in Biology if the applicant has completed an independent work (e.g. degree project) in a relevant subject comprising at least 30 higher education credits and have good oral and written proficiency in English. The special qualification may also have been obtained through other equivalent education, which is assessed on a case-by-case basis. In order to enable interdisciplinary initiatives and significant in-depth studies in certain areas, qualifications other than the applicant's subject-specific competence in Biology may be taken into account.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • Master’s degree in biology/marine biology or substantial equivalent knowledge acquired in some other way.
  • Practical experience with animal vision behavioral experiments.
  • Experience with fieldwork-based research.
