jobs.title: Doctoral student in Geographic Information Science (GIS) at MGeo
jobs.description_html:
The PhD student will be based at the GIS Centre, Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, Lund University. The GIS Centre conducts research, education and development in Geographical Information Science (GIScience), with particular expertise in geospatial analysis, GeoAI, digital twins, and spatial data infrastructures.

The position will be part of the Centre's research activities in GeoAI and Spatial Intelligence, with a particular focus on Autonomous GIS. This emerging research direction explores how artificial intelligence, large language models and multi-agent systems can enable GIS to understand complex spatial problems, reason about geographic information, and autonomously plan and execute geospatial workflows.

The GIS Centre provides an interdisciplinary research environment where expertise in GIScience, geospatial technologies and AI meet applications in environmental analysis, urban planning, sustainability and other societal challenges. The PhD student will work closely with researchers at the Centre and have opportunities to collaborate with national and international research partners.

The Centre offers a collegial, supportive and collaborative working environment that encourages scientific curiosity, independent thinking and professional development.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.


Subject and project description

The doctoral student will be admitted to third-cycle studies in Geobiosphere Science, with a specialisation in Geographical Information Science (GIScience). GIScience is an interdisciplinary research field concerned with the theories, methods and technologies for collecting, managing, analysing, modelling and communicating geographical information. The subject encompasses both fundamental methodological research and applications across environmental, societal and technological domains.

The doctoral research will focus on Autonomous GIS and Spatial Intelligence, an emerging research direction at the intersection of GIScience and artificial intelligence. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs), GeoAI and multi-agent systems are creating new opportunities to transform GIS from systems that primarily execute user-defined operations into intelligent systems capable of interpreting spatial problems, reasoning about geographical information, planning and executing geospatial workflows, and evaluating their results.

Despite these advances, important scientific challenges remain. These include the ability of AI systems to understand spatial concepts and relationships, integrate geographic knowledge with computational reasoning, select and coordinate appropriate geospatial methods, and ensure the reliability, transparency and geographical validity of autonomous analyses.

The doctoral student will investigate methods and frameworks for advancing Spatial Intelligence and Autonomous GIS, potentially addressing topics such as geospatial reasoning with LLMs, multi-agent architectures, autonomous geospatial workflow planning and execution, integration of geographic knowledge and analytical tools, and evaluation of the reliability and quality of AI-generated geospatial analyses.

The research is expected to contribute new scientific knowledge and methods in GIScience while advancing the foundations of intelligent and increasingly autonomous geospatial systems. The specific research questions and methodological approaches will be further developed in collaboration with the supervisors during the doctoral studies.

Work duties

Your main responsibility will be to pursue doctoral studies and conduct independent research in Autonomous GIS and Spatial Intelligence, leading to a doctoral thesis. You will develop research questions, investigate and develop new methods, design and conduct experiments, evaluate results, and communicate your findings primarily through publications in high-quality, peer-reviewed scientific journals..

You will work closely with your supervisors and other researchers at the GIS Centre, while gradually developing your independence as a researcher. Your doctoral education will also include relevant doctoral courses, participation in research seminars, and opportunities to present and discuss your research at national and international scientific conferences. You will be encouraged to engage in research collaborations and contribute to the Centre's academic activities and research environment. International travel may be required for conferences, research visits and collaborative activities.

In addition to your doctoral studies, you may participate in teaching and other departmental duties, corresponding to a maximum of 20% of your working time. These duties may include assisting with teaching, supervising student exercises and projects, and contributing to educational activities, particularly in GIS, geospatial analysis and GeoAI. The extent and nature of these duties will be determined based on departmental needs and your qualifications and interests.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

Specific admission requirements

  • To meet the specific admission requirements for third-cycle studies in Geobiosphere Science with a specialisation in Geographical Information Science, the applicant must have completed an independent degree project in a relevant subject comprising at least 30 higher education credits, or have acquired equivalent qualifications. Qualifications from other relevant disciplines may also be considered, particularly when appropriate for the interdisciplinary nature of the doctoral research.

 

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following qualifications and competences are also required:

  • A Master's degree in Geographical Information Science, Geoinformatics, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, or a closely related field.
  • Good knowledge of artificial intelligence and machine learning, including an understanding of fundamental methods and principles, and familiarity with modern deep learning approaches and large language models (LLMs).
  • Experience with AI and machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or similar technologies.
  • Strong programming skills in Python, with the ability to develop, implement, test and evaluate computational methods and algorithms.
  • Good analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to approach complex scientific and technical challenges systematically.
  • An interest in GIScience, geospatial analysis and spatial intelligence, with the motivation and ability to develop interdisciplinary expertise at the intersection of geographical information science and artificial intelligence.
  • Good ability to work independently and collaboratively, including the capacity to formulate research problems, take initiative and contribute constructively to an interdisciplinary research environment.
  • Good communication skills in English, both written and spoken.

 

The following qualifications will be considered advantageous:

  • Practical experience developing applications using LLMs, agentic AI, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool integration or multi-agent systems.
  • Experience with geospatial programming libraries and tools such as GeoPandas, Shapely, Rasterio, PyQGIS or ArcPy.
  • Knowledge of spatial reasoning and knowledge representation, including geographic semantics, ontologies, knowledge graphs or neuro-symbolic AI.
  • Experience in developing and evaluating computational methods and AI-based systems, including experimental design, software testing, version control, and integration of computational tools and APIs.
  • Demonstrated scientific writing skills, particularly experience preparing manuscripts or publications for peer-reviewed scientific journals.
  • Previous involvement in scientific research or publications in artificial intelligence, GIScience, GeoAI or related fields.

 

Selection criteria

The selection of eligible applicants will be made based on the above-mentioned qualifications and competences. In addition, personal qualifications will also be considered in the evaluation process including:

  • Strong scientific curiosity and creativity, with the ability to formulate original ideas and explore innovative approaches.
  • Ability to think critically, evaluate methods and results, and approach scientific challenges constructively.
  • A collegial and cooperative attitude, with a willingness to share knowledge, support colleagues and contribute positively to the research environment.
  • Good interpersonal and communication skills, including openness to feedback and respect for different perspectives.
  • Reliability, responsibility and professionalism, including the ability to honour commitments and contribute constructively to shared activities.
  • Motivation and enthusiasm for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of artificial intelligence and GIScience.

About the employment

The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, starting 2027-01-07 or due agreement. Third cycle studies at the Faculty of Science consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§.

How to apply

The application should be written in English and you must attach to your application:

  • CV and personal letter with a justification of why you are interested in the training place/employment and in what way the PhD research topic matches your interests and your educational background.
  •  Copies of issued study certificates and/or diplomas. These should prove your basic and special eligibility for the doctoral education subject and show that you have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral education project.

jobs.title: PhD student in biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The Biomarkers in Brain Disease research group at the Department of Experimental Medical Science investigates how disease mechanisms in the body and brain interact in Huntington’s disease. This work involves in vivo and in vitro experiments, microscopy and molecular biology methods.

The workplace and research environment are shared by five research groups, all working on neurodegenerative diseases, with approximately 25–30 people in total.

Together, they create a stimulating and international research environment in which we share research equipment and chemicals and hold joint laboratory meetings. The atmosphere is friendly and encourages a wide range of discussions. The research group is active in the European Huntington’s Disease Network and Lund University Huntington Centre.

Project description

The body’s biological clock regulates functions such as sleep, metabolism, immune function and brain activity. The central clock in the hypothalamus coordinates rhythms in the body’s cells and organs, which also have their own rhythms. Disturbances in sleep and circadian rhythms are common in neurodegenerative diseases, including Huntington’s disease (HD). Research suggests that these disturbances are not merely symptoms but may contribute to neurodegeneration.

HD is an inherited disorder that affects movement, cognition and psychiatric function. The mutated gene, which contains an expanded CAG repeat sequence, and the huntingtin protein are expressed not only in neurons but also in cells throughout the body.

Despite increasing knowledge, it remains unclear how disruptions to the body’s biological clocks affect the course of HD. It is also unknown whether modifying clock function could alter disease progression in HD.

This doctoral project will combine in vitro and in vivo studies and use methods such as RNA sequencing. The project requires a balance between experimental laboratory work and data analysis.

Tasks and responsibilities

The main task for a doctoral student is to devote yourself to your doctoral studies, therefore you will be both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

In addition to your full-time doctoral studies, you may participate in the supervision of Bachelor’s or Master’s students.

Qualifications

  • a second-cycle degree, completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 higher education credits at the second-cycle level, or in some other way acquired essentially equivalent knowledge within or outside the country.
  • good ability to utilize the doctoral studies

Merits for the position are:

  • priority will be given to applicants who have graduated no more than three years before the closing date for applications
  • Good knowledge of neurodegenerative diseases and molecular biology
  • Demonstrated experience of in vivo and in vitro studies
  • Very good knowledge of molecular biology
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and collaborate effectively
  • Good ability to present research clearly in writing and visually
  • Good spoken and written English skills
  • A well-organised and independent approach to work
  • Experience of primer design and RT-PCR optimisation
  • Experience of working collaboratively on ambitious research projects
  • Ability to accept constructive feedback and a willingness to develop and learn during the doctoral programme

Great emphasis will be placed on how the applicant, through his/her experience and competence, is judged to have the ability needed to complete the doctoral studies

What we offer

Lund University is a government agency, which means that you get special benefits, generous holidays and a favourable occupational pension.  As a doctoral student at Lund University, you are both admitted as a student and employed, which gives you several benefits. Read more about being admitted and employed  at the university's website.

Rules and regulations concerning employment as a doctoral student can be found in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), Chapter 5, Sections 1-7. Provisions regarding admission to doctoral studies are found in Chapter 6, Section 3 of the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100). More information is available on the university's website

It must also include a CV, degree certificate or equivalent, and any other documents you wish to bring to our attention, such as copies of academic transcripts, referee details and letters of recommendation. jobs.title: Doctoral student in Numerical simulations of turbulent heat transfer over rough surfaces
jobs.department: Lund University, Faculty of Engineering, LTH, Department of Energy Sciences
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The doctoral student will be employed at the Department of Energy Sciences, Faculty of Engineering (LTH), Lund University, and will be part of the Division of Heat Transfer. The research environment conducts research in fluid mechanics, heat transfer and computational fluid dynamics, with particular emphasis on the numerical modelling and simulation of turbulent flows and engineering applications.

The doctoral student will work in a research environment combining fundamental research with applications of direct relevance to industry. The project will be carried out in close collaboration with Siemens Energy AB, Ericsson AB, TRATON AB and RISE. This provides an opportunity to work at the interface between fundamental research, advanced numerical methods and industrially relevant problems.

The doctoral student will have access to expertise in Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), turbulence, heat transfer, numerical methods and high-performance computing. The work will involve extensive use of high-performance computing resources, including both GPU- and CPU-based computing platforms.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se. 

Subject and project description

Surface roughness has a significant influence on turbulent flow, wall friction and heat transfer in many engineering systems. Understanding and predicting these effects is important in a wide range of applications, including energy systems, thermal management and transport applications. Despite its practical importance, accurately predicting turbulent heat transfer over realistic rough surfaces remains challenging, particularly when the properties of the working fluid and the relative thicknesses of the momentum and thermal boundary layers vary.

The aim of this doctoral project is to develop a deeper physical understanding of the interaction between surface roughness, turbulence and heat transfer, and to translate this understanding into improved engineering models.

The research will primarily use high-fidelity numerical simulations, including Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) and Large Eddy Simulation (LES). Different CFD codes will be employed depending on the problem and required level of fidelity, including OpenFOAM, CaNS and nekRS. The simulations will make extensive use of modern high-performance computing resources based on both GPUs and CPUs.

The project will investigate how surface roughness influences turbulent flow and heat transfer for different fluids and thermal conditions. Particular attention will be given to the interaction between roughness geometry, turbulent structures, and the momentum and thermal boundary layers, including conditions in which the relative thicknesses of the thermal and momentum boundary layers differ.

The high-fidelity simulation data will be used to identify relevant physical mechanisms and scaling relations and to support the development of reduced-order and engineering models for rough-surface heat transfer, including improved models and correlations suitable for Reynolds-Averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) simulations.

The overall objective is to establish a connection between fundamental turbulence physics, high-fidelity numerical simulations and computational models that can be applied to engineering design.

The project will be conducted in close collaboration with Siemens Energy AB, Ericsson AB, TRATON AB and RISE, providing opportunities for scientific exchange and interaction with researchers and engineers working on industrial applications of turbulent flow and heat transfer.

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral studies, which include participation in research projects as well as third-cycle courses, seminars and scientific conferences.

A central part of your work will be to perform and analyse high-fidelity numerical simulations of turbulent flow and heat transfer over rough surfaces. You will use CFD and high-performance computing frameworks, which may include OpenFOAM, CaNS and nekRS, on CPU- and GPU-based systems. Applicants should already have experience with comparable simulation tools and High Performance Computing (HPC) systems; familiarity with the specific codes used in the project is an advantage.  

The work duties include:

  • Performing DNS and LES of turbulent flow and heat transfer over rough surfaces using OpenFOAM, CaNS, nekRS or comparable CFD and scientific-computing frameworks.
  • Setting up, running, validating and analysing simulations on GPU- and CPU-based high-performance computing systems.
  • Investigating the influence of surface roughness geometry and characteristics on turbulent momentum and heat transfer.
  • Investigating the effects of fluid properties and thermal conditions, including different relationships between momentum and thermal boundary-layer thicknesses.
  • Processing, analysing and visualising large datasets and identifying physical mechanisms and developing scaling relations from DNS and LES data.
  • Developing reduced-order models, correlations and improved RANS modelling approaches for turbulent heat transfer over rough surfaces.
  • Assessing and validating the developed models against high-fidelity numerical data and, where available, experimental data.
  • Collaborating with researchers at Lund University and with the project's industrial and research partners.
  • Presenting research results at project meetings, scientific conferences and international workshops.
  • Writing scientific articles for publication in international peer-reviewed journals and contributing to the doctoral thesis.

The work may involve travel within Sweden and internationally for project meetings, visits to research and industrial partners, conferences and research collaborations.

The duties may also include participation in teaching and other departmental work, however to a maximum of 20% of working hours.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • A Master’s degree, or equivalent qualification, in mechanical engineering, engineering physics, aerospace engineering, energy engineering, applied mathematics, computational science, or another subject relevant to the project.
  • Good knowledge of fluid mechanics, CFD, and turbulent flows, and relevant knowledge of heat transfer.
  • A substantial research project or thesis in CFD, turbulence, heat transfer, or a closely related field.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently set up, run, troubleshoot, validate and analyse numerical simulations. This should be supported by research experience, rather than coursework alone.
  • Scientific programming experience in a relevant language, such as C/C++, Fortran and Python or Matlab.
  • Practical experience running computational simulations on HPC systems.
  • Ability to plan and carry out research tasks with limited day-to-day supervision, analyse results critically and communicate findings clearly.
  • Very good knowledge of English, spoken and written.

Other qualifications

For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered meriting:

  • Experience with DNS or LES, wall-bounded turbulence, turbulent heat transfer, surface roughness or convective heat transfer.
  • Experience with a CFD or high-fidelity simulation framework, such as OpenFOAM, CaNS, nekRS or a comparable research code.
  • Experience with parallel computing or GPU-accelerated scientific computing.
  • Knowledge of RANS, wall modelling or thermal turbulence modelling.
  • Research experience beyond the Master’s thesis, such as work as a research assistant or research engineer.
  • Experience presenting or publishing research results or collaborating with industry.

Applicants are not expected to have experience with every code used in the project. However, they should have demonstrated the ability to carry out computational research independently using a comparable CFD or scientific-computing framework. They are expected to contribute from an early stage, building on existing experience in numerical simulation and HPC.

The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, starting as soon as possible. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§.

More about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staffpages.

Other

The doctoral student will be expected to interact regularly with the project's academic and industrial partners. The position may therefore include visits to partner organisations and participation in project meetings, workshops and conferences in Sweden and abroad.

How to apply

Applications shall be written in English and include:

  • CV and cover letter stating why you are interested in the doctoral programme and this particular research project, and explaining how your educational background, research experience and interests relate to CFD, turbulence and heat transfer.
  • Copies of issued study certificates and/or awarded degree certificates. These must confirm that you meet the general and specific admission requirements for the doctoral programme and demonstrate that you have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral research project.
  • Degree transcripts showing completed courses and grades.

We welcome your application.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in applied nuclear physics
jobs.description_html:
The Nuclear Structure Group at the Division of Particle and Nuclear Physics at Lund University is seeking a skilled and highly motivated PhD student to work on upcycling state-of-the-art detectors used in nuclear structure studies for environmental monitoring and emergency preparedness. The Division of Particle and Nuclear Physics, which has approximately 50 employees, conducts a broad range of research in both theoretical and experimental particle and heavy-ion physics, as well as experimental nuclear physics. The Nuclear Structure Group is active in several international collaborations exploiting large-scale accelerator facilities across the globe. With the present position, however, we thrive to intensify local collaborations with the Biospheric and Anthropogenic Radioactivity group.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.
As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.
More about being a doctoral student at the Science Faculty.  

Project Description

The project "From Lundium to L.U.N.D.I.U.M." (Swedish Radiation Safety Authority) will see the upcycling of various state-of-the-art components of the Lundium decay station for studies of Super Heavy Elements into L.U.N.D.I.U.M.: the Lund University Next-generation Device for Identification of Unknown radioactive sources and environmental Monitoring. L.U.N.D.I.U.M. will have unprecedented alpha-beta-gamma resolving capabilities stemming from its high granularity of detector components and contemporary multi-coincidence data acquisition systems.

The research environment constitutes an interdisciplinary community of knowledge and practice focused on data analysis and simulations of complex datasets to be used for radiation safety and emergency preparedness within the disciplines of physics, work environment, medical radiation physics, and environmental monitoring.

We are now recruiting one PhD student to be integrated into the research group and lead this development from conceptualization and optimization via Monte Carlo Geant4 simulations to realization of the device.

The PhD student will collaborate during specific phases of their doctoral education, with the Biospheric and Anthropogenic Radioactivity group for sample collection and preparation.

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme, which includes participation in research projects as well as third cycle courses, seminars and conferences. 

The PhD project will address the need for expanding the Swedish network of environmental monitor and emergency preparedness with the development and usage of a new-generation device for nuclear forensics. The tasks include:

  • Optimize via Monte Carlo simulations the geometry and elements of the new device upcycling the existing state-of-the-art detector components for measurement of various types of environmental filter and electroplated samples.
  • Conduct and coordinate the mechanical construction of the device and develop its data acquisition system and data analysis framework.
  • Validation of the measurements using simulated contamination samples provided by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) for yearly proficiency tests.
  • In close collaboration with the Biospheric and Anthropogenic Radioactivity group, develop methods to analyse radioactive aerosols from environmental samples.

At various stages of the project, close collaboration is envisaged with researchers at the University of Jyväskylä, Finland, in charge of a comparable measurement station.

The research projects will be reported in the form of articles submitted for publication in scientific journals, reports to the funding organisation, and conference contributions.

The duties also include participation in teaching and other departmental work (up to a maximum of 20% of working time).

Qualifications

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Specific admission requirements

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third-cycle programme in Physics, if they:

  • has at least 45 second cycle credits in physics or engineering physics or an associated field, or
  • has a second cycle (master) degree in physics or engineering physics or an associated field.

The specific entry requirement may also have been obtained through other equivalent education, which is assessed in each individual case. Finally, the student must be judged to have the potential to complete the programme.

 Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • completion of courses amounting to at least 60 credits that are directly relevant to the PhD education
  • a strong ability to work independently and the ability to formulate and address scientific problems
  • good written and oral communication skills
  • good ability to collaborate
  • very good proficiency in English, both spoken and written
  • an interest in interdisciplinary work

Other qualifications (advantages)

For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as other qualifications:

  • excellent laboratory skills concerning contemporary radiation detectors
  • proficiency with multi-parameter data acquisition systems
  • proficiency in modern object oriented programming
  • knowledge of environmental radioactivity or radioecology knowledge of radionuclide production in nuclear power plants and spallation sources
  • previous experience to ionizing radiation detection
  • previous experience with Monte Carlo radiation transport codes

Other

The following criteria will be considered:

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Risk and Safety of Heterogeneous Swarm Systems
jobs.department: Lund University, Faculty of Engineering, Aviation and Aeronautical Sciences
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The Department of Aviation and Aeronautical Sciences strives to be a leading center for aeronautics research, development, and education. The department operates a certified commercial flight school (ATO) and an authorized drone school (ADS) under the name of Lund University School of Aviation, Sweden's only state-run civilian flight school. The department’s research facilities are based at Campus Ljungbyhed, providing a unique setting that integrates research, development, and education with access to airport infrastructure, including a runway system and controlled airspace. We seek to understand, innovate, and advance aviation through collaborative efforts, making it more accessible, sustainable, and safe in the digital age. The research emphasizes three primary areas: sustainable aviation, unmanned aviation, and aviation safety, with safety being a central theme across all initiatives.

This doctoral student position is at the Department of Aviation and Aeronautical Sciences and will work at the intersection between unmanned aviation and aviation safety, as part of the Center for Heterogeneous Adaptive Swarm Systems (CHASS) funded by Stiftelsen för Strategisk Forskning*  (SSF). CHASS includes three dual-use relevant large industrial partners (Saab, Sectra Communications and BAE Systems Hägglunds) and societal participation from the Swedish Defence Research Institute (FOI), the Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency (MCF) and the Swedish Civil Aviation Administration (LFV).

The duty station is Ljungbyhed.

*More about SSF

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se

Subject and project description

The research area is Risk and Safety of heterogeneous swarm systems.

The multi-disciplinary center for heterogeneous adaptive swarm systems, CHASS, is a national effort funded by the Swedish Strategic Research Foundation (SSF) to bring together leading researchers in AI, autonomous systems, robotics, and swarm intelligence to develop novel solutions for autonomous heterogeneous swarm systems for the benefit of Swedish industry and society. The vision is to make Sweden a leader in intelligent, adaptive, and trustworthy swarm systems by pioneering autonomous heterogeneous collectives of space, aerial, ground, surface, and underwater platforms that can operate as a unified intelligent entity with minimal human intervention. The research program focuses on six key themes: Drone Design, Adaptation, & Production; Perception, Sensing, & Communication; Autonomy, Localization, Mapping & Navigation; Coordination, Self-Governance, & Self-Improvement; Human Swarm Interaction; and Swarm-based Services & Socio-Technical Aspects.

CHASS is led by Linköping University and besides Lund University also includes Örebro University, each with CHASS-affiliated doctoral students, as well as a large number of industry and government stakeholders, providing a stimulating research environment. CHASS will drive world-class research in autonomous swarm systems through a strong, stimulating, and well-connected international research environment. Research outcomes will be validated in real-world scenarios with industry and public-sector partners. CHASS will also serve as a national hub for autonomous swarm systems, promoting education, knowledge sharing, innovation, and policy development.

The doctoral student position in this announcement will work within the theme of Swarm-based Services & Socio-Technical Aspects. It develops and evaluates risk assessment and safety management methodologies (for the phases before, during, and after operations) for heterogeneous swarms, including frameworks for risk assessment, adaptive capacity and control, and accountability and responsibility. The position will include interaction with other doctoral students and researchers within this theme, as well as the Human Swarm Interaction theme and the other technological development themes.

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme, which includes participation in research projects as well as third cycle courses, seminars and conferences.

The work duties include:

  • You will work in a multi-disciplinary research project focused on socio-technical aspects of control, risk, and safety of heterogeneous swarms resilience.
  • You will likely combine qualitative (e.g. interviews) and quantitative (e.g. modelling, statistics) methods.
  • You will travel in Sweden and abroad to interact with fellow researchers to collaborate and present research findings at scientific conferences.
  • As parts of the research may be conducted in collaboration with defence-related organisations, a security screening will be carried out if applicable.
  • The duties also include participation in teaching and other departmental work (however, a maximum of 20% of working hours).

Qualifications

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in Risk and Safety (TEVBRF11) if the applicant has:

  • at least 90 credits in subjects of relevance to the field, including at least 60 second cycle credits, or
  • a BSc in Fire Protection Engineering amounting to 210 credits.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • good knowledge in risk, system safety, design, and governance of socio-technical systems in complex settings,
  • good ability to take initiative and solve research challenges with drive, creativity, and persistence,
  • good ability to work in a structured way in a collaborative and inter-disciplinary environment,
  • good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems,
  • good written and oral communication skills,
  • good ability to cooperate with other researchers and practitioners,
  • very good knowledge of English, spoken and written.

Other qualifications

For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as meriting qualifications:

  • knowledge of aeronautical engineering, human-computer interaction, human factors engineering, cognitive science, human control of AI, unmanned aviation, critical infrastructure resilience, interaction design, industrial design engineering, and related disciplines,
  • skills and experience in modelling and simulation,
  • skills and experience in relevant software and programming environments, such as Matlab, Python, C++, UAS communication protocols (MAVLink), ROS2, git.
  • skills and experience in statistical analysis and quantitative research methods,
  • skills and experience relating to relevant qualitative research methods, such as interviews,
  • driving licence B,
  • practical experience of operations in manned or unmanned aviation.

Consideration will also be given to how the applicant, through his or her experience and skills, is deemed to have the abilities necessary for successfully completing the third cycle programme.

The division for Concrete Structures at KTH Civil and Architectural Engineering is in search for a doctoral student to be assigned a project on hydraulic design of structures within hydropower. Many dam facilities have been rebuilt or are to be upgraded to achieve a higher level of safety. A bottom outlet is a critical structure from both a dam safety and operational point of view. jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Civil and Architectural Engineering

The division for Concrete Structures at KTH Civil and Architectural Engineering is in search for a doctoral student to be assigned a project on reinforced concrete structures within hydropower. Dams in Sweden and many other countries are aging and have an average age of over 50 years. Spillways and associated concrete structures play a crucial role in reducing the risk of dam overflow and serious damage. However, over the years, these have been exposed to varying flows, including extreme high flows, which in many cases has caused damage. The most common repair method today is underwater concrete casting, which is costly and experience shows that many such repairs do not last as long as planned.

The project is part of a national research program within the hydropower area called SVC – Swedish Centre for Sustainable Hydropower. The research is carried out together with senior researchers at KTH and in interdisciplinary research collaboration with international researchers and industry partners. The aim is to create a better understanding of how damage occurs, what forces and hydraulic loads act, and how these affect both concrete and the rock subsurface. The project is expected to provide decision-making information for maintenance, repair and reconstruction of embankments and associated structures.

jobs.title: Doctoral student on structural health monitoring of concrete hydro dams
jobs.department: KTH, School of Architecture and Built Environment
jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Civil and Architectural Engineering

The division for Concrete Structures at KTH Civil and Architectural Engineering is in search for a doctoral student to be assigned a project on reinforced concrete structures within hydropower. Dams in Sweden and many other countries are aging and have an average age of over 50 years. As they age, damage becomes more common. Typical visible damage includes cracks, leaching and scratching of the concrete surface and can be detected by visual inspections. However, there are also many other types of damage that may be more difficult to detect, such as reinforcement corrosion. In order to maintain older dams in full operation with a high level of safety, the response of the dams should be continuously monitored.

The aim is to create a good understanding of the structural response of concrete dams during normal operation, what should be measured and where sensors should be placed. The project will also identify which types of sensors are appropriate to use and identify reasonable alarm limits.

jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Industrial Economics and Management

The deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has expanded rapidly across public and private sectors. AI-driven technologies—particularly machine learning algorithms and large language models —are becoming integral to knowledge creation, task augmentation, and business analytics. This shift has catalyzed a rise of AI ecosystems, which brings together AI startups, intermediaries, and established enterprises, fundamentally reshaping how employees, businesses, and entire industries function. However, while certain use cases offer efficiency gains, organizations frequently grapple with critical challenges, such as low returns on investment, output unreliability, and pressing ethical dilemmas.

This PhD project aims to critically analyze the organizational implications of AI. The PhD student may explore questions such as, but not limited to: How do organizations mitigate the managerial challenges stemming from the probabilistic nature of AI technologies? How will AI transform the modern industry; and what are the opportunities and risks associated with such transformation? Along with the Big Tech companies and AI giants, what role do startups and intermediaries play in a more responsible transformation towards AI-based economy?

The PhD position is a part of the Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program - Humanity and Society (WASP-HS), a national research program in Sweden. WASP-HS fosters novel interdisciplinary knowledge about AI and autonomous systems and their impact on humanity and society. WASP-HS enables cutting-edge research, expertise, and capacity building in the social sciences and humanities. For more information, see here.

jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Engineering Mechanics

FLOW is a strong community of researchers engaged in fundamental and applied research in fluid mechanics within the department of Engineering Mechanics.

We are currently seeking a PhD student in probabilistic machine learning to join the Fluids and Surfaces Group within FLOW. AI is becoming a critical investment across science and engineering, but fluid mechanics poses particular challenges: flows are often high-dimensional and chaotic, and couple physical processes across many scales.

This position offers an exciting opportunity for a highly motivated candidate to develop trustworthy probabilistic methods for inference, optimization and data assimilation. These methods will integrate simulations and experimental data into reliable tools for the design, prediction and control of complex fluid systems.

The work focuses on turbulent flows that carry electric charge, as found for example in power transformers. These systems involve coupled processes that are only partly understood, and measurements are sparse and costly. This makes them an ideal testbed, where models must be calibrated, uncertainties quantified and experiments chosen with care, with direct impact on safer and more sustainable power infrastructure. The project is funded by Digital Futures och Hitachi Energy

jobs.title: Doctoral student in fusion plasma physics and nuclear engineering
jobs.department: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Electrical Engineering 

The provision of plasma-facing components (PFCs) with sufficient lifetime is one of the major technological obstacles to be overcome in developing fusion reactors. Recently, the damage of PFCs due to interaction with runaway electrons (RE) has become a highly critical issue in evaluations of disruption consequences. ITER, currently seeks for the validation of relevant numerical models and tools against existing experimental evidence in order to gain confidence in their applications to predictive reactor modelling.

PhD project will focus on the development of modelling tools for simulations of RE-induced PFC damage and their validation against data from EUROfusion Consortium, and DIII-D (USA). The validated models will be employed for predictive modelling of specific ITER scenarios following input from the ITER Organization. The modelling of MeV RE energy deposition in PFCs will be performed with Monte Carlo simulations. These results will serve as input for the thermomechanical models to be developed in FEM and CFD software to address severe deformation and potential explosion of the material.

We offer expertise in the theory and modelling of plasma-surface interactions and electron transport into matter, access to state-of-the-art experimental data from the largest tokamaks worldwide and close collaboration with the Experiments & Plasma Operation Section of the ITER Organization.

Supervision: Prof. S. Ratynskaia. Decisions are made on admission.

Admission requirements

  • acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge

Programming skills in languages such as Fortran, Python, or C/C++,  is required for this position. 

In addition to the above, there is also a mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.

Selection

  • independently pursue his or her work,
  • collaborate with others,

  • analyze and work with complex issues,

jobs.title: PhD student in plant evolution
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Ecology and Genetics
jobs.description_html:
Are you passionate about studying how flowers have convergently evolved in response to bee pollinators? We are now looking for a PhD student in plant evolution to join us at the Plant Ecology and Evolution program, Department of Ecology and Genetics.

The Department of Ecology and Genetics (IEG) is an international environment with staff and students from all over the world. We are part of the Evolutionary Biology Center (EBC) which is a prime environment for graduate students interested in addressing fundamental and applied biological questions through an evolutionary perspective.

Project description

Convergent evolution in buzz-pollinated flowers
Convergent evolution, where similar traits evolve repeatedly across independent biological groups is a recurrent and important phenomenon in the history of life. In most studies of convergent evolution, similarity in function is assumed from similarity on phenotype (form). However, in principle, it is possible that similar traits evolve independently without functioning in the same way.

To date, few studies have explicitly compared similarity in form and function across a taxonomically broad sample of convergent plant lineages, and this is the main knowledge gap that the PhD student will address here. As a model system, we will study flowers that are pollinated by vibration-producing bees (buzz pollinated flowers). These flowers are one of the most widespread examples of convergent evolution in plants, encompassing more than 20,000 species. Our project will study independent origins of buzz pollinated flowers to: (1) evaluate the extent of convergence in key floral traits across plants in several plant families, (2) test specific hypotheses for the function of buzz pollinated flowers across independent evolutionary origins, and (3) combine analyses of trait and functional convergence to understand the pathways of convergence and evolutionary novelty in plants.

Duties
The PhD student will work with both bumblebees and with recently developed bee-size robotic shakers (robo-buzzers) to explore form and function of buzz pollinated flowers. This is an experimentally focused project that requires skills for working with delicate electronic equipment, careful experimentation, and handling live bees. The student should be willing to learn the use and troubleshooting of electronic and mechanical hardware and corresponding software. Floral characterization will include the use of X-ray micro-computed tomography. Other tasks include growing and caring for plants in the glasshouse and maintaining bumblebee colonies.

The PhD student is also expected to actively participate in the academic activities of our research group (including attending weekly meetings), develop analytical frameworks, prepare manuscripts for publication, and present their work at national and international meetings.

Qualifications required
To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must:

  • Hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in biology, evolutionary biology, plant biology, or electrical engineering or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.
  • Be able to work closely with plants and bees.
  • Be able to handle and effectively use delicate and complex electro-mechanical equipment and associated software.

Candidates must be able to express themselves fully in spoken as well as written English.

Qualifications desired

  • Knowledge of ecological and evolutionary theory
  • Demonstrated capacity to design and troubleshoot experiments
  • Experience of working with technically complex electro-mechanical equipment
  • Knowledge of basic biophysical and biomechanical principles
  • Experience with statistical analyses and associated software (e.g., R, MatLab)
  • Previous experience with plant and bee work
  • Academic writing skills appropriate for their career stage
  • Familiarity with pollination biology
  • Capacity to work as part of a team and contribute to the academic development of more junior members

About the employment
The employment is a temporary position according to the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5 §7. Scope of employment: full-time. Starting date 1 March 2027 or as agreed. Placement: Uppsala.

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines.

  2. your CV, including your education, research experience, and references to publications if applicable,
  3. names and contact details of two referees (email addresses, institution, and phone numbers).

Use of AI when applying:

jobs.title: PhD student in Chemistry with a specialisation in Anodeless Sodium-ion Batteries
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Chemistry - Ångström Laboratory
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Chemistry - Ångström conducts research and education in the chemistry field. The department has more than 270 employees and has a turnover of 300 million SEK. At the department's six programs, we conduct very successful research of a high international standard. We have a large number of externally funded research projects, often with international cooperation and we see continued good growth in our subject area. The department has education assignments in engineering programs and master's programs. More information is available on our website. 

Duties
Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) designed for electric vehicles and grid storage have longstanding sustainability and security-of-supply concerns. Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) address both concerns, but do not currently hold enough energy to replace LIBs in all applications. The most promising strategy to improve the energy density of SIBs is to remove the conventional anode material from SIBs: an “anodeless” cell. However, serious challenges remain to increase lifespan and develop them to commercial viability. The project aims to address these challenges to commercializing next-gen SIBs by focusing on the stability of sodium metal anodes.

The PhD position will involve the development of electrolytes and electrochemical techniques for anodeless sodium-ion batteries. The overarching aim is to develop high energy density sodium-ion batteries that are made from sustainable materials and are free of critical raw materials. The PhD position will be based in Uppsala University, but the candidate will be expected to collaborate closely with industrial actors (Altris AB and Polestar), and the position will involve a 6 month placement in Humboldt University of Berlin to gain expertise in electrochemical dilatometry (to be completed within the 3rd year of the PhD).

The work will involve a combination of fundamental electrochemical evaluation of anodeless SIBs, development and characterization of novel liquid and gel electrolytes, advanced operando techniques (particularly operando microscopy and electrochemical dilatometry) and development of anodeles cells in near-commercial multi-layer pouch cells. Teaching and other departmental duties may be part of the position, to a maximum of 20% of the working hours.

The duties of the PhD candidate will include:

  • Construction and development of anodeless SIBs (single and multi-layer pouch cells).
  • Operando characterisation (optical microscopy and dilatometry) of Na deposition/stripping.
  • Development and characterisation of SIB liquid electrolyte, as well as explorations of gel electrolyte.
  • Development of charge/discharge protocols to improve reversibility of Na deposition/stripping
  • Research visits to Altris (Sweden) and HU Berlin (Germany)

Requirements
To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must

  • been awarded a second-cycle degree in Chemistry, Engineering, Materials Science or equivalent, or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • acquired essentially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

The candidate must have:

  • Very good oral and written proficiency in English.
  • Good organisation and time management skills
  • Experience working within a laboratory environment.
  • Experience with battery materials.

Consideration will also be given to good collaborative skills, drive and independence, and how the applicant’s experience and skills complement and strengthen ongoing research within the department, and how they stand to contribute to its future development.

Additional qualifications
Additionally to the requirements above, it is considered meritous to have:

  • Experience with anodeless or metal-ion batteries.
  • Experience with electrochemical techniques of metal plating/stripping.
  • Experience with electrolyte development for metal-ion batteries.
  • Experience with multi-layer pouch cell assembly and characterisation.
  • Experience with operando characterisation techniques for battery cycling.

For all of the above, experience with sodium-, potassium- or lithium-ion systems is most relevant, but experience with calcium- and magnesium-ion systems are also meritous.

Duties
We are recruiting a PhD student to the Crespi group at the Department of Chemistry - Ångström Laboratory for the Swedish Research Council-funded project “Hemiphosphaindigos: New Gears for Molecular Machines” (2026-04728). The project explores how phosphorus can be used to control light-induced structural changes in organic molecules and to develop new photoswitches and molecular motors.

The PhD student will primarily design and synthesize new phosphorus-containing indigoid chromophores, purify and characterize the products using techniques including NMR and mass spectrometry, and investigate their photochemical properties. Experiments will include UV-Vis spectroscopy, irradiation studies, photostationary-state analysis, quantum-yield measurements and thermal kinetics. A central goal is to connect molecular structure and phosphorus functionalization with isomerization efficiency and stability.

In later stages, the student will contribute to studies of directional molecular motion and the effects of supramolecular confinement on photochemistry. Advanced time-resolved spectroscopy and computational chemistry will be integrated through expertise within the group and international collaborations, with opportunities for training in complementary methods. jobs.title: PhD student in Chemistry – specializing in Molecular Biomimetics
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Chemistry - Ångström Laboratory
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Chemistry - Ångström conducts research and education in the chemistry field. The department has more than 270 employees and has a turnover of 300 million SEK. At the department's five programs, we conduct very successful research of a high international standard. We have a large number of externally funded research projects, often with international cooperation and we see continued good growth in our subject area. The department has education assignments in engineering programs and master's programs. More information is available on our website.

The student will be part of the bioinorganic chemistry group within the molecular biomimetics program. The program is highly recognized internationally with strong visibility and the group is situated in a modern building at the Ångström Laboratory. Strong cross-disciplinary collaborations are characteristic for the program

Project description
The project involves biochemistry and biophysics, with a focus on so-called hydrogenase enzymes. Hydrogenases are redox-active metalloenzymes that catalyze the interconversion of protons and molecular hydrogen, enabling molecular hydrogen metabolism central to microbial energy systems. Recent findings have challenged the prevailing view of [FeFe] hydrogenases as fully reversible catalysts, instead revealing enzymes with strong intrinsic catalytic bias toward either hydrogen uptake or production. This project explores the hypothesis that such enzymes act as “metabolic rectifiers,” supporting unidirectional electron flow with minimal energy loss—an adaptation potentially critical for life near thermodynamic limits.

Duties
The doctoral student will participate in a research project with two main objectives: to establish the prevalence of unidirectional catalysis among hydrogenases by characterising enzymes from different ecological and phylogenetic contexts, and to identify the molecular determinants of catalytic directionality through the rational design and analysis of enzyme variants. Complementary studies will aim to develop kinetic models linking thermodynamic reversibility to catalytic directionality.

The doctoral student's role in the project will primarily involve the isolation and characterisation of novel [FeFe] hydrogenases, as well as the detailed characterisation of selected enzymes using a combination of electrochemistry and spectroscopy (EPR and FTIR spectroscopy) to elucidate their reaction mechanisms. Writing scientific publications will also be an important part of the position. The work will be carried out in collaboration with other specialists at Uppsala University and at other universities in Sweden and abroad.

The main duties of the doctoral student are to devote themselves to their doctoral studies, which include participation in the research project described above and completion of third-cycle courses. Duties may also include teaching and other departmental responsibilities, corresponding to a maximum of 20% of the working time.

Requirements

jobs.title: PhD student in Computational Science with focus on Simulation-based inference and Epidemiological Modeling
jobs.department: Uppsala universitet, Department of Information Technology
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in working with research in Computational Science, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at the Department of Information Technology, Uppsala University.

The Department of Information Technology holds a leading position in both research and education at all levels. We are currently Uppsala University's third largest department, with 350 employees, including 120 teachers and 120 PhD students. Approximately 5,000 undergraduate students take one or more courses at the department each year. You can find more information about us on the Department of Information Technology website.

Project description
The project focuses on the development of computational and data-driven methods for epidemiological modelling and analysis. A central component is the development of stochastic models and Bayesian methods for combining epidemiological models with different types of data, with the aim of enabling reliable estimates and situational awareness. The project offers several possible research directions, including statistical validation and diagnostics for simulation-based inference, the use of neural networks to construct informative prior distributions, and game-theoretic modelling of epidemics and the value of information in decisions concerning public health interventions. The common foundation is computational modelling and Bayesian inference, while the specific research direction can be adapted to the doctoral candidate's background and interests. The project thus offers opportunities to work at the intersection of applied mathematics, statistics, machine learning and computational science, with epidemiological applications providing a common focus.

A more detailed project description is available at: https://stefanengblom.github.io/files/docs/Comput_Modeling_Epidemics.pdf

Duties 
The doctoral student will primarily devote their time to graduate education. Other departmental duties of at most 20%, including teaching and administration, may also be included in the employment.

Requirements 
To meet the general entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must:

  • hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in Computational Science, Enigineering Physics, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Data Science, or a related subject, or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

The University may permit an exemption from the general entry requirements for an individual applicant, if there are special grounds (Chapter 7, § 39 of the Higher Education Ordinance). For special entry requirements, please see the subject’s general study plan.

The successful candidate should have a solid background in mathematical modelling, statistics, computational methods or a closely related area. Experience in scientific programming and the ability to implement and evaluate computational methods are required. Good written and spoken English is also required, as the research and scientific communication will be conducted in English.

The position requires the ability to work independently and take responsibility for one's own research, as well as to collaborate effectively with others. The candidate should have strong analytical and problem-solving skills, a structured approach to work, and the ability to communicate research results clearly.

Additional qualifications
Experience in one or more of the following areas is considered an advantage:

  • Bayesian statistics, statistical inference or simulation-based inference.

  • Machine learning, particularly neural networks and probabilistic machine learning.
  • Sequential Monte Carlo methods, particle filtering or state estimation.

Experience with programming in Matlab, Python, R, C or C++ is beneficial. Previous experience with research software, simulation frameworks or the analysis of real-world data is also an advantage.

In your application and personal letter, please state clearly how your background fulfills the requirements and aligns with the additional qualifications.

jobs.description_html:
Do you want to conduct research on the population ecology of plants? Do you want to join an outstanding academic environment at Uppsala University’s Evolutionary Biology Centre? We are now looking to recruit a PhD student who wishes to begin their research career together with us.

The Department of Ecology and Genetics (IEG) Department of Ecology and Genetics – Uppsala University at the Evolutionary Biology Center (EBC) is an international environment with staff that conducts research to understand ecological and evolutionary processes across all levels of biological organization. IEG provides access to advanced national and local research infrastructures, including free super computing resources (NAISS) and the latest molecular technologies and sequencing platforms (SciLifeLab platforms). IEG hosts a Climate Lab with controlled environmental chambers, greenhouses and a state-of-the-art molecular lab. PhD-students at IEG can join the PhD school which provides ample opportunities for networking on and off campus with PhD-students from the other two biology departments at Uppsala University (The Department of Organismal Biology, and the Department of Cellular and Molecular Biology).

The position is offered by the research program in Plant Ecology and Evolution at IEG. Information about the program’s current research can be found here.

Duties
The PhD project will address central current questions about plant life history and population dynamics, with focus on how demographic parameters (survival and reproduction) are affected by plant ageing and how environmental factors influence the same “vital rates” and thus the dynamics and distribution patterns of populations. The Department of Chemistry for Life Sciences conducts research and education in analytical chemistry, biochemistry and organic chemistry. More than 100 people, including around 45 PhD students, work at the department. New employees and students are recruited from all over the world and English is the main working language. The department is located at the Biomedical Centre in Uppsala, which facilitates collaborations with research groups in biology, pharmacy, medicine and SciLifeLab and gives access to advanced infrastructure for experimental and theoretical studies. You can find more information about us here.

Project description
We are looking for a PhD student in analytical chemistry to develop novel methods for single-cell analysis and quantification using direct infusion mass spectrometry. A key objective is to optimize sampling and ionization probes for sensitive detection of metabolites and lipids from individual cells, enabling studies of cellular heterogeneity. The project will involve custom-built analytical platforms coupled to high-resolution mass spectrometry and span the full workflow, from cell culture and experimental design to data acquisition, molecular annotation, and data processing. The work will also include development of targeted tandem mass spectrometry methods and reactive chemistry strategies for confident analyte identification and quantification.

As a PhD candidate, you will be involved in all aspects of the project and collaborate with interdisciplinary teams in chemistry, biology, medicine, and information technology. You will contribute to the development of innovative analytical methodologies through experimental work and  molecular annotation strategies. The position offers access to state-of-the-art instrumentation and opportunities to develop creative solutions for studying metabolites and lipids in biological systems.

The project is expected to result in internationally competitive research and provides excellent opportunities for pushing the boundaries of analytical chemistry and collaborating with leading researchers across disciplines.

Tasks may include
Independent planning, execution, and analysis of experimental work Method development, optimization, problem solving, and technology development Scientific collaboration within and outside the research group Communication of research results

The position is based in the research group of Prof. Ingela Lanekoff, which develops innovative mass spectrometry methodologies to address fundamental questions in biology and medicine. The group's research focuses on mass spectrometry imaging and single-cell mass spectrometry to reveal chemical processes underlying biological function and dysfunction. The group has secured several major research grants, providing long-term resources, access to cutting-edge instrumentation, and opportunities for international collaborations. jobs.title: PhD student in experimental nuclear physics with a focus on nuclear fission and gamma-ray emission
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Physics and Astronomy
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in working with experimental nuclear physics, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at Uppsala University.

The research conducted at the Department of Physics and Astronomy encompasses a wide range of physics topics, distributed over nine divisions. The department is located in the Ångström laboratory and employs nearly 400 people, 100 of whom are doctoral students. It offers a broad physics curriculum to undergraduate and graduate students, participation in nationally and internationally leading projects for researchers, and opportunities for partnership with industry and various outreach activities. Read more on www.uu.se/physics.

The Department of Physics and Astronomy, Division of Applied Nuclear Physics, at Uppsala University conducts research and education in applied nuclear physics. Its activities aim to deepen our understanding of the properties of atomic nuclei and apply this knowledge in areas such as energy and materials research.

The successful candidate will join an internationally active research group investigating nuclear-reaction dynamics and nuclear fission through experiments and modelling. Our research tests theoretical predictions and addresses fundamental questions relevant to nuclear physics and astrophysics. It also produces high-precision nuclear data for applications in nuclear-energy systems, cancer treatment, and radiation-tolerant microelectronics. The group collaborates with leading research facilities across Europe.

This doctoral project forms part of a Nordic collaboration between Uppsala University and the University of Oslo (UiO), within the Norwegian Nuclear Research Centre (NNRC). It brings together expertise in nuclear fission, nuclear structure, gamma-ray spectroscopy, detector development, and nuclear modelling. A substantial part of the experimental work will take place at the Oslo Cyclotron Laboratory (OCL).


Duties

The doctoral project will ultimately investigate how excitation energy and angular momentum are shared between fission fragments and subsequently carried away by gamma-ray emission. You will measure prompt fission gamma-ray spectra, multiplicities, and total energies as functions of excitation energy, and attempt to extract fission-product yields and isomeric yield ratios. These measurements will test our understanding of nuclear fission and provide data to improve predictions of gamma-ray heating and other fission observables relevant to Generation IV reactors operating with fast neutron spectra.

You will prepare and conduct experiments at OCL in close collaboration with researchers and technical specialists at UiO. The experiments will use the uranium-235(d,pf) reaction as a surrogate for neutron-induced fission of uranium-235. Detecting the outgoing proton together with fission fragments and gamma rays will allow the measured observables to be related to the excitation energy of the fissioning nucleus.

A central part of your work will be centered around the OSCAR gamma-ray detector array, charged-particle detectors, and a newly developed fission chamber. You will contribute to detector characterisation, calibration, commissioning, and optimisation of the experimental setup.

You will analyse the experimental data using coincidence techniques, detector-response corrections, background subtraction, and uncertainty analysis. Characteristic gamma-ray transitions will be used to identify selected fission products, while delayed emission will provide complementary information about fragment angular momentum through isomeric yield ratios.

The project also includes computational fission modelling in close collaboration with the nuclear data section at the International atomic energy agency. Using TALYS and fission models such as FREYA and GEF, you will assess how well current calculations describe energy sharing, angular momentum, and fragment de-excitation. Comparisons with the measurements will help identify model limitations and guide further development.

The position involves extended research visits to Oslo and may include detector tests and experiments at other international facilities. You will present your research in peer-reviewed publications, at scientific conferences, and in collaboration meetings.


Requirements

Applicants must meet the general eligibility requirements for doctoral studies through one of the following:

  • Hold a Master’s degree in physics, engineering physics, nuclear engineering, applied physics, or another subject relevant to the project;
  • or Have completed at least 240 higher education credits, including at least 60 credits at Master’s level and an independent project of at least 15 credits;
  • or Have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge through other studies or professional experience.

The position also requires:

  • An interest in physics, experimental work, data analysis, and physical modelling.
  • The ability to work independently and systematically, with attention to data quality.
  • Good collaboration skills.
  • Good oral and written communication skills in English.
  • Willingness and ability to undertake research visits abroad, particularly to Oslo, and participate in experimental campaigns and scientific conferences.


Additional qualifications

Desired qualifications that will be used in the ranking of the candidates:

  • Good knowledge of physics, including nuclear physics and radiation detection.
  • Programming experience, for example in Python or C++, and an interest in developing your scientific-computing skills.
  • Gamma-ray spectroscopy, coincidence measurements, or nuclear-fission experiments. Radiation detectors, detector electronics, or data-acquisition systems.
  • Experimental data analysis using ROOT or comparable tools.
  • Monte Carlo simulations of radiation transport and detector response, for example using Geant4.
  • Nuclear-reaction or fission calculations using TALYS, FREYA, GEF, or related codes.
  • Statistical analysis, uncertainty propagation, or detector-response unfolding.
  • Scientific computing involving large experimental or simulated datasets.
