Are you interested in exploring the driving processes behind phytoplankton succession in lakes and assessing how phytoplankton will respond to future environmental changes? Are you looking for an employer, who invests in sustainable career development and offers supportive working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD student position at Uppsala University, which will be placed at the Department of Ecology and Genetics within the Limnology program.

The Limnology program is an internationally renowned working environment with staff and students from all over the world. The program engages in research and education on the biogeochemistry and ecology of inland waters, spanning from microscopic to global scale. The program actively promotes a collegial and inclusive research culture through regular social activities, encouraging well-being, creativity, and professional growth.

Project Description
Phytoplankton form an important foundation of lake food webs and their community composition changes markedly throughout the year in response to physical and chemical changes as well as predation pressures. These changes are in turn moderated by different functional traits between groups, which determine how they respond to environmental conditions. Using models, we can study how environmental changes (such as climate warming, eutrophication, and extreme weather events) influence successional patterns in phytoplankton and identify conditions that create windows of opportunity for specific functional groups. We can then use these models to assess potential future changes. We are seeking a highly-motivated PhD student who is keen to use process-based biogeochemical models to investigate these dynamics. The outcomes of this work will improve our ability to forecast changes in phytoplankton communities, with direct application to lake ecosystem functioning and drinking water provisioning. The position is based at Uppsala University’s Department of Ecology and Genetics, within the Limnology program.

Duties
Your duties will have a strong focus on data handling and process-based, dynamical modelling, but also include teaching, course work, and collaborating in research teams.

Requirements

  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

Candidates who have not yet completed their degree but are expected to meet the degree requirements before the start date are encouraged to apply.

This work lies in the intersection of physics, biogeochemistry, and ecology, and has a strong numerical emphasis. Eligible candidates need to demonstrate skills with advanced numerical approaches (e.g. modelling, statistics, or large-scale data analysis). Are you interested in working in formal verification and programming language techniques applied to quantum systems, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in a sustainable working environment and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at the Department of Information Technology, Uppsala University. 

The Department of Information Technology holds a leading position in both research and education at all levels. We are currently Uppsala University's third largest department, with 350 employees, including 120 teachers and 120 PhD students. Approximately 5,000 undergraduate students take one or more courses at the department each year. You can find more information about us on the Department of Information Technology website.

The position is hosted in a research environment which includes verification experts (Parosh Abdulla, Mohammed Faouzi Atig, Bengt Jonsson, Philipp Ruemmer, Kostis Sagonas, Wang Yi), as well as experts in programming languages (Johannes Borgström, Eva Darulova, Lars-Henrik Erikson, Sofia Ouhbi, Tjark Weber, Tobias Wrigstad). The department is known for both strong theoretical work as well as tool development in these areas (UPPAAL, Concuerror, Nidhugg and other tools), publishing in top conferences such as POPL, PLDI, ICALP and CAV. 

Project description
As both private and public investment in quantum computing continues to surge, the steady upscaling of quantum hardware (now reaching thousands of qubits) has resulted in increasingly sophisticated quantum software pipelines. Given the strategic use of quantum software (e.g. in security), there is an urgent need for verifying the trustworthiness of quantum programs at scale. Features of modern quantum programs such as Quantum Error Correction lead to hybrid quantum-classical architectures, resulting in new challenges for verification. Current tools and techniques do not offer the desired combination of scalability, automation and guarantees to verify such programs. The project aims to address this gap by combining techniques from classical verification and programming language theory with those for complex arithmetic, in order to contribute both theoretical insights and software artifacts advancing the state of the art in quantum program verification.

Duties 
The doctoral student will primarily devote their time to doctoral education. Other departmental duties of at most 20%, including teaching and administration, may also be included in the employment.

Requirements 
To meet the general entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must:

  • hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in computer science or mathematics or a related field, or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

The University may permit an exemption from the general entry requirements for an individual applicant, if there are special grounds (Chapter 7, § 39 of the Higher Education Ordinance). For special entry requirements, please see the subject’s general study plan.

We are looking for candidates with:

  • a mathematical background,
  • excellent problem-solving skills,
  • high motivation and capacity to persistently work on difficult problems,
  • interest in programming,
  • good communication skills with sufficient proficiency in oral and written English,
  • ability to work both independently and collaboratively.

Additional qualifications 
Experience or coursework in one or more of the following areas is considered an advantage: formal methods, programming language theory or semantics, logic, automata theory, automated theorem proving, and quantum computing.

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines.

Application
The application must include:

  1. A statement (max 2 pages) describing the applicant’s motivation, research interests, a concise summary of their Master’s thesis (or comparable project), and the earliest possible starting date; contact information for at least one reference (no reference letter required at this stage).
  2. A CV.
  3. Degrees and transcripts with grades (officially translated to English or Swedish).
  4. The Master’s thesis (or draft), publications, and other relevant self-produced reports.

Promising applicants will be invited for interviews before a hiring decision is made.

About the employment
The employment is a temporary position according to the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5 § 7. Scope of employment: 100%. Starting date 15 January 2027 or as agreed. Placement: Uppsala

For further information about the position, please contact: Assistant Professor Ramanathan Thinniyam Srinivasan, email: ramanathan.s.thinniyam@it.uu.se 

Please submit your application by 15 November 2026, UFV-PA 2026/2571.

jobs.title: PhD student in Chemical Physics: Development of Quantum Chemical Calculations of X-ray Spectra in Condensed Phase
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Physics is located in the AlbaNova University Center and has approximately 230 employees, 250 students at undergraduate level and 80 graduate students. There are four research subjects within the postgraduate program: Physics, Theoretical Physics, Chemical Physics and Medical Radiation Physics. These subjects span over several research groups with different research activities. For information about the Department of Physics, see: www.fysik.su.se/english.

Project description

Subject: Chemical Physics

The theoretical description of X-ray induced electronic transitions in liquid solutions and solid materials is complicated by the strong influence of the environment and the dynamical response for core-excitations. Recently the development in high-resolution spectroscopy, in particular resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS), allows for detailed investigations of molecular interactions and electron-correlation. However, X-ray spectroscopy in condensed phase requires improvements in theoretical modelling for reliable interpretation of the experimental data. Depending on background and interests, you will primarily develop accurate methods either for treatment of X-ray induced transitions in extended systems using advanced embedding techniques or for the treatment of low energy excitation phonons and vibration.

You will work in a European collaboration involving theoretical and experimental groups, and be involved also in experiments. The project ”Theory Development for High-Resolution RIXS Experiments on Liquid Solutions and Solid Materials” is a collaboration with Prof. Marcella Iannuzzi (University of Zurich) and is financed by the Swiss National Science Foundation. Partner organisations include Dr. Teodoro Laino (IBM Research), Prof. Thorsten Schmitt (Paul Scherrer Institut), and Prof. Lothar Weinhardt (Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, KIT Light Source).

We seek a motivated and creative candidate with a strong collaborative mindset eager to learn new skills. The position offers opportunities for international collaborations and participation in international conferences. You will be supported in developing your science communication skills. You will develop an understanding in quantum chemistry and simulation techniques to accurately model photo-induced processes. You will work in the division of Chemical Physics at the Department of Physics, in which the research spans over a wide range of experimental and theoretical projects. The research interests in the Molecular Dynamics Quantum Chemistry group range from accurate quantum mechanical studies of molecules to realistic simulations of electrolyte solutions and energy materials. Atomic, Molecular and Complex Quantum System Physics is one of the leading research areas at Stockholm University and also an area at the Faculty of Science that have been selected to profile the University.

Preliminary start date Jan/Feb 2027. This and other positions in the project are also announced at https://www.cp2k.org/positions under the heading "Four Doctoral Positions in RIXS Theory and Experiment". For more information about the research group, see: www.su.se/english/profiles/odelius

Qualification requirements

In order to be admitted to postgraduate education, the applicant must have the general and specific entry requirements. The qualification requirements must be met by the deadline for applications.

You meet general entry requirements if you have completed a second-cycle degree, or completed courses equivalent to at least 240 higher education credits, of which 60 credits must be in the second cycle, or have otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere.

Specific entry requirements. In order to be accepted as a PhD student in Physics or Theoretical Physics a BSc in Physics (or equivalent) is required. The studies must include 60 credits of second-cycle courses in physics out of which at least 15 credits correspond to a second-cycle degree project. The degree project does not have to have been examined at the application deadline, but work corresponding to half a semester of full-time studies should have been devoted to it. For the subject Chemical Physics courses in chemistry may replace the required physics courses. The subject Medical Radiation Physics requires a second-cycle degree project of 30 credits in the subject area, or with 60 credits of physics, a second-cycle degree project of 30 credits in another subject area.

In addition, proficiency in English language, equivalent to English B in Swedish high school, is required, or

  • Previously completed University degree taught in English
  • IELTS score (Academic) of 6.0 or more (with none of the sections scoring less than 5.0)
  • TOEFL score of 550 or more (computer based test 213, internet based 79)
  • Cambridge/Oxford - Advanced or Proficiency level

Selection

The selection among the eligible candidates will be based on their capacity to benefit from the training. The following criteria will be used to assess this capacity:

  • documented knowledge in a relevant field of research
  • capacity for analytical and creative thinking
  • initiative
  • independence
  • ability to collaborate
  • written and oral proficiency

Admission Regulations for Doctoral Studies at Stockholm University.

About the employment

We offer a fixed-term employment as a doctoral student according to Chapter 5 of the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100). The period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for four years. As a doctoral student, you should primarily devote yourself to your own doctoral education, but the employment may include work with education, research and administration to a limited extent (maximum 20 %).

A new employment as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, the employment is then renewed for a maximum of two years at a time.

Stockholm University strives to be a workplace free from discrimination and with equal opportunities for all.

Contact

For more information about the project, please contact Prof. Michael Odelius, odelius@fysik.su.se, and Assoc. Prof. Markus Kowalewski, kowalewski@fysik.su.se.

For information about the employment, please contact Prof. Michael Odelius, odelius@fysik.su.se, who can also forward questions to the PhD student council at Fysikum.

Application

Apply for the PhD student position at Stockholm University's recruitment system. Attach a personal letter and CV as well as the attachments requested in the application form. It is the responsibility of the applicant to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the job advertisement, and that it is submitted before the deadline.

The instructions for applicants are available at: How to apply for a position.

jobs.title: Doktorand i pedagogik
jobs.department: Mittuniversitetet, Institutionen för pedagogik, psykologi och socialt arbete
jobs.description_html:
Pedagogik är ett akademiskt ämne som undersöker olika former av systematiska påverkansprocesser som exempelvis fostran, ledarskap, lärande, undervisning och utbildning på individuell nivå, inom grupper och på en samhällelig nivå. Detta studeras inom olika organisationer och kontexter, exempelvis inom det formella utbildningssystemet eller inom arbetslivet och ur ett livslångt lärandeperspektiv. Vid Mittuniversitetet har pedagogikämnet utbildning och forskning kopplat till lärarutbildningen och till det beteendevetenskapliga programmet. Forskningen är organiserad i fyra forskargrupper: Didaktik, Inkludering och Mångfald (DIM), Higher Education and E-Learning (HEEL), Kritiska perspektiv i Utbildningsforskning (KUF) och Leadership in Education Administration and Development (LEAD). 

Vi söker en doktorand med fokus på högre utbildning och livslångt lärande i arbetslivet och de förutsättningar som råder vid pedagogiska processer som exempelvis organisationsutveckling, kompetensutveckling och lärande i arbetslivet. Av speciellt intresse är ett högskolepedagogiskt perspektiv på livslångt lärande och den roll som högre utbildning och aktuell samhällsutveckling spelar för att stödja arbetslivets pedagogik. I den utlysta tjänsten kommer du att i samarbete med dina handledare – erfarna forskare inom tjänstens tema – bidra till att utforska detta område.

 

Arbetsuppgifter
Forskarutbildning i ämnet pedagogik innefattande initialt 100 % forskning. I ett senare skede av utbildningen kan undervisning och administrativt arbete ingå upp till 20%.

 

Behörighet
Grundläggande behörighet har den som avlagt en examen på avancerad nivå eller fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå eller på något annat sätt inom eller utom landet förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper. Särskild behörighet har den som har grundläggande behörighet varav minst 90 högskolepoäng i pedagogik på grundnivå inkluderande ett självständigt arbete om 15 högskolepoäng samt minst 30 högskolepoäng i pedagogik på avancerad nivå inkluderande ett självständigt arbete om 15 högskolepoäng, eller på något annat sätt inom eller utom landet har förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.

 

Övriga krav 
Vi söker en person som trivs med att hantera intellektuella utmaningar. Vidare har du en god förmåga att samarbeta och kommunicera. Du är intresserad av att skapa professionella relationer och nätverk med andra forskare och det omgivande samhället, både nationellt och internationellt. Du är även flexibel och bekväm i att hantera krav och motgångar i ditt arbete.

 

Bedömningsgrunder
Vi kommer att värdera följande bedömningsgrunder vid anställningen:

  • God förmåga att tillgodogöra sig utbildning på forskarnivå.
  • Dokumenterad god förmåga att självständigt planera och organisera arbetet.
  • Dokumenterad god samarbetsförmåga och förmåga att skapa relationer och nätverk.
  • God förmåga att uttrycka sig i tal och skrift på såväl svenska som engelska.
  • God förmåga att hantera för anställningen särskilda krav.                  

Övriga meriter som är relevanta för den utlysta tjänsten är en allmänpedagogisk utbildning på grundläggande och avancerad nivå och ett dokumenterat intresse för högskolepedagogik, livslångt lärande, arbetslivets pedagogik och utveckling av pedagogiska processer i arbetslivet. 

 

Handläggning
Beredningen av anställningen följer de former som anges i högskoleförordningens 5 kap och fortgår i enlighet med Mittuniversitetets anställningsordning. 

 

Anställning och tillträde 
Doktorsexamen, 100 % egen forskarutbildning.

Doktorandanställningen avser en anställning som motsvarar fyra års heltidsstudier och beräknas leda fram till en doktorsexamen. Om studietakten i forskarutbildningen förändras ändras anställningstiden i motsvarande omfattning.

En ny anställning som doktorand gäller för högst ett år, anställningen får därefter förnyas med högst två år i taget. Bestämmelser gällande anställning som doktorand finns i Högskoleförordningen (1993:100), 5 kap 1-7 §§. 

Tillträde 2027-04-01 eller enligt överenskommelse.

 

Anställningsort: Sundsvall

Lön: Enligt Mittuniversitetets lönetrappa för doktorander.  

 

Information
Närmare upplysningar lämnas av ämnesföreträdare professor Jimmy Jaldemark jimmy.jaldemark@miun.se eller 010-142 82 88 samt av prefekt Ulrika Danielsson, ulrika.danielsson@ miun.se. 

 

Ansökan
Ansökningshandlingar ska vara på svenska eller engelska. 

Till din ansökan ska följande dokument bifogas:

  • Personligt brev
  • CV
  • Intyg/betyg och övriga styrkta merithandlingar du som sökande vill åberopa
  • Intressebeskrivning där du redogör för ditt forskningsintresse inom den angivna inriktningen för den utlysta tjänsten, samt dina förväntningar på forskarutbildningen.
  • Examensarbete på avancerad nivå eller magister-/masterarbete.

 

Välkommen med din ansökan via vårt rekryteringssystem senast 2026-12-15.

jobs.title: Doctoral Student in Psychology
jobs.department: Department of Psychology and Social work
jobs.description_html:
Job description
The research project is at the intersection of social psychology and sociolinguistics, examining how accents function as social signals. The focus is on social perception, attitudes, emotions, and behaviours related to foreign accents.

The research addresses questions of stereotypes, discrimination, and social inclusion from a Swedish and international perspective, with a consistent gender perspective throughout. The project is interdisciplinary and connects to work and organisational psychology, political science, gender studies, and research on integration and belonging.

Methodologically, the project is primarily based on experimental studies and psychometric approaches, with the possibility of applying neuroscientific methods as well.

The position is within the Department of Psychology, which is characterised by a close and personal environment with strong collegial support. The doctoral student will be part of an interdisciplinary and internationally oriented research environment and will work in close collaboration with supervisors, with considerable emphasis on developing independence in planning, implementation, and scientific communication. In the later stages of the dissertation, the doctoral student may have the possibility to design their own sub-study within the project's overarching themes.

The position involves doctoral studies, comprising research (80%) and teaching and administrative work (20%). The primary duties consist of conducting supervised research leading to a doctoral dissertation. The position also includes completing 60 higher education credits in doctoral courses, as well as participating in seminars and other activities within the subject area and the department. 

 

Entry requirements
General entry requirements include a second-cycle level qualification, or fulfilment of courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits must be at second-cycle level, or the equivalent knowledge gained in some other way in Sweden or abroad. Specific entry requirements include at least 90 credits in the subject of psychology or the equivalent knowledge gained in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

 

Other Requirements
Strong English skills, both spoken and written, are required. Good knowledge of Swedish or another Scandinavian language (Norwegian or Danish) is an asset.

The applicant must be driven and independent, analytical, initiative-taking, collaborative, development-oriented, and persistent.

Higher education at the advanced level in psychology, as well as prior experience in the project's research area, are assets for the position. Experience in developing or validating psychometric tools, working with EEG/ERP or other neuroscientific methods, and knowledge of tools such as R, MATLAB, or Python are also considered assets. A scientific publication or manuscript in progress may be considered an asset, particularly if it relates to the project's research area.

 

Assessment criteria
Selection among eligible applicants is made on the basis of an overall assessment of the applicant's ability to successfully complete a doctoral education. The assessment will place particular emphasis on the scientific quality of independent degree projects, the project plan submitted with the application, the applicant's personal qualities, and the applicant’s understanding of and interest in the project's research area.

 

Employment process
Processing of the appointment will comply with the provisions in Chapter 5 of the Higher Education Ordinance (Högskoleförordningen, SFS 1993:100) and will be carried out in accordance with Mid Sweden University’s Employment Procedures.

 

Terms of employment 
The doctoral position corresponds to five years of employment and is expected to lead to a doctoral degree. In addition to doctoral studies, which comprise 80% of the full-time position, teaching and administrative work will make up the remaining 20%, making it equivalent to a full-time post. If the pace of study in doctoral education changes, the employment period will be adjusted accordingly.

Initial doctoral student positions are valid for a maximum of one year, after which the position may be renewed by no longer than two years at a time. Provisions regarding doctoral studentship employment can be found in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), Chapter 5, Sections 1-7. 

Start date: 2027-01-15 or as agreed

Place of employment: Östersund

Salary: In accordance with Mid Sweden University’s salary scale for doctoral student.

 

Information
For more information, contact the Head of department, Ulrika Danielsson, ulrika.danielsson@miun.se or 010-142 84 90, or the Project leader, Marie-France Champoux-Larsson, marila@miun.se or 010-142 85 38.

 

Application
Application documents must be submitted in Swedish or English.

A cover letter, CV, proof of completed degrees, undergraduate and advanced level theses, a project plan, and any scientific publication/manuscript in progress should be attached to the application.

The project plan (approx. 2 – 3 single-spaced pages excluding references) should present a possible research project within the scope of the position’s research area and must include a background to the research area, one or more research questions, a description of methods and research design, and a brief discussion of the project's relevance to the position. The project plan does not need to correspond to the final dissertation project, but is intended to give the applicant the opportunity to demonstrate their ability for scientific reasoning, research design, and critical thinking.

Qualifications cited in the application must be substantiated.

Please submit your application through our recruitment system no later than 2026-11-22.

jobs.title: VDSP - PhD Completion Contract
jobs.description_html:
Job description:

At the University of Vienna more than 10,000 personalities work together towards answering the big questions of the future. Around 7,500 of them do research and teaching, around 2,900 work in administration and organisation. We are looking for a/an

VDSP - PhD Completion Contract

51 Faculty of Physics
Working hours: 30 | Collective bargaining agreement: §48 VwGr. B1 Grundstufe (praedoc)

Reference no.: 6367

The Vienna Doctoral School in Physics is home to 180 doctoral candidates in Physics at the University of Vienna who work at the forefront of science and receive training, mentoring and support to become independent researchers and to connect with the scientific community.

Your personal sphere of influence:

The Vienna Doctoral School in Physics offers up to nine 3-months PhD Completion Contracts for fellows of the Doctoral School who have held a position as University Assistant (praedoc) or as PhD project staff at the University of Vienna before. These Completion Contracts aim to support highly qualified fellows in the final phase of their doctoral studies. The recipients will be employed as University Assistants (praedoc) and will work at the Faculty of Physics. The start of the contracts is possible from 01 January 2027 onwards - the Fellowship must be completed within the year 2027.

Your future tasks:

  • You actively participate in research, teaching & administration at the Faculty of Physics.
  • Your main task is to complete and to submit your dissertation.
  • You meet and consult with your supervisor(s) on a regular basis in order to prioritize your tasks and get the necessary support to complete your dissertation successfully in time.
  • You actively seek support (workshops, training, coaching etc.) if necessary.
  • You contribute to the organizational and administrative tasks of the Faculty of Physics e.g. supervision of students, organization of courses and holding examinations in accordance with the assignment.

This is part of your personality:

Eligibility Criteria:

  • Actively enrolled to PhD studies in Physics at the University of Vienna.
  • Full member of the VDSP who has followed all PHD curricular requirements as well as all regular VDSP requirements:
    • Positively completed PhD presentation “FÖP”.
    • Signed doctoral thesis agreement.
    • All required annual progress reports BSP/V02E (formlerly called DZ/V02) and VDSP reports submitted.
    • All compulsory coursework successfully completed.
    • Participated in all required VDSP mentor meetings (at least once per year).
  • Commitment to complete your doctoral studies within the anticipated time (within 3 months).
  • Excellent academic record.

What we offer:

We offer you the unique opportunity to complete your scientific education and early career research training with your written PhD thesis in a focused effort that allows you to succeed.

The monthly gross salary for 40 hours/week for VwGr. B1 Grundstufe (prae doc) is € 3.836,10. Please note that the advertised Completion Fellowships are for 30 hours/week VwGr. B1 (prae doc), with relevant work experience determining the assignment to a particular salary grade. 

It is that easy to apply:

The following information need to be submitted as one single pdf-file up until 16 November 2026 via the VDSP webform:

  • Transcript of your study records (Bachelor, Master and PhD)
  • Curriculum vitae including full list of publications and conference contributions
  • Timeline for the completion of your doctorate
  • Table of contents of your written thesis
  • Short description of the structure of the thesis (3-5 pages)
  • Statement with key information (no length requirement – you have to convince the Selection Committee that you are able to complete your written thesis soon):
    • Duration of previous/current PhD contract(s) at the University of Vienna and type of contract(s) e.g. prae-doc or project staff
    • Teaching duties
    • why the original time plan needs to be extended (e.g. personal circumstances, care duties, problems with lab equipment, COVID-related issues, etc.)

The VDSP office will forward your application to your supervisor(s) and ask for a declaration of support. This information will not be shared with the applicants. All applications and statements of support will be brought before the VDSP Selection Committee, which will convene shortly after the deadline.

Important:

  • Eligibility: VDSP students who have been employed by the University of Vienna as University Assistant or Project Staff Member within six months before the start of the completion contract.
  • Relevant work experience determining the assignment to a particular salary grade.
  • Your existing work contract will be extended for up to three months.
  • Successful applicants are employed at the University of Vienna and are therefore subject to all associated rights and obligations.
  • The successive contract regulations must be followed/kept in mind. Make sure to check your individual case in consideration of your career planning. In case of questions contact HR to clarify your situation.

If you have any content questions, please contact:

VDSP Office

jobs.description_html:
Job description:

The University of Vienna is a community of almost 11,000 individuals, including approximately 7,700 academic staff members, who passionately pursue answers to the profound questions that shape our future. They represent individuals driven by curiosity and a relentless pursuit of excellence. With us, they find the space to try things out and unfold their potential. Are you inspired by their passion and determination? We are currently offering a

PhD position on Arctic energy budget diagnostics at VINAR

53 Faculty of Earth Sciences, Geography and Astronomy
Startdate: 01.12.2026 | Working hours: 30 | Collective bargaining agreement: §48 VwGr. B1 Grundstufe (praedoc)

Reference no.: 6313

Explore and teach at the University of Vienna, where more than 7,700 academics thrive on curiosity in continuous exploration and help us better understand our world. Does this sound like you? Then join our accomplished team!

Your personal sphere of influence:

The research group “Climate Diagnostics”, led by Prof. Leopold Haimberger and Dr. Michael Mayer, is part of the Department of Meteorology and Geophysics. The group is known for its work in coupled atmosphere-ocean-cryosphere energy budget diagnostics as well as in monitoring the homogeneity of input datasets for climate reanalyses.


To learn more about our team, we invite you to visit our website: https://imgw.univie.ac.at/forschung/


We seek a highly motivated candidate to pursue their doctoral thesis on detailed energy and moisture budget diagnostics to trace the sources of major precipitation events at Greenland peripheral glaciers. The thesis should look, however, also at larger scales, since we have reason to believe that the Arctic energy imbalance has been increasing over recent decades, beyond the current estimates provided by climate models. Through this analysis, you will develop advanced diagnostics for verifying modelled energy budget components to novel references at various scales.


Funding for a PhD candidate are available from the Vienna International Network for Atmospheric Research (VINAR). 

Your future tasks:

Active participation in achieving the project goals, which means you will:

  • Evaluate local glacier mass balances at high latitude peripheral glaciers, e.g. Zackenberg, with the possibility to take part in a field trip.
  • Enhance the mass budget modelling using state of the art interpolation tools, e.g. diffusion models
  • Trace the energy and water sources that lead to temporarily positive mass budgets at those glaciers, using Eulerian and Lagrangian diagnostics.
  • Study the evolution of surface energy budgets over Arctic areas in general-> permafrost thawing, ice melt
  • Teach classes within our bachelor or master programs in Meteorology (independently / within the scope of the provisions of the collective bargaining agreement)
  • Become an active member of the Vienna International School of Earth and Space Sciences (VISESS / doctoral school).

This is part of your personality:

  • Completed master or diploma in the atmospheric sciences (e.g., meteorology, climatology), or a related field;
  • Programming and data analysis experience;
  • A good team spirit and willingness to collaborate
  • Strong English communication skills.

These skills would be an advantage:

  • Experience with data assimilation, nonuniform model grids;
  • Expert knowledge of programming, preferably in Python and/or Fortran.
  • Mountaineer/glacier experience

What we offer:

Some flexibility with regard to choosing the exact topic of your doctoral thesis: The position is devoted to Arctic research, but the exact topic will be defined either before you join us, or in the first month of your employment, based on discussions with the working group.

Inspiring and supportive working atmosphere:You will be part of an international team in a healthy and fair working environment with excellent research infrastructure. You will not perform your work in isolation but collaborate with a strong research team.

Fair salary plus health care and social benefits: The gross monthly salary of at least EUR EUR 3.776,10 (on a full-time basis, payable 14 times per year, amount as of 01.01.2026) allows for a comfortable life in a vibrant city with affordable housing prices and quick access to the outdoors.

Work-life balance: You have flexible working hours and the option to partly work remotely (within Austria) upon agreement.

Training and coaching: We offer you the opportunity to develop your skills on an ongoing basis.

Enrollment in the VISESS doctoral school, with benefits described here: https://visess.univie.ac.at/phdprogramme/ 

Good public transport connections: Your workplace is easily accessible by public transport.

Get off to a great start in your new job: the Welcome Compass helps you settle into your new role at the University of Vienna and life in Vienna.

Equal opportunities for all: We welcome every additional/new personality to the team!

The University of Vienna aims to become carbon neutral by 2030: We fully support low-carbon options for travelling. 


The employment duration at this University assistant predoctoral position is 4 years. Initially limited to 1.5 years, the employment relationship is automatically extended to 4 years if the employer does not terminate it within the first 12 months by submitting a non-extension declaration.

jobs.description_html: The Department of Computer Science (Dialog Systems and Machine Learning) at Heinrich Heine University Dusseldorf is seeking a PhD Student in Natural Language Processing (m/w/d) Job-ID: J000000684 Working hours: Full time Location: Düsseldorf Start date: 01.01.2027 Limited until: 31.12.2027 Payment group: EGr. 13 TV-L Organization: Mathematisch-Naturwissen­schaftliche Fakultät Job Category: science / research / teach Apply till: 02.12.2026 The Dialogue Systems and Machine Learning group at Heinrich Heine University investigates fundamental questions in human–computer interaction, at the intersection of Natural Language Processing and Machine Learning. Our research focuses on building intelligent dialogue systems that can learn, reason, adapt, and interact effectively with humans in dynamic and uncertain environments. We develop principled methods for dialogue modelling, representation learning, reinforcement learning, knowledge acquisition, and user simulation. Our mission is to advance the foundations of machine intelligence towards dialogue systems that are adaptive, trustworthy, and genuinely useful to people. Main tasks The goal of Prof. Milica Gasic' DFG project “Curriculum learning in natural language generation” is to develop a deeper understanding of how and why hallucinations arise in neural natural language generation models. Rather than treating hallucinations solely as an undesirable property of the final output, we investigate them as a phenomenon emerging from the interaction between data, learning objectives, representations, and the mechanisms by which models acquire and use knowledge. A central goal is to identify the conditions under which hallucinations emerge and, ultimately, develop principled approaches for reducing their magnitude and severity. The project will investigate learning mechanisms underlying reliable language generation, with particular emphasis on curriculum learning and learning from feedback, exploring approaches such as inverse reinforcement learning and their connection to Theory of Mind. Your Profile The candidate must hold or be close to obtaining a master’s degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, Computational Linguistics or a related field. The master’s thesis must have been submitted by the time of application. Some exposure to Natural Language Processing or Machine Learning is desirable. Excellent programming skills are essential. The candidate should be fluent in English with good writing skills. Knowledge of German is not required, but a willingness to learn German is desirable. Our Offer The position comes with a salary representative in academia (EG 13 TV-L, starting at € 4,759.37; classification depends on prior professional experience). The position is initially a one-year fixed-term contract, with the option of extension based on satisfactory performance. There will be no teaching duties in the first year. It is a qualification position in the sense of the Act of Academic Fixed-Term Contract (Wissenschaftsvertragsgesetz-WissZeitVG), which is to promote the scientific qualification of the employee. The start date is negotiable, but the preferred start would be on 1st January 2027. Do you want to conduct basic research that can inform solutions for sustainable agriculture? Join our group (EDGE) at the University of Vienna as a PhD student within the MSCA Doctoral Network Agripolys and apply environmental analytical chemistry to investigate the enzymatic degradation of polymers in agricultural soils. 

Your personal sphere of influence:

Polymers are important for numerous agricultural applications. To avoid the accumulation of polymers in soils and other environmental systems, soil biodegradability is a key desired feature for many polymers. To inform the development of soil biodegradable polymers, a fundamental understanding of the activity and specificity of soil enzymes is needed. Rooted in environmental analytical chemistry (centered around high-resolution mass spectrometry), this project (Agripolys DC6) aims to decipher biodegradation pathways of several promising polymer classes and thereby shine light on the degradation potential of soil enzymes.

Our research group is part of the Centre for Microbiology and Environmental Systems Science (CeMESS) at the University of Vienna, Austria. We are dedicated to conducting cutting-edge research at the intersection of (bio)chemistry, microbiology, and environmental science.

jobs.institution: Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA)
jobs.description_html:
About

The Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) is looking for highly qualified candidates with Bachelor’s or Master’s degrees to apply for our PhD program. We offer fully funded PhD positions in Astronomy, Biology, Computer Science, Chemistry & Materials, Data Science & Scientific Computing, Earth Science, Mathematics, Neuroscience, and Physics in a world-class research environment on the outskirts of Vienna.

 n 2019, ISTA was ranked #3 in the world-wide Nature Index ranking (normalized). In 2018, ISTA was ranked within the top ten of Nature Index Rising Stars “Top 30 academic institutions under 30” list.

All students are offered 5-year contracts, they receive internationally competitive salaries, and full social security coverage. 

The application deadline is January 8, 2027 (15:00 CET) for a PhD program start date in September 2027.

APPLY NOW

Your tasks

-----------------------------------------------

Join our Virtual Student Open Day on November 18th!
 

The Virtual Student Open Day is a great opportunity to explore our programs and campus virtually, wherever you are located. The program includes a range of live sessions from the Graduate School Office, academics, and students.

You can find out about our PhD program, the ISTA research experience, support services, the ISTA campus and much more by attending one of the talks.

-----------------------------------------------

International and Diverse Scientific Community
Our scientists, from professors to postdocs to students, hail from all corners of the world, representing over 80 different nationalities, and build on research and degrees earned from the finest global scientific institutes and universities.

English-Speaking
We use English throughout the Institute as the language of instruction and communication.

Interdisciplinary
 Our Graduate Program is characterized by modern comprehensive training with a special interdisciplinary focus.

Cutting-Edge Research Training
Students work closely with outstanding faculty within small research groups and have access to first-rate facilities. Students spend the first year completing coursework and rotations before affiliating with a group.

This first phase of exploration allows students to ensure that the research topic, as well as the research group, are the best match for them before embarking on in-depth thesis research in the second phase.

Entry with a Bachelor's or Master's Degree
We welcome students with a Bachelor’s or a Master’s in science to apply for our PhD program.

Funding
All PhD students are offered 5-year contracts. All students making reasonable progress are fully funded until the time of their thesis defense.

ISTA relies on diverse funding sources to support all its researchers. Our Grant Office supports ISTA scientists who would like to apply for external funding. Students also receive financial support to attend scientific conferences and workshops.

Careers
Our distinguished alumni have gone on to successful careers after their PhD studies at ISTA.

PhD students receive support through our mentorship and career development programs which focus on training in transferable skills for academia and beyond. Throughout their studies, PhD students are supported by Career Services, which provide career development advice and training.

We also provide xista, an in-house science venture that supports researchers in the commercial development and use of their research results.

-----------------------------------------------

Your profile

Skills/Qualifications

ISTA welcomes students with different academic backgrounds who can bring their skills and experiences to the scientific setting.

Students with a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Astronomy, Biology, Computer Science, Chemistry & Materials, Data Science & Scientific Computing, Earth Science, Mathematics, Neuroscience, and Physics are encouraged to apply.

 

Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion

ISTA cherishes diversity in personalities, backgrounds, experiences and thoughts among all our employees. Diversity creates a workplace that enables employees to gain new ideas and insights and that will take science into exciting new directions.  

ISTA is committed to equal opportunities and social equity, regardless of age, gender (identity), ethnicity, race, social/cultural background, creed, religion, sexual orientation, and physical/cognitive abilities. Please see our Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion web page for more information. 

 

WHAT ARE THE SELECTION CRITERIA?

The selection committee uses a collection of indicators to evaluate the applicant’s preparedness, motivation, and potential. The following will be considered:

Scientific Promise:

  • Undergraduate performance: overall, with a special focus on relevant field-specific courses
  • Reference letters provided by professors and senior scientists: one letter from industry is acceptable, but letters from an academic background are given priority. Referees are asked to address analytical capabilities, technical proficiency, ability to work independently and motivation/commitment
  • Statement of purpose: the applicant’s past research experience and motivation for applying to this particular PhD program: is it a good academic fit? Does the program contribute to the candidate’s future career plans?, etc.
  • Additional relevant skills (field-specific): demonstrated by internships and/or participation in research projects, participation in science Olympiads, programming languages, lab 

Your benefits

Background:

Quality of the undergraduate background
Transferable skills: communication skills, experience with working in teams, previous mobility and international experiences, leadership experience as demonstrated in student organizations, etc.
Diversity: e.g. a woman in computer science/math/physics; an applicant who switched fields, etc.
ISTA processes applications for its PhD program once a year. To apply, you have to create an online account, which will allow you to track your application through its various stages. 

Your application

WHAT APPLICATION MATERIALS ARE REQUIRED?

We ask you to upload the following documents to the application portal:

  • CV
  • Statement of purpose that explains your research experience and your motivation for applying to the ISTA PhD program. It should be 1-2 pages maximum. In your statement, specify up to three research groups you find the most interesting. At this stage you do not need to contact potential supervisors.
  • University transcripts and diplomas of all degree programs and all years you have attended and/or are currently enrolled in (in English and in original language).
  • Contact information of 3 referees
    All documents must be submitted in English. Copies of university transcripts must be in both English and in their original language.
  • The application deadline is January 8, 2027 (15:00 CET).

Chemical conversion coatings are one of the most effective and commercially successful ways to do this. They protect the metal and help paint adhere to it. At the Department of Electrochemistry and Big Data, we run a robotic high-throughput testing platform combined with machine learning for AI-assisted discoveries. We are offering a 3-year position, as soon as possible, as a PhD student in the quickly developing field of high-throughput and robotic experimentation in materials science. jobs.institution: DIW Berlin - Deutsches Institut für Wirtschaftsforschung e.V.
jobs.description_html:
The DIW Graduate Center (GC) at the German Institute for Economic Research welcomes applications from highly qualified students from around the world to enroll in its structured doctoral program in Economics.

The goal of the DIW Graduate Center is to provide outstanding doctoral students with a research environment and a training structure that will allow their talents to fully develop. The program equips them with a deep understanding of economic and social processes while offering them the opportunity to apply their knowledge at the largest economic research institute in Germany.

We are looking for Doctoral Students for the DIW Graduate Center PhD Program in Economics The DIW Graduate Center offers a five-year program of in-depth training in Economics leading to a PhD from one of Berlin’s universities. Students will complete a rigorous coursework curriculum and receive on-the-job training in DIW Berlin’s research departments. Students' research may be theoretical or applied in nature. Most work at the GC, however, has a strong empirical component. The program also encourages funded internships at prestigious institutions such as the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank and government ministries, as well as research stays at renowned universities around the world.

The DIW Graduate Center offers five years of funding with a standard stipend of 1,650 euros per month in the first year and a work contract in subsequent years. After completing the first year, doctoral students will join one of the research departments at the institute.

Requirements: Applicants to our PhD program must hold a master’s degree or diploma in Economics. Applications may also be submitted while the degree is still in progress, provided it is completed before the program starts. Degrees from other related fields (such as statistics, quantitative social sciences, mathematics or engineering) may also fulfill requirements for the program if the applicant has a sufficient background in Economics.

Applicants whose native language is not English must demonstrate English language proficiency unless they hold a degree from a university in an English-speaking country or can document at least one year of studies in an English-speaking degree program. A high score on the TOEFL or IELTS test is considered sufficient evidence of English proficiency. Knowledge of German is not required for a successful application, but students are encouraged to learn German and improve their language skills over the course of the program

Application and Information: We value diversity and therefore welcome all applications—regardless of gender, disability, nationality, or ethnic and social background.

Please apply only online through our application portal by January 15, 2027, quoting the reference number GC-1-26-Stip-e and include the following application documents:

  • Motivation letter (max. 2 pages) explaining your reasons for applying and briefly outlining your major research interests;
  • Detailed curriculum vitae (without photograph);
  • Two academic letters of recommendation, to be submitted directly by senior academics (e.g., professors, postdoctoral researchers) via our application site;
  • Copies of academic transcripts and other certificates;
  • Completed application form (can be found on our application site);
  • IELTS or TOEFL scores, if applicable;
  • GRE General Test – Test Taker Score Report (PDF), if applicable. Please also attach your GRE Test if you have already submitted it to the Institutional Account.
You can access the application portal via our GC website under application site.

Please note that only applications submitted through the application portal will be considered and that the application is to be completed in English.

Do you have any questions about this call for applications or the online application? You may find your question already answered on our GC website, particularly in the FAQ section of the application site — please take a look before contacting us.

If you still have questions after reviewing our GC website, please contact gradcenter@diw.de for content-related inquiries and recruiting@diw.de for technical questions regarding the online application.

Founded in 1925, DIW Berlin (the German Institute for Economic Research) is one of the leading economic research institutes in Germany. The Institute analyzes the economic and social aspects of topical issues, formulating and disseminating policy advice based on its research findings. DIW Berlin is part of both the national and international scientific communities, provides research infrastructure to academics all over the world, and promotes the next generation of scientists. A member of the Leibniz Association, DIW Berlin is independent and primarily publicly funded.

jobs.title: Research Fellow positions (Doctoral Researchers) (x/f/m)
jobs.institution: Max-Planck-Institut für ausländisches öffentliches Recht und Völkerrecht
jobs.description_html:
At the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law, scholars pursue research relating tofundamental issues and current developments in the areas of public international law, European Union law, and the constitutional and administrative law of individual states, together with numerous visiting scholars from all over the world. In its fields, our library is the largest in Europe and one of the most comprehensive in the world.

The newly established Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER), headed by Dr. Gordon Friedrichs at the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg, invites applications for two Research Fellow positions (Doctoral Researchers) (x/f/m) with a preferred starting date of 1 January 2027 (the positions are funded for three years)
The Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER) investigates how global order istransformed as states - particularly great and middle powers - pursue competing visions of the principles, rules andinstitutions that structure international relations amid intensifying geopolitical rivalry. The group conceptualizes theseprocesses as constellations of global (dis)ordering through which states seek to advance their visions of order by creating,reshaping, connecting, bypassing, or disengaging from international institutions, building new formal or ad hoc institutionalarrangements, and strategically leveraging economic and technological interdependence. DISORDER examines how suchconstellations emerge across the fields of security, economy, and technology, and what forms of global order they produce,transform, or erode.

Job description The successful candidates will develop independent doctoral dissertation projects within the framework of the Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER). Their research should contribute to the group’s broader inquiry into how states pursue competing visions of global order through international institutions and how these processes reshape global order across different issue areas.

Possible orientations of the doctoral projects include:
  • an actor-centred perspective, examining how a particular great or middle power pursues its vision of global order across different issue areas institutional settings; or
  • a domain-centred perspective, comparing how different states interact with and reshape international institutions within aparticular field, such as security, economy, or technology
Potential empirical cases may include, but are not limited to, the United States, China, Russia, India, Brazil, Japan, and other international actors such as the European Union.

The doctoral researchers will:
  • develop and conduct an original PhD project that contributes to the conceptual and empirical agenda of the DISORDER research group;
  • conduct empirical research using qualitative methods such as process tracing, qualitative content and discourse analysis, and semi-structured interviews;
  • contribute to the comparative and collaborative research activities of the group;
  • participate in research group meetings, workshops, conferences, and other academic activities;
  • present research findings at international conferences and prepare publications for peer-reviewed academic outlets;
  • contribute to the organization of workshops, conferences, and other activities of the research group and the MPIL.
Your profile
  • An excellent Master’s degree or equivalent in Political Science, with a specialization in International Relations or Foreign Policy Analysis
  • A strong research interest in global order, international institutions, and great- and middle-power politics, including their foreign policies
  • A substantive interest in one or more of the group’s empirical issue areas (security, economy, and technology)
  • A strong interest in qualitative research and familiarity with relevant research methods
  • Excellent written and spoken English
  • Additional language skills and country- or region-specific expertise relevant to the proposed doctoral project are considered assets
  • The ability to conduct independent research while contributing actively to a collaborative research environm
We offer
  • An attractive and international work environment with an unparalleled research infrastructure and a good working atmosphere
  • A varied, responsible and team-orientated job
  • Remuneration in accordance with the guidelines of the MPG funding agreements (65 per cent of EG13, TVöD-Bund)
  • Access to our world-leading library and a multitude of databases
  • A workplace that is easy to reach by public transport and free employee parking spaces
  • A job ticket for public transport
  • Offers for work-life balance and four affiliated daycare centres
Application The Max Planck Society has set itself the goal of employing more severely disabled people. Applications from severely disabled persons are expressly encouraged. The Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. Furthermore, the Max Planck Society aims to increase the proportion of women in areas where they are underrepresented. Women are therefore strongly encouraged to apply.

Interested candidates are invited to submit their complete application exclusively via the online application system availableon our website by 22 November 2026.

Applications should include a CV, a cover letter of no more than two pages, copies of relevant degree certificates and transcripts of records, a one-page summary of the applicant’s Master’s thesis, a five-page PhD project proposal that clearlyrelates to the research agenda of the DISORDER group and indicates which of the thematic orientations outlined above the proposed project primarily addresses, and two letters of recommendation.

The documents will be deleted after the application process. The interviews will take place in late November/early Decemberin person at the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg. Application expensescannot be covered.

For questions regarding the positions, please contact Dr. Gordon Friedrichs at friedrichs@mpil.de.


Max Planck Institute
for Comparative Public Law and International Law
Im Neuenheimer Feld 535
69120 Heidelberg

jobs.title: Research Associate / PhD Candidate (m/f/d) iMOL
jobs.institution: Johann Wolfgang Goethe-Universität Frankfurt am Main
jobs.description_html: The Johann Wolfgang Goethe University Frankfurt am Main is one of the largest universities in Germany with around 41,000 students and with about 7,000 employees. Founded in 1914 by Frankfurt citizens and since 2008 once again proud of its foundation status Goethe University possesses a high degree of autonomy, modernity and professional diversity. As a comprehensive university, the Goethe University offers a total of 16 departments on five campuses and 159 degree programs along with an outstanding research reputation. Furthermore, the Goethe University is part of the Group of Rhine-Main-Universities (RMU). As part of the DFG Research Training Group iMOL (GRK 2566) at Goethe University Frankfurt, we are looking for creative and highly motivated candidates. iMOL connects advanced imaging with molecular life sciences. The doctoral program trains outstanding young researchers in cutting-edge microscopy and AI-driven image analysis, enabling them to investigate the principles of life across different spatial and temporal scales. A position is available starting on 01.03.2027 as Research Associate (m/f/d) PhD Candidate E 13 TV-G-U initially, the position is limited to a fixed term of three years. The salary grade is based on the job characteristics of the collective agreement applicable to Goethe University (TV-G-U). This position is also available on a part-time basis. Your responsibilities Preparation of medical and biological samples Preparation and application of next-generation microscopy techniques Computer-assisted acquisition and analysis of multidimensional imaging data Visualization of biological and medical samples Presentation and publication of research findings Your profile You hold a completed university degree (Master’s, Diploma, or State Examination) in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biophysics, Physics, Molecular Biology, Medicine, Computer Science or a related field and have a strong interest in microscopy. Experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage: Working with cells and organisms Light and electron microscopy Image processing, computer-assisted image analysis, and data evaluation We are looking for technical aptitude, an independent and careful approach to work, and enthusiasm for interdisciplinary collaboration. Good English language skills are an advantage due to our international research environment. Goethe University is committed to equal opportunity, family friendliness, and diversity. To strengthen the diversity of perspectives and lived experiences within the university, applications from individuals with a migration background and from members of other groups that have so far been underrepresented are particularly welcome. Applicants with a severe disability, or those legally equivalent, will be given preferential consideration in cases of equal suitability. If women are underrepresented in a faculty or administrative unit, they will be given preferential consideration in cases of equal qualifications. Interested? We look forward to receiving your application! Please submit your application documents (cover letter, detailed CV, academic transcripts, and a description of your research interests and motivation) as a single PDF file by November 30, 2026, via email to: Prof. Dr. Achilleas Frangakis, office.frangakis@biophysik.org For further information, please visit: https://imol.uni-frankfurt.de/apply/ Please note that the application documents will not be returned. Costs incurred during the application process will not be reimbursed by Goethe University. www.uni-frankfurt.de

jobs.title: PhD positions at the International Max Planck Research School for Chemistry and Physics of Quantum Materials
jobs.institution: Max-Planck-Institut für Chemische Physik fester Stoffe
jobs.description_html: The International Max Planck Research School for Chemistry and Physics of Quantum Materials is a joint PhD program between the Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids in Dresden, Germany, Technische Universität Dresden and the University of St Andrews, Scotland. By working together, we create a highly attractive overall package of PhD‑level research on solid-state chemistry and condensed matter physics, building on world‐class research activities in quantum materials at the three institutions. PhD positions at the International Max Planck Research School for Chemistry and Physics of Quantum Materials Our program will provide successful candidates with a stimulating environment, in which they will have the opportunity to interact and work with world-leading scientists from the three sites and use our excellent infrastructure and facilities. Our research is generously funded and successful candidates will receive competitive payment based on the primary location of their research project. We seek to recruit multiple PhD students in 2027 for a range of inter‐institutional research projects in the broadly defined field of quantum materials. Research work will be combined with graduate courses and general skills training. Both experimental and theoretical projects are offered and a complete list of all projects is available on our website. Excellent candidates from any country are encouraged to apply. Applicants are expected to have an outstanding bachelor's or master's degree in a field of study that is well-aligned with our research activities. The IMPRS-CPQM places great importance on fostering a pleasant working atmosphere and encouraging friendly cooperation. We are committed to increasing the proportion of women in areas where they are underrepresented. We have also set ourselves the goal of employing more people with severe disabilities. Your application Closing date for applications is November 30, 2026. Accepted candidates are expected to start their projects no later than September 2027. Apply now For more information, including application guidelines, please visit our website: https://imprs-cpqm.mpg.de

Doctoral Position for developing advanced magnetic concepts required in future high power grid interfaces Sprachauswahl FAQ de Deutsch English Stellenportal chevron_left Übersicht chevron_left Übersicht Doctoral Position for developing advanced magnetic concepts required in future high power grid interfaces 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Laboratory for High Power Electronic Systems (HPE) at the Department of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering of ETH Zurich conducts internationally leading research on power electronic converter systems, which are required, for example, in future energy distribution systems for the integration of renewable energy sources or in traction applications/electric vehicles. Another research focus is on solid-state pulse modulators for medical applications (computer tomography/cancer treatment) and accelerators (CERN). For the design and optimisation of the various power electronic systems, we develop advanced multi-physics models/digital twins/virtual prototypes at the component and system level. For a new research project on high-power grid interfaces for future data centres, PV, and energy storage systems, we are looking for a: Doctoral Candidate (PhD position), with a workload of 100% of  for developing advanced magnetic concepts required in future high power grid interfaces Job description We are looking for highly motivated individuals with an outstanding academic background to pursue a Doctorate (PhD) in the multidisciplinary field of developing, modelling and optimising advanced magnetic devices (inductors, transformers and filters) for use in future high-power grid interfaces and active rectifiers These devices are essential for filtering and protection in grid interfaces and significantly impact the achievable system power density and efficiency Bidirectional grid interfaces connect the AC grid to the DC 'load', and potential applications include large-scale data centres, large-scale photovoltaic (PV) systems and battery energy storage systems for storing the fluctuating energy of renewable energy sources To maximise the efficiency and power density of these high-power grid interfaces, you will design new magnetic device concepts and develop multi-physics models that describe (HF) losses in the windings and cores, cooling/temperature distribution, parasitic capacitances, magnetic couplings between the different components, and electrical insulation In addition to designing the magnetic devices, you will work on optimising the modulation schemes and operation during grid failures of the grid interfaces, as these have a significant impact on the magnetics design The developed concepts and models will be integrated into optimisation procedures for power electronic converter systems in a computationally efficient way This is essential for achieving outstanding system efficiencies and power densities, as well as gaining a competitive edge The models are also part of an ongoing, wider modelling framework development project at HPE, offering the opportunity to collaborate with other Doctoral candidates (PhD candidates) on different modelling aspects For verifying the new concepts and developed models, you will design and build different magnetic devices (including a converter system) to operate the magnetics under realistic conditions Our laboratory is offering a challenging and scientifically exciting full-time position within a dynamic international team at one of the world's leading technical universities We also strongly encourage participation in international conferences and offer a competitive salary, jobs.title: Doctoral position in robotic spraying for biocementation
jobs.description:
Doctoral position in robotic spraying for biocementation Sprachauswahl FAQ de Deutsch English Stellenportal chevron_left Übersicht chevron_left Übersicht Doctoral position in robotic spraying for biocementation 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Chair for Digital Building Technologies invites applications for a PhD position on robotic spraying as an additive manufacturing process for biocementation. The research brings together two closely coupled lines of work: the development of an additive robotic fabrication system based on material deposition and microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation (MICP), with a focus on applying MICP to the fabrication of architectural elements. This PhD is part of the SNSF-funded project “DFabuLis: Digital Fabrication Using Living Systems”, conducted in collaboration with Dr. Dimitrios Terzis, Senior Scientist in the Laloui group at EPFL. Project background Conventional cement-based construction binds aggregates through an energy-intensive process. Bio-binders offer a different fabrication logic. In biocementation, certain bacteria precipitate calcium carbonate between particles, allowing binding to form under ambient conditions. This project treats the bio-binder as a fabrication parameter. Through robotic deposition of bacterial and cementation solutions, mineral binding can be spatially controlled across a printed structure, producing architectural elements with locally differentiated density, strength, porosity, and surface properties within a single component. The research will investigate how robotic deposition of biocement can be translated into architectural production strategies, from material placement and component geometry to surface formation and assembly. In collaboration with the Soil Mechanics Laboratory at EPFL, the project connects robotic fabrication with the characterisation and formulation of bio-binders. The resulting strategies will be explored in architectural-scale demonstrators. Job description You will develop a robotic fabrication process for biocementation, including adapting existing deposition hardware, and the computational workflow linking design intent to material placement You will use it to produce architectural components, investigating through making how graded biocementation can inform structure, surface, and assembly You will assess the environmental footprint of the process and use it to guide fabrication and design choices You will conduct research in close collaboration with project partners at ETH and EPFL and, where applicable, industry partners. You will work closely with the Soil Mechanics Laboratory at EPFL, whose characterisation of the material will inform the development of the process You will write scientific articles for publication in peer-reviewed journals, present at international conferences, and contribute to teaching through the supervision of semester and master's projects Profile A Master's degree in architecture or a closely related discipline, with a demonstrated body of work in digital fabrication Competence in building and modifying fabrication equipment; experience with robotics, electronics, or control software is a strong asset Fluency in computational design and experience moving between digital models and physical results Interest in biological or material processes; experience in a wet lab is welcome but not required. Interest in circular and low-impact construction; familiarity with life cycle assessment is an advantage Excellent written and spoken English; conversational German is an advantage Strong communication skills and a collaborative disposition, as the project spans disciplines and research groups Workplace Workplace We offer The Chair for Digital Building Technologies within the Institute of Technology in Architecture conducts research at the intersection of computational design, materials, and construction-scale fabrication. Over more than a decade, the group has developed and operated powder-bed and extrusion-based printing systems at architectural scale, with built results including the tallest 3D-printed structures in the world. In-house expertise in materials, mechanical design, electronics, and software, together with complete workshop and prototyping infrastructure, allows research ideas to move directly from concept to machine to printed artifact, and doctoral researchers are given considerable latitude in shaping that trajectory. Our highly diverse and international group offers extensive networks within ETH and internationally. We are committed to diversity by offering flexible working hours, home office options, and other measures to ensure team members can perform their roles effectively. chevron_right Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. jobs.title: Two Doctoral Positions in the SNSF Research Project "From Homes to Habitat – Swiss Housing Cooperatives as Agents of Socio-Ecological Transition"
jobs.description:
Two Doctoral Positions in the SNSF Research Project "From Homes to Habitat – Swiss Housing Cooperatives as Agents of Socio-Ecological Transition" Sprachauswahl FAQ de Deutsch English Stellenportal chevron_left Übersicht chevron_left Übersicht Two Doctoral Positions in the SNSF Research Project "From Homes to Habitat – Swiss Housing Cooperatives as Agents of Socio-Ecological Transition" 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken ETH Wohnforum – ETH CASE (Centre for Research on Architecture, Society & the Built Environment) at the Department of Architecture, ETH Zurich, is seeking two doctoral researchers (100%, four years) to join the SNSF-funded research project “From Homes to Habitats – Swiss Housing Cooperatives as Agents of Socio-Ecological Transition,” starting on 1 June 2027 or upon agreement. The PhD will last from 2027-2031 (4 years). Project background How can housing support a shift towards more sustainable ways of living? The overall research project investigates the potential of housing cooperatives in Switzerland as agents of socio-ecological transition. Moving beyond their established role in providing affordable housing, the project examines how housing cooperatives develop innovative social, spatial, and ecological practices across diverse territorial contexts. While existing research has predominantly focused on housing cooperatives in major cities, the project investigates housing cooperatives in metropolitan, peri-urban, rural, peripheral, and Alpine territories, examining how different urbanisation processes shape cooperative housing practices and their potential for socio-ecological transformation. The project is hosted at ETH Wohnforum – ETH CASE, Department of Architecture, ETH Zurich, under the responsibility of Prof. Dr. Elli Mosayebi , Professor of Architecture and Design. The doctoral researchers will work within an interdisciplinary research team bringing together expertise in architecture, housing, urban and territorial studies, and socio-ecological transformation. In addition, you will benefit from being associated to the Doctoral Programme at the ETH Zurich Department of Architecture’s Institute of Landscape and Urban Studies (LUS). ETH Wohnforum – ETH CASE (Centre for Research on Architecture, Society & the Built Environment) is an interdisciplinary institute for research, consulting and education in the field of housing, architecture, and urban development at the department of architecture at ETH Zurich. Job description We are seeking two motivated doctoral researchers to join our interdisciplinary research team and contribute to the investigation of housing cooperatives as agents of socio-ecological transition across Switzerland. Your responsibilities and tasks will include: Contribute to the development of the project's conceptual and methodological framework. Participate in the mapping and typology building of housing cooperatives across Switzerland. Design and conduct qualitative case studies within the respective territorial focus. Undertake fieldwork, including site visits, interviews, participant observation, and spatial documentation. Analyse architectural, spatial, social, and ecological practices through qualitative and visual research methods. Participate in the organisation of workshops with researchers, housing cooperatives, and relevant stakeholders. Profile Master's degree in architecture, urban studies, sociology, or a related discipline, with a strong interest in housing, territorial transformation, and socio-ecological questions. Strong interest in interdisciplinary research at the intersection of architecture, society, and ecology. Knowledge of and/or experience with qualitative research methods, including interviews, participant observation, and case study research. Interest in architectural and spatial analysis, mapping, and visual research methods. Experience with architectural drawing, GIS, or cartographic tools is an advantage. Ability to work independently and collaboratively within an interdisciplinary research team. Strong analytical, communication, and academic writing skills. Excellent command of written and spoken English. Knowledge of German, French, and/or Italian is highly desirable, particularly for conducting fieldwork in Switzerland. Workplace Workplace We offer ETH Zurich is a family-friendly employer with excellent working conditions. You can look forward to an exciting working environment, cultural diversity and attractive offers and benefits. The positions offer the opportunity to pursue doctoral research within an interdisciplinary and collaborative research environment at ETH Zurich, engaging with contemporary debates on housing, architecture, urbanisation, and socio-ecological transition.The doctoral researchers will benefit from close collaboration with the ETH Wohnforum research team and an international network of academic and practice-based partners.
