jobs.title: PhD position: PFAS free membranes for use in electrolysers
jobs.description_html:
Why apply?
This multidisciplinary project integrates electrochemistry, metal–organic framework-based materials, and membrane chemistry to develop the next generation of high-performance membranes and unlock new possibilities for advanced molecular separation and transport.

Can you design the membrane that powers the next generation of electrolysers?
Electrolysis and electrocatalysis have a key role to play in creating a more sustainable chemical industry. At the heart of these technologies are membranes that control the transport of protons and other species—but today’s proton exchange membranes rely heavily on PFAS-based materials such as Nafion®. We are looking for a PhD candidate to develop a new generation of high-performance, PFAS-free proton-conductive membranes. In this project, you will combine the unique properties of proton-conductive metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) with those of proton-conductive polymers to create innovative membrane materials. You will systematically investigate how molecular structure, composition, and membrane architecture determine proton transport and overall performance. Your research will span materials chemistry, membrane science, and electrochemistry. You will establish design principles for high-performance proton-conductive membranes and put your materials to the test in different electrolyser configurations. This is an opportunity to work at the interface of fundamental materials science and real-world energy technology, with the ambition to develop membrane materials that can help enable a cleaner and more sustainable chemical industry. The PhD students will be supervised by Dennis Hetterscheid (Leiden Institute of Chemistry).

What you bring
We are looking for an enthusiastic and motivated candidate who is excited to pursue an interdisciplinary PhD at the interface of electrochemistry, materials chemistry, and membrane science. The project combines electrochemistry, MOF synthesis and characterization, physical measurements, and electrolysis studies, offering the opportunity to develop expertise across multiple fields.

You hold an MSc degree in Physical Chemistry, Chemistry, Materials Science, or a related discipline, with a background in one or more of the following areas: electrochemistry, membrane chemistry, MOF synthesis, or materials characterization. jobs.title: PhD Position Optimizing Multi-actor Transport and Logistics Systems
jobs.description_html:
Would you like to develop new theory and algorithms for problems with multiple interacting actors? Are you interested in working at the intersection of game theory and mixed-integer optimisation?

Job description
Transport and logistics systems consist of many players with potentially conflicting objectives that continuously strive to maximize their performance. The competition and collaboration between these players can influence their decision-making, which is something that traditional Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulations with a single decision-maker cannot capture. The goal of this PhD is to develop novel methodologies at the intersection of operations research and game theory to address these problems. Applications can go beyond the transport and logistics domain.

Your research will focus on mathematical modelling and algorithm development for planning and operating multi-actor systems, taking into account that the actions of one actor influence the opportunities and performance of others. A central methodological component of the position is the development of scalable optimisation algorithms for large and computationally challenging problem instances. You will formulate mathematical programming models and design solution approaches based on techniques such as column generation, branch-and-price, and Benders decomposition.

You will be expected to:
  • develop new game-theoretic/optimization models for multi-actor decision problems;
  • design scalable solution methods for large-scale optimisation problems;
  • contribute to scientific publications in leading journals in operations research, transportation, and logistics;
  • communicate research findings to an interdisciplinary audience.

You will join the Transport and Logistics section of the Department of Engineering Systems and Services

Job requirements

  • An MSc degree in operations research, econometrics, applied mathematics, computer science, industrial engineering, systems and control, or a closely related discipline.
  • A strong background and demonstrated experience in mathematical optimisation, in particular mixed-integer programming.
  • Excellent programming skills (e.g., Python, Julia, Java, or C++) and experience with optimization solvers.
  • Very good academic writing and communication skills in English.

jobs.title: PhD in Entanglement Routing in Quantum Optical Fiber Networks
jobs.description_html:
Are you passionate about building an entanglement-based routing in quantum optical networks?
Join us to develop an innovative entanglement-based routing architecture and protocol, and set up an experimental testbed to route entangled photons in the presence of classical telecom traffic in multi-node quantum optical fiber networks.

Information
Efficient distribution and routing of entanglement are indispensable for quantum‑secure communication (e.g., advanced QKD networks), distributed quantum computing, quantum‑secure enterprise connectivity and quantum teleportation services across metropolitan or regional distances. However, unique features of quantum information, such as non-amplification, no-cloning, or measurement without altering the quantum states, make it difficult to re-use the architecture and protocols of classical telecom networks for quantum communication and networking. In contrast to classical optical signals, quantum states are extremely fragile and degrade rapidly due to loss, noise, and decoherence, especially over long distances. As a result, conventional telecom solutions such as optical amplification, regeneration, and routing cannot be directly applied to quantum networks. Nevertheless, recent advances in quantum state generation and measurement have opened new opportunities for developing quantum network architectures and protocols for routing and teleportation, a critical enabler for quantum networks.

In this PhD project, you will set up an experimental testbed for a multi-node quantum optical fiber network that enables entanglement generation and detection, frequency conversion, and entanglement routing of quantum-classical packets between nodes connected by optical switches. Additionally, you will investigate the coexistence of classical telecom traffic and quantum signals and the effects of impairments such as noise and crosstalk. The project will combine theoretical and simulation studies and validate them with experimental studies. The project will leverage KPN’s expertise to address real‑world constraints—including scalability, interoperability, reliability, and manageability—while developing the telecom‑grade quantum networks.

The PhD position is fully funded by our industry partner (KPN) in Smart Optical Networks Lab (SONL) of the Electro-Optical Communication group. The research activity of SONL covers a wide range of topics, including network design and software control, reconfigurable interconnects for telecom, datacenters, AI clusters, and quantum networks, down to heterogeneous photonic integrated circuits and systems for enabling low-latency, fast network reconfiguration in real systems. Additionally, we focus on innovative solutions for switching and routing in secure quantum-optical networks. jobs.title: PhD in Machine Learning for Quantum Systems (1.0 FTE)
jobs.description_html:

The successful candidate will join Interpretable Machines for Physics (IMP), a research group led by Dr. Anna Dawid. They will work on the mechanics of ML and developing new ML approaches to challenging quantum problems, with a strong focus on making these approaches interpretable, reliable, and scalable. In this position, you will learn about state-of-the-art deep learning solutions as well as the challenges of understanding neural networks. You will be given increasing scientific freedom, supported by structured mentoring, including career development plans guided by your plans after the PhD. The starting date is flexible, the latest in November 2027.

The position is set in the exciting, friendly, and interdisciplinary environment of the aQa (Applied Quantum Algorithms) group, which is a team of faculty, postdoctoral researchers, and students across the Leiden Institute of Physics (LION), the Leiden Institute for Advanced Computer Science (LIACS), the Leiden Institute for Chemistry (LIC), and the Leiden Mathematical Institute (MI) at the Leiden University.

jobs.title: PhD Researcher Van Vollenhoven Institute for Law, Governance and Society (1.0 FTE)
jobs.description_html:
PhD Researcher in “A Sociology of Post-Imperial Islamic Legal Culture: Insights from Central Asia, the Middle East, North Africa, and Southeast Asia” (Minaret Project), 1.0 FTE.

The Van Vollenhoven Institute for Law, Governance and Society (VVI) invites applications for one PhD Researcher (1.0 FTE, 4 years) from September/October 2027 – September/October 2031 to join the Minaret Project, a HORIZON Unit Grant-funded interdisciplinary and transnational research initiative, which examines the interconnection between law, religion and governance in post-imperial Muslim-majority societies to promote democracy and good governance.

The project brings together 11 universities with 15 PhD researchers across 3 work packages and 15 subprojects, with the applicant contributing to the subproject Neo-Imperialism and Constitutional Reform: The Global Dimension. This subproject examines to what extent international organizations and global governance actors act as neo-imperial forces shaping constitutional reform in North Africa and the Middle East.

It will explore how donor-driven “rule of law” and “good governance” programs are developed, interpreted, and implemented in countries such as Jordan, Lebanon, and Syria. Particular attention will be paid to how the legal frameworks promoted by international actors relate to the government practices in these countries, and in particular to those embedded in local traditions and religious values.

Drawing on policy-document analysis and elite interviews with a diverse range of actors -including international advisers, domestic policymakers, civil-society representatives, legal practitioners, religious scholars, and community leaders-, the study will investigate how transnational constitutional models are negotiated, adapted, resisted, or hybridized in practice. It will contribute to debates on postcolonial constitutionalism by examining the processes through which legal and governance norms circulate across borders, as well as the forms of influence, dependency, and agency that shape their adoption.

Ultimately, the project seeks to develop a nuanced account of how external interventions affect perceptions of legitimacy, legal pluralism, and sovereignty in transitional Muslim-majority societies.

What you will do
The PhD researcher will join the Leiden-based Minaret team, working closely with two senior-researchers and two external mentors (one academic and one non-academic, associated with the project). The position provides the opportunity to conduct original empirical research on the underlying structures of constitutional reform in said countries, while also contributing to public engagement and the collaborative life of the project. All PhD researchers are required to undertake two secondments abroad with the project’s associated partners, one academic and one non-academic, of between two and six months' duration. This will not only enhance research capabilities but also equip the PhD researcher for academic and non-academic roles.

Academic Research
  • Conduct socio-legal and policy analysis with key stakeholders in selected countries.
  • Write a doctoral dissertation and co-author academic publications based on qualitative research.
  • Contribute to the project’s comparative framework within the subproject; within the work package (Imperial Genealogies and Constitutional Formation) and between the work packages.


Communications & Engagement
  • Present research findings at events organized by the research project, such as 3 summer schools and 4 training events.
  • Willingness and ability to spend extended periods abroad for fieldwork and 2 secondments.
  • Help organize international workshops, conferences, and events with academic and civil society partners.
  • Contribute to project website and social media accounts.

Where you will work
The Faculty of Law is based in both Leiden and The Hague and, with over 7,000 students and approximately 600 staff members, is one of the largest law faculties in the Netherlands. The faculty is committed to innovative, multidisciplinary research and a constantly evolving curriculum that addresses key societal challenges. Our faculty is large enough to make an impact on both a national and international scale, yet small enough to offer a personal and engaging learning experience. In this way, we contribute every day to a safer and more sustainable world. Impact with law! For more information, please visit https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/law.

The Van Vollenhoven Institute for Law, Governance and Society (VVI) is part of the Leiden Law School. The VVI seeks to advance knowledge of the formation and functioning of legal systems in their social contexts, the impact of these systems on society and vice versa, their effectiveness in governance, and their contribution to development. The Institute adopts a socio-legal and global approach, doing research on law in the books and law in action in Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Europe. VVI staff teaches several socio-legal thematic and regional courses for both Dutch and foreign exchange students. In addition, VVI provides PhD supervision, advisory services and training courses to policy makers and practitioners. For more information, see www.vvi.leidenuniv.nl.

What you bring
In our team, we are looking for someone who can work independently while also contributing to a collaborative environment. Since every position is unique, we will devote careful attention to your onboarding. If some aspects of the work are new to you, we will identify what support you need and develop a tailored plan for your professional growth.

We do not expect candidates to already have all the qualifications listed below. Training will be provided in areas such as socio-legal studies, research methods, and the specificities of constitutional reform in the Middle East. jobs.title: PhD Position Flexibility in Nuclear Power
jobs.description_html:
Can nuclear- and renewable energy play nice?

Job description
Both Europe and the Netherlands are committed to transitioning to a CO2-neutral economy by 2050. As part of this commitment, the Netherlands has built large-scale wind park, and a significant amount of energy comes from solar power as well. While wind and solar energy help to decarbonize power generation, it also comes at a cost. Due to the intermittent availability of wind and solar energy, grid congestion can occur (which means that the grid lacks sufficient capacity to handle demand or supply of electricity). Therefore, the grid must be carefully managed. In many countries, gas power plants help manage the grid. However, since natural gas counteracts decarbonization, the question arises: “which other technologies can help reduce grid congestion?

Small modular reactors (SMR) - nuclear reactors below 300 MWe – may be able to operate flexibly to help counteract grid congestion. As such reactors have less inertia, they are better suited to load-following than large-scale nuclear power plants. Even so, their ramp rates are much lower than other technologies. Through smart design of the power cycle and the inclusion of thermal energy storage, ramp rates of SMR’s can be greatly enhanced.

In this thesis project, you will design advanced power cycles with or without energy storage for SMR’s to enable enhanced load-following. Using numerical techniques, you will couple transient power cycle modelling with nuclear reactor modelling to analyse any feedback to the reactor. You will run different load-following scenarios to ascertain technologically feasible enhanced ramp rates. You will be assisted by an expert supervisory team during your PhD. As the Dutch Nuclear industry is growing rapidly, and the Dutch Government has announced a significant expansion of nuclear energy, your results may actively contribute to shaping the Dutch nuclear landscape.

Your Working Environment
You will join the Process & Energy (P&E) department at TU Delft’s Mechanical Engineering faculty.Our department works along the themes of Energy, Flow and Processes. You will work together with top researchers highly skilled in thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics. Moreover, we collaborate with researchers from the Reactor Institute Delft. You will have opportunities for professional development through both technical and non-technical courses. jobs.title: PhD Position Experimental Analysis of Boiling Instabilities in Advanced Nuclear Steam Generators
jobs.description_html:
Help determine operational limits of next-gen nuclear steam generators!

Job description
Advanced nuclear reactor designs like the high temperature gas cooled reactor or molten salt reactor offer certain advantages compared to traditional light water reactors. One such advantage is their potential to operate with a high thermal efficiency. This advantage stems from the fact that these reactors operate at much higher temperatures, enabling superheated steam generation.

Traditional light water reactors utilize so-called U-tube steam generators in which saturated steam is produced. It is well known that such steam generators suffer from spontaneous oscillations of two-phase mass flow and pressure drop on the shell side. This phenomenon is well understood in light water reactors, allowing for safe and stable operation. However, these boiling instabilities are more severe in once-through helical steam generators, as the dryout point will shift rapidly up and down along the helical tubes. This oscillating behaviour can lead to thermal fatigue of the tube walls, which can ultimately result in mechanical failure. While this phenomenon is already complex enough in and of itself, it typically coincides with parallel channel instabilities.

In this project, you will develop and build a laboratory steam generator set-up to study boiling instabilities in helical tubes. In the first year, you will help design and build the set-up along with a team of skilled technicians and an energetic supervisory team. Subsequently, you will study the characteristics of the boiling instabilities within the set-up and compare them to a numerical model.

Your Working Environment
You will join the Process & Energy (P&E) department at TU Delft’s Mechanical Engineering faculty.Our department works along the themes of Energy, Flow and Processes. You will work together with top researchers highly skilled in thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics. Moreover, we collaborate with researchers from the Reactor Institute Delft. You will have opportunities for professional development through both technical and non-technical courses. jobs.description_html:
Do you want to uncover how food properties shape children's eating behaviour and energy intake, combining nutrition, sensory science and innovative digital tools to help promote healthier eating? Join our Child Eating Behaviour team as PhD candidate at Wageningen University & Research.

Your duties and responsibilities include:
  • identifying and critically reviewing the literature on factors that influence children's eating behaviours and dietary patterns;
  • designing and conducting experiments on the role of food properties in moderating eating behaviour and energy intake in children, using innovative digital tools to track eating behaviour;
  • analysing your experimental studies and publishing the findings in peer-reviewed journals and at international conferences;
  • translating your evidence into recommendations to improve the food environment for children in the Netherlands;

jobs.title: PhD Position: Nitrogen Valorization in High-Temp Electrochemical Cells (F/M/X)
jobs.description_html:
Sustainable ammonia production is an important challenge in the transition towards a climate-neutral chemical industry. Conventional ammonia synthesis is highly energy intensive and relies predominantly on fossil-derived hydrogen. Electrochemical routes offer the possibility to produce ammonia using renewable electricity while enabling new, decentralized production concepts.

This PhD project will focus on the development of advanced materials, electrodes, and membrane-electrode assemblies for high-temperature electrochemical ammonia synthesis using solid oxide and protonic ceramic electrochemical cells (SOC and PCC technologies). The research will address the electrochemical conversion of nitrogen- and NOx-containing streams towards NH3.

The project will combine catalyst and electrode development with ceramic-cell fabrication, electrochemical testing, product analysis, and advanced materials characterization. Different catalyst integration strategies, including infiltration and exsolution, will be investigated to improve activity, selectivity, and long-term stability. Particular attention will be given to electrode–electrolyte interfaces, reaction mechanisms, and degradation under realistic operating conditions.

This PhD position is part of HyNITROGEN (https://groenvermogennl.org/en/nieuws/e20-3-million-for-hynitrogen-consortium-research-into-sustainable-nitrogen-chemistry) a large national research program within GroenvermogenNL that brings together more than 40 academic and industrial partners to develop sustainable production routes for ammonia and other nitrogen-based chemicals using renewable hydrogen and green electricity.

jobs.description_html:
Are you a graduate in exact sciences, engineering or econometrics, passionate about using data and AI to improve people's lives?Eindhoven University of Technology is looking for a PhD candidate to develop innovative data-driven solutions that predict and optimise the impact of housing improvements on children's health and wellbeing.

Millions of children, even in high-income countries, are born and grow up in homes with poor insulation, inadequate heating, or insufficient ventilation, affecting their health and development. This research is part of the NWO-funded research programme Homes for Upcoming Generations, which brings together social scientists, medical doctors, building engineers and industry partners.

As a PhD candidate, you will be part of the TU/e's internationally renowned Urban Systems and Real Estate group (Department of the Built Environment), conducting cutting-edge research at the intersection of urban systems, real estate, data science, and smart technologies. jobs.title: PhD Position Systematic Derivation of Formal Languages and Their Correctness
jobs.description_html:
From Semantics to Syntax — Systematic Derivation of Formal Languages and Their Correctness   

Job description
Formal languages, such as type theories and program logics, let us state and prove precisely what software should do. Today, each new language is designed by hand: experts invent the syntax, then check that it really means what it should. This is slow, and it has to be redone for every new problem. This project explores a different approach: start from the mathematical meaning of a language and derive the language itself from it, together with a proof that the two match. Several recent type theories were built this way, but each one with its own ad hoc techniques. Together, we want to find out whether there is one general recipe behind them. You will develop this theory using tools from category theory and type theory, and check your results in the Agda proof assistant. You will be supervised by Dr. Benedikt Ahrens in the Department of Software Technology at TU Delft.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • conducting this research, both individually and as part of a team;
  • participating in scientific life at TU Delft and in the Netherlands, for example by attending and organizing seminars;
  • participating in scientific life more globally, including publishing papers and attending workshops and conferences;
  • contributing to teaching in computer science, providing the opportunity to gain teaching experience.

Job requirements
Applications will be evaluated on the following criteria:
  • Masters degree in mathematics, computer science, or a related field
  • Experience in both category theory and theoretical computer science (e.g., type theory, logic or programming language semantics), or a strong motivation and ability to learn them.
  • Experience with a proof assistant (e.g., Agda, Rocq or Lean) is a plus, but not required.
  • Enjoyment of precise mathematical reasoning,
  • Ability to work independently and to collaborate across the maths/CS boundary;
  • Excellent written and spoken English
  • Willingness to contribute to, and possibly experience in, student supervision and teaching

jobs.title: Promovendus Ouderenzorg & Innovatie - Bouw mee aan de GOUD-poli
jobs.description_html:
Welkom bij de Universiteit Maastricht!

Dit is jouw kans om deel uit te maken van een onderzoeksproject dat de poliklinische zorg voor kwetsbare ouderen wil verbeteren! Wij zoeken een gemotiveerde promovendus die helpt bij de doorstart en doorontwikkeling van de GOUD-poli en participeert in zowel kwantitatief als in kwalitatief onderzoek.

Promovendus Ouderenzorg & Innovatie – Bouw mee aan de GOUD-poli
  • Ons doel: De werkdruk voor huisartsen te verlichten en tegelijkertijd de zorg voor geriatrische patiënten te verbeteren door nauwe samenwerking tussen huisarts en internist-ouderengeneeskunde.
  • Jouw collega’s: Je wordt onderdeel van de GOUD-poli (Gespecialiseerde Ouderenzorg Dichtbij poli), een samenwerkingsinitiatief van het Maastricht UMC+ en huisartsenorganisatie ZIO. Binnen een interdisciplinair team van internist-ouderengeneeskunde, huisartsen, epidemiologen, gezondheidseconomen, onderzoekers en studenten werk je nauw samen met de deelnemende huisartsenpraktijken. Je standplaats is het Maastricht UMC+ en je komt in dienst bij Maastricht University, waar je onderdeel wordt van onderzoeksinstituut CAPHRI (Care and Public Health Research Institute). CAPHRI (www.caphri.nl) heeft als missie om met hoogwaardig, methodologisch vernieuwend, interdisciplinair en maatschappelijk relevant onderzoek bij te dragen aan een gezonde samenleving voor iedereen. CAPHRI onderzoekt en verbetert gezondheid, zorg en welzijn, met nadruk op preventie, participatie, maatschappelijke relevantie, doelmatigheid en waarde van zorg.

Wij zijn op zoek naar een enthousiaste en gemotiveerde promovendus die wil bijdragen aan innovatieve zorg voor kwetsbare ouderen. Als promovendus speel je een centrale rol in de evaluatie van de effectiviteit van de GOUD-poli (Gespecialiseerde Ouderenzorg Dichtbij poli), een nieuwe eerstelijnsvoorziening die gericht is op verbetering van diagnostiek, efficiëntie en samenwerking in de zorg voor kwetsbare ouderen.

De GOUD-poli werd ingevoerd in zeven huisartsenpraktijken, waar eens per zes weken een internist-ouderengeneeskunde kwetsbare ouderen beoordeelt in nauwe samenwerking met de huisarts. Het doel is om de juiste zorg op de juiste plek te bieden, onnodige verwijzingen naar andere medisch specialisten te voorkomen en zowel de patiëntervaring als de ervaringen van zorgprofessionals te verbeteren.

Wat jij doet
Om dit initiatief te evalueren, voer je zowel kwantitatief als kwalitatief onderzoek uit.

Onderzoeksthema’s binnen het promotietraject:
  • Evaluatie van de effectiviteit van de GOUD-poli op verwijs- en zorgpatronen (pre- en post-interventiestudie).
  • Ervaringen van zorgprofessionals met de GOUD-poli (kwalitatief onderzoek).
  • Ervaringen van kwetsbare ouderen en mantelzorgers met de GOUD-poli (enquêteonderzoek).
  • Beschrijvende analyse van casuïstiek die gepresenteerd wordt op de GOUD-poli.
  • Analyses van de medicatiereviews tijdens en het opvolgen van de adviezen hieromtrent na de GOUD-poli.
  • Kosteneffectiviteit van de GOUD-poli.

Het project biedt de kans om samen te werken in de eerste- en tweedelijnszorg en daadwerkelijk impact te maken op de manier waarop zorg voor kwetsbare ouderen lokaal wordt georganiseerd, met mogelijke opschaling binnen Nederland.

Ben jij klaar om koers te zetten voor de komende jaren? Dan ontmoeten we je graag.

Wat jij meebrengt
Het gaat ons niet om vinkjes, maar om wie jij bent en wat jij meebrengt. Herken jij jezelf hierin?

Je bent een enthousiaste en gemotiveerde onderzoeker die open en nieuwsgierig is, creatief denkt en met doorzettingsvermogen en nauwkeurigheid te werk gaat. Je neemt initiatief, werkt punctueel en gedijt goed in teamverband. Met jouw organisatorische, communicatieve en sociale vaardigheden werk je effectief samen binnen een multidisciplinair team.

Verder neem je mee:
  • Een masterdiploma in geneeskunde, farmacie of aanverwante studies.
  • Uitstekende mondelinge en schriftelijke beheersing van zowel het Nederlands als het Engels (beiden op minimaal C1 level volgens CEFR).
  • Ervaring met het verzamelen en analyseren van kwalitatieve onderzoeksgegevens en het uitvoeren van statistische analyses is een pré.
  • Ervaring met dataverzameling en -beheer in Castor is een pré.
  • Ervaring met data-analyse (bijv. in R of SPSS) is een voordeel, maar geen vereiste. Motivatie om dit te leren is essentieel; er zijn trainingsmogelijkheden aanwezig.
  • Ervaring met patiëntencontact, bij voorkeur met ouderen, is een pré.
  • Een rijbewijs en beschikking over een auto zijn eveneens een pré.

Ben jij afgestudeerd en net basisarts en wil jij ook klinische ervaring opdoen, dan bestaat er ook de mogelijkheid tot participatie in het A(N)IOS dienstenrooster van de interne geneeskunde in het MUMC+.

Wat je van ons mag verwachten
Bij de Universiteit Maastricht werk je in een internationale, open en betrokken omgeving. We bieden:
  • Een jaarcontract (0.8-1.0 fte), bij wederzijdse tevredenheid wordt het contract verlengd met 2 jaar.
  • Een brutosalaris tussen €3.204 en €4.051 bruto per maand (bij een fulltime dienstverband van 38 uur per week), exclusief 8% vakantiegeld en een 8,3% eindejaarsuitkering.
  • 29 vakantiedagen (op basis van fulltime), vier extra vrije feestdagen, en de mogelijkheid om 12 extra dagen op te bouwen via compensatie-uren.
  • Flexibele werktijden, een thuiswerkvergoeding en hybride werken.
  • Vrijheid en ruimte om je werk zelfstandig in te richten en je eigen ideeën te ontwikkelen.
  • Een hechte community van collega’s waarmee je nauw samenwerkt.
  • Een goede pensioenregeling via het ABP, bedrijfsfitness en toegang tot een uitgebreid sportaanbod.
  • Een inspirerende werkomgeving in het hart van Europa.

Lees meer over de PhD-journey aan de Universiteit Maastricht, van de start van je onderzoek tot het afronden van je promotie en daarna.

Als promovendus word je automatisch ingeschreven bij een van onze Graduate schools. Lees meer over onze Graduate schools.

Over de Faculty of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences (FHML)
FHML werkt aan gezondheid in de breedste zin van het woord: van molecuul tot mens, en van gezondheidszorg tot preventie. We leiden zorgprofessionals en onderzoekers op binnen innovatieve onderwijsprogramma’s, en doen baanbrekend onderzoek op het gebied van gezondheid en welzijn. Als onderdeel van het Maastricht UMC+ (MUMC+) vormt onze internationale en interdisciplinaire gemeenschap een unieke samenwerking tussen universiteit en academisch ziekenhuis, waar onderwijs, onderzoek en zorg samenkomen.

Nieuwsgierig geworden?
Wil je meer weten over deze functie of over werken bij onze universiteit? Neem contact op met Fabienne Magdelijns via fabienne.magdelijns@mumc.nl. De einddatum van de publicatie is 15 November 2026.

Upload je cv en motivatiebrief. Licht in je motivatiebrief toe waarom je een PhD wilt doen, wat je aanspreekt in dit onderzoeksonderwerp en hoe de functie aansluit bij jouw achtergrond en ervaring.

De eerste sollicitatiegesprekken vinden bij voorkeur plaats op vrijdag 6 november 2026.

Solliciteer via onderstaande knop. We hopen je snel te leren kennen!

Over de Universiteit Maastricht
Aan de Universiteit Maastricht zoeken we samen naar antwoorden waarmee we de wereld vooruithelpen. Dat doen we samen met 23.300 studenten en 5.400 medewerkers, verspreid over 5 steden in de regio, 6 faculteiten en ruim 70 onderzoeksinstituten in de Euregio. Hier krijg je de ruimte om grenzen te verleggen en nieuwe kansen te ontdekken; voor jezelf en voor de wereld om je heen. Want echte antwoorden vinden we samen.

De vacature staat open voor interne- en externe kandidaten. Bij gelijke geschiktheid hebben interne kandidaten voorrang.

Bij Maastricht University nemen we graag zelf contact op met potentiële kandidaten. We vragen daarom vriendelijk om geen acquisitie of aanbiedingen van bureaus of tussenpersonen.

Universiteit Maastricht zet zich in voor het bevorderen en behouden van een diverse en inclusieve gemeenschap. Wij geloven dat diversiteit in onze medewerkers- en studentenpopulatie bijdraagt aan de kwaliteit van onderzoek en onderwijs aan de UM. Dit willen we mogelijk maken door middel van inclusief beleid en innovatieve projecten in samenwerking met studenten en medewerkers. We moedigen je aan om voor deze functie te solliciteren.

jobs.title: PhD Position in Accountable and Responsible AI
jobs.description_html:
Are you eager to conduct high-impact research spanning computer science, economics, law, and the creative industry—while living in Amsterdam, a dynamic city renowned for its high-quality life and its thriving AI and creative sectors?

Join Us!
A fully funded four-year Ph.D. position is available in the Complex Cyber Infrastructure research group at the University of Amsterdam.

As Artificial Intelligence (AI) becomes deeply embedded in our society, the urgency to warrant its responsible and accountable use is increasing. Examples include the control that creative industry actors need to manifest when using AI pipelines in the (moving) image industry.

This PhD project aims to focus on the emerging field of Accountable and Responsible AI, with the goal of advancing knowledge and practice at the intersection of AI research, creative industry practices, and societal regulatory expectations. Two projects underpin this position: SafeGenAI – a creative industry endeavour to enable creative industry actors to safely use GenAI tools; and LLM4LM – a large consortium addressing the legal-tech challenges in cross-organisational multi-domain agentic solutions. The candidate will not only have a chance to contribute to shaping the next generation AI systems within the creative industry and logistics practices, but also potentially to design more transparent, fair, and compliant ones with evolving societal and regulatory expectations.

The successful candidate will be embedded in a team that will help transfer fundamental research results into the creative industry and legal practices, respectively. Moreover, they will be working closely with the supervision team, as well as the other PhD students and postdocs in the research group.

This is what you will do
In this context, you will investigate the following key challenges:
  • Opacity in GenAI inferencing: How can the inferencing and reasoning processes of GenAI systems be made sufficiently transparent and traceable to support accountability in high-stakes professional contexts?
  • AI legal compliance-by-design: How can GenAI systems be built to satisfy the requirements of the regulations such as the EU AI Act — including transparency, human oversight, and risk management — while remaining practically useful in domain-specific workflows?
  • SMEs lack the expertise to navigate complex regulatory environments: How can domain-specific structured knowledge be integrated into GenAI systems to ground their outputs, reduce hallucination, and support trustworthy decision for non-expert users?

What we ask of you
Your experience and profile:
  • MSc in CS, AI or a closely related field.
  • Strong interest in Interest in finance and financial services is a plus.; previous experience in these fields is a plus.
  • Enthusiasm for the research process: studying research papers, solving complex problems, applying creative thinking, evaluation, reflection and disseminating findings via writing and oral presentations.
  • The ability to critically analyse abstract models as well as concrete implementations.
  • The ability to work individually as well as effectively in a team
  • Fluency in written and spoken English

This is what we offer you
A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is as soon as possible. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students.

The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week and dependent on relevant experience, ranges between € 3,204 to € 4,051 (scale P). This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile PhD Candidate is applicable.. A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants. The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable.

We also have an extensive secondary benefits package.

You will work in this team
The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000, as well as 1,800 members of staff working in education, research or support services. Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, be it elementary particles, the birth of the universe or the functioning of the brain.

The mission of the Informatics Institute (IvI) is to perform curiosity-driven and use-inspired fundamental research in Computer Science. The main research themes are Artificial Intelligence, Computational Science and Systems and Network Engineering. Our research involves complex information systems at large, with a focus on collaborative, data driven, computational and intelligent systems, all with a strong interactive component.

The Complex Cyber Infrastructure (CCI) group is part of the Informatics Institute at the University of Amsterdam. CCI focuses on the complexity of human-made systems on all scales. Cyber Infrastructure is rapidly evolving from relatively simple fixed components to programmable and virtualized objects with many degrees of freedom, owned, operated and governed by different entities in multiple administrative domains interacting on the Internet. Harnessing this complexity in a transparent, trustable way for safe and secure data processing is a major research topic that defines the focus of CCI research. The challenges are addressed by combining methods and results from research into sustainable and sovereign distributed data processing, programmable networks, policy reasoning and normative control, and software (language) engineering.

Want to know more about our organisation? Read more about working at the University of Amsterdam.

jobs.title: PhD Candidate in Network Modelling for Food Safety and Regulatory Decision-Making
jobs.description_html:
Job description

Maastricht University’s School of Business and Economics, in collaboration with Sciensano, the Belgian institute for health and a leading public-health research organisation, is looking for a PhD candidate in Network Modelling for Food Safety and Regulatory Decision-Making.

Sciensano brings established expertise in food safety, food contaminants, exposure assessment, risk analysis, and scientific evidence generation for public authorities. The collaboration connects methodological research at Maastricht University with Sciensano’s policy-facing work supporting food safety assessment and risk-manager decision-making at Belgian and European levels.

The position focuses on the development of new multi-layer network modelling approaches for structured food-safety data. The aim is to support evidence generation for contaminant risk assessment, food safety monitoring, and regulatory decision-making.

The PhD candidate will conduct original methodological research while working in close connection with public-health and regulatory questions. The project offers a distinctive opportunity to develop rigorous computational models in a setting where scientific evidence, regulatory judgement, and societal impact are closely connected.

The project
This PhD project develops new multi-layer network modelling approaches for structured food-safety data. The project addresses an open methodological challenge: how to specify, estimate, validate, and interpret network models that can support evidence generation for contaminant risk assessment and regulatory decision-making.

The project focuses on the development of network-based models for analysing complex relationships in food safety data, including information relevant to contaminants, consumption patterns, exposure assessment, and regulatory prioritisation. The methodological contribution lies in developing models suited to this type of heterogeneous and relational data, rather than simply applying existing algorithms to a new domain.

The work builds on Sciensano’s established activities in food safety, exposure assessment, and contaminant risk analysis. Sciensano’s work supports science-based policy, legislation, and decision-making by risk managers at Belgian and European levels. This collaboration gives the project a strong societal and institutional grounding, while preserving a clear methodological research ambition.

The precise modelling choices and empirical focus will be developed as part of the PhD trajectory, in close dialogue with the supervisory team and Sciensano researchers. The candidate will be supervised by a team from Maastricht University’s School of Business and Economics and Sciensano, combining SBE’s methodological expertise with Sciensano’s expertise in food safety, while drawing on both institutions’ experience with regulatory decision-making.

The candidate will:
  • develop new network modelling approaches for structured food-safety data;
  • work on model specification, estimation, validation, interpretation, uncertainty assessment, and robustness analysis;
  • analyse heterogeneous data relevant to food safety, contaminants, consumption patterns, exposure assessment, and regulatory decision-making;
  • investigate how network models can support contaminant risk assessment, monitoring prioritisation, and evidence generation for food safety authorities;
  • implement computational methods in reproducible research workflows;
  • publish research in international peer-reviewed journals and present findings at academic conferences;
  • collaborate with researchers from Maastricht University, Sciensano, and relevant academic or policy-facing partners;
  • complete a doctoral dissertation within the agreed timeframe.

Candidate profile
We are looking for a candidate with a strong quantitative and computational background who is motivated to develop rigorous modelling approaches for societally relevant regulatory questions.

The candidate should have:
  • a completed or near-completed master’s degree in a relevant field, such as computer science, data science, applied mathematics, statistics, econometrics, operations research, physics, computational social science, systems science, or a related quantitative discipline;
  • demonstrated experience with programming for data analysis or computational modelling, preferably in Python, R, Julia, or a comparable language, and willingness to further develop skills in writing reproducible, modular, and maintainable research code;
  • a foundation in at least one relevant methodological area, such as network modelling, statistical learning, machine learning, probabilistic modelling, complex systems, or computational modelling, together with the ability and motivation to develop the specialised network-modelling expertise required for the project;
  • an interest in structured, relational, and heterogeneous data;
  • the ability to formulate research questions with both methodological and applied relevance;
  • strong analytical skills and the capacity to work independently;
  • strong written and spoken English communication skills, preferably at C1 level or higher according to the CEFR, with the ability to explain technical concepts to interdisciplinary academic, public-health, and policy-facing audiences;
  • ability and willingness to work in an interdisciplinary environment involving methodological, food-safety, public-health, and regulatory expertise.

Experience with food safety, contaminant risk assessment, exposure assessment, nutrition, toxicology, public health, or regulatory science is welcome but not required. Domain-specific knowledge can be developed during the project in collaboration with Sciensano. A strong technical profile and an interest in food safety decision-making are more important.

The starting date is negotiable, but ideally the position would start in January 2027.

Employment conditions
At Maastricht University, the PhD candidate will work in an international, open, and engaged academic environment. The position offers:
  • a 18-month contract, 1.0 FTE, with the prospect of a 2,5 year extension based on mutual satisfaction;
  • a gross monthly salary between €3,204 and €4,051, based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week;
  • 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus;
  • 29 vacation days, based on full-time employment, four additional days off, and the possibility to accrue up to 12 extra days through compensation hours;
  • flexible working hours, a home office allowance, and the option to work from home;
  • supervision by researchers from Maastricht University and Sciensano;
  • the opportunity to develop new methodology in network modelling, computational analysis, and structured food-safety data;
  • close collaboration with Sciensano, a public-health institute with established expertise in food safety, exposure assessment, contaminant risk analysis, and scientific evidence generation for public authorities;
  • access to doctoral training, research seminars, methodological expertise, and professional-development opportunities;
  • opportunities to publish in international journals and present at academic conferences;
  • an interdisciplinary research environment combining methodological rigour with public-health and regulatory relevance;
  • a solid pension plan via ABP, company fitness schemes, and access to various university sports facilities;
  • an inspiring work environment in the heart of Europe.

Find out more about the PhD journey at Maastricht University, from starting your research to completing your PhD and beyond.

As a PhD candidate, you will be automatically enrolled in one of our Graduate Schools. Find out more about our Graduate Schools.

Further information
For questions about the scientific content of the project, the research environment, or the collaboration between Maastricht University and Sciensano, please contact:
  • Rui Jorge Almeida via rj.almeida@maastrichtuniversity.nl
  • Mirjana Andjelkovic via Mirjana.Andjelkovic@sciensano.be

For questions about the application procedure or employment conditions, please contact:
  • Miranda Van den Beuken via miranda.vandenbeuken@maastrichtuniversity.nl

Application procedure
Applications should include:
  • a motivation letter describing the candidate’s interest in the position and fit with the project;
  • a curriculum vitae;
  • transcripts or a list of completed courses and grades;
  • a writing sample, such as a master’s thesis, research paper, or technical report;
  • if available, examples of programming, modelling, or data-analysis work;
  • the names and contact details of at least two academic referees.

In the motivation letter, candidates are encouraged to explain how their methodological background could contribute to the development of multi-layer network models for food safety and regulatory decision-making. Prior experience in food safety or public health is not required, but candidates should be willing to engage with domain experts and policy-facing research questions.

Applications should be submitted no later than 18 November 2026.

Please note that incomplete applications will not be considered. The vacancy is open for internal and external candidates. In case of equal qualifications, internal candidates will be prioritised.

At Maastricht University, we prefer to contact potential candidates directly. We therefore kindly ask that no agencies or intermediaries submit offers or approaches.

Apply now via the button below. We look forward to getting to know you!

About the School of Business and Economics (SBE)
SBE is an international faculty for economics, business, and policy. We combine academic depth with societal engagement. Our education is small-scale and interactive. jobs.title: PhD in Energy-Efficient Sensors and Computing Hardware from 2D Materials
jobs.description_html:
Are you eager to shape the next generation of chips using atomically thin materials? In this PhD position, you will develop 2D nanomaterials and devices for more energy-efficient sensing and computing. The project will be undertaken within the NanoComputing Research Lab in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e), at the heart of Europe’s leading semiconductor region.

Information
In this PhD position, you will investigate 2D materials as a platform for next-generation sensing and computing devices. You will develop growth recipes for 2D materials and fabricate and characterize devices that could contribute to emerging energy efficient brain-inspired computing hardware.

What you'll contribute to
Specifically, you will:
  • develop metal-organic chemical vapour deposition (MOCVD) growth recipes for large-area 2D materials, such as MoS₂ and WSe₂, with controlled defect densities;
  • optimize transfer processes to integrate the grown 2D materials onto target device substrates, enabling heterogeneous integration;
  • develop scalable fabrication processes in the TU/e cleanroom (NanoLab@TU/e) for device arrays, including sensors and transistors;
  • engineer metal–semiconductor and dielectric interfaces to improve device performance;
  • characterize materials and devices, and work with circuit designers to link material properties to device and circuit performance;
  • publish your results in leading journals and present them at international conferences;
  • supervise Bachelor’s and Master’s student projects.

Your research environment
You will join the NanoComputing Research Lab (NanoComputing Research Lab), in the Integrated Circuits group of the Department of Electrical Engineering at TU/e. You will be supervised by Dr. Abhishek Singh Dahiya (project leader) and Prof. Aida Todri-Sanial. You will have access to TU/e’s state-of-the-art cleanroom and characterization facilities.

What we're looking for
A master’s degree in electrical engineering, nanotechnology, or a related field, with a solid foundation in semiconductor materials and device physics, and prior experience in the growth of nanomaterials (preferably 2D materials using CVD), nanofabrication processes such as atomic layer deposition, lithography, etching etc., and 2D material transfer process.

jobs.title: PhD Position in ML-Based Interpretation of Geophysical Legacy Data for Mineral Exploration
jobs.description_html:
Develop and test new methods for deep exploration of sediment-hosted copper systems by integrating legacy seismic and well-log data with basin modelling, geochemistry and machine learning.

Job description
We are looking for a PhD candidate who is keen to explore how legacy seismic and well-log data acquired for petroleum exploration can be transformed into a new resource for deep mineral exploration. The candidate will combine quantitative geophysical interpretation, basin modelling and machine learning to investigate a challenging target: the thin Kupferschiefer horizon buried beneath the Netherlands and the North Sea.

The Dutch subsurface offers an exceptional dataset of more than 6,000 wells, including approximately 1,700 in which the Kupferschiefer has been identified, together with extensive high-quality 2D and 3D seismic reflection data and available cores. Yet these data were acquired and interpreted for hydrocarbon exploration. Recognizing and mapping a horizon a few metres thick at kilometers depth, and identifying features associated with its mineral potential, requires methods that can extract information across datasets with very different resolution, coverage and physical meaning.

The goal of this PhD project is to develop an integrated methodology for characterizing the Kupferschiefer and its geological context. You will analyse well logs to identify the target horizon and extrapolate it to wells where it has not yet been recognized. You will use seismic data for cross-well correlation and improved spatial characterization, and basin analysis to investigate the roles of stratigraphy, faulting and basin evolution. Geological, petrophysical, geochemical and mineralogical information will be integrated to identify characteristics and fingerprints associated with copper mineralization.

Machine learning will be an important part of this methodological development. You will establish robust and interpretable baseline models for well-log analysis and investigate approaches designed for sequential data, including convolutional and transformer-based models. You will also contribute to multimodal methods that combine seismic, well-log, geological and geochemical information while incorporating geological knowledge and physical constraints. A postdoctoral researcher will work alongside you for one year, focusing primarily on advanced multimodal and physics-informed machine-learning developments.

The research is part of the EU-funded INTELLIGENT project. Results from the Dutch basin will be combined with complementary studies by other groups working on the Kupferschiefer and related systems to develop a regional-scale mineral-system model and transferable exploration workflows. Your multidisciplinary research work will be carried out within the Applied Geophysics and Petrophysics Section and the Resource Engineering Section of GSE at TU Delft. Through close collaboration with TNO, the National Materials Observatory and partners from universities, geological surveys, research institutes and industry across Europe, you will test new methodological ideas within an international network and against a real, societally relevant exploration challenge.

Job requirements
Being creative and independent, you have the ability to conduct independent research and collaborate across geoscience, engineering and data-science disciplines.

You also have:
  • An MSc degree in geophysics, geology, earth sciences, geological or petroleum engineering, or a closely related discipline.
  • Interest in applied geophysics and resource exploration and machine learning methods.
  • Experience in scientific programming (preferably Python or Matlab).
  • Good writing and communication skills.

Experience in one or more of the fields below is considered an advantage:
  • Basin analysis, basin modelling or sedimentary-basin evolution.
  • Quantitative interpretation of seismic reflection data and well logs.
  • Petrophysics, low temperature geochemistry and mineralogy.
  • Machine Learning (deep learning and/or statistical learning methods).

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.

For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.

At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.

Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences
The Faculty of Civil Engineering & Geosciences (CEG) is committed to outstanding international research and education in the field of civil engineering, applied earth sciences, traffic and transport, water technology, and delta technology. Our research feeds into our educational programmes and covers societal challenges such as climate change, energy transition, resource availability, urbanisation and clean water. Our research projects are conducted in close cooperation with a wide range of research institutions. CEG is convinced of the importance of open science and supports its scientists in integrating open science in their research practice. The Faculty of CEG comprises 28 research groups in the following seven departments: Materials Mechanics Management & Design, Engineering Structures, Geoscience and Engineering, Geoscience and Remote Sensing, Transport & Planning, Hydraulic Engineering and Water Management.

Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Civil Engineering & Geosciences.

Conditions of employment
Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met.

Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%.

As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills.

The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged.

In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. Additional information

jobs.title: Promovendus
jobs.description_html:
In de zorg wordt elke dag een grote hoeveelheid ongebruikte medicijnen weggegooid. Dat is zonde, het is niet duurzaam en het kost onnodig veel geld. Er zijn verschillende redenen waarom dit gebeurt. De farmaceutische keten is vooral lineair ingericht: van producent via apotheek naar patiënt, en als het niet gebruikt wordt de afvalbak in. Redenen voor het niet gebruiken van medicatie zijn divers. Ook wet- en regelgeving maken het lastig om over te stappen op een circulaire werkwijze. Daarnaast weten we nog onvoldoende onder welke kwaliteitscondities circulair medicijngebruik mogelijk is, binnen welke wettelijke kaders het is toegestaan en hoe de bekostiging van de keten verspilling in stand houdt of juist kan helpen voorkomen.

Er zijn dus meerdere elementen die de transformatie naar duurzaam medicijngebruik in de praktijk tegenhouden. In het REMARK-onderzoek brengen we deze elementen in kaart en zoeken we naar manieren om wél circulair met medicijnen om te gaan, zodat verspilling wordt voorkomen. In dit promotieonderzoek breng je in kaart binnen welke juridische, kwaliteits- en financiële kaders circulair medicijngebruik mogelijk is. Zo draag je direct bij aan de transformatie naar duurzame zorg.

Projectomschrijving
REMARK is een uniek project waarin een breed consortium samenwerkt aan de transformatie naar duurzame zorg. Het is een samenwerking tussen Tilburg University, de Technische Universiteit Eindhoven, Erasmus Universiteit, samen met vele andere consortiumpartners, bijvoorbeeld zorginstellingen, apotheken, ondernemers en ketenpartijen.

Het onderzoek richt zich op de langdurige zorg, waaronder verpleeghuizen en langdurige psychiatrie. In deze context is nog weinig onderzoek gedaan, terwijl er juist veel impact te behalen is door de grote volumes van medicatie die wordt weggegooid.

Promotietraject: regelgeving, kwaliteit en financiering van de farmaceutische keten

In dit promotietraject onderzoek je welke stappen een medicijn doorloopt tot het bij de cliënt in een zorginstelling terechtkomt, en welke regels, kwaliteitseisen en geldstromen daarbij een rol spelen. Vervolgens onderzoek je onder welke voorwaarden deze keten circulair kan worden ingericht. Je werkt aan samenhangende deelstudies:

  • het in kaart brengen van de wet- en regelgeving rondom de farmaceutische keten in de langdurige zorg, op nationaal en Europees niveau, en het identificeren van de juridische ruimte en knelpunten voor het hergebruik van medicijnen;
  • het vaststellen van de kwaliteits- en veiligheidscondities waaronder ongebruikte medicijnen verantwoord opnieuw kunnen worden uitgegeven, bijvoorbeeld rond bewaarcondities, verpakking, houdbaarheid en traceerbaarheid;
  • het analyseren van de financiering en bekostiging van de keten: welke geldstromen en prikkels houden verspilling in stand, en welke bekostigingsmodellen maken circulair werken mogelijk;
  • het samen met zorginstellingen, apotheken en andere ketenpartners vertalen van deze inzichten naar oplossingen die de circulaire logistieke farmaceutische keten verbeteren.
  • Het samen met alle stakeholders uittesten in de praktijk van de oplossingen.

Zo is dit promotietraject niet alleen theoretisch werk. Je duikt echt de praktijk in en onderzoekt wat wel werkt en wat niet en waarom.

Jouw functie
Als promovendus krijg je de ruimte om wetenschappelijke diepgang te combineren met maatschappelijke impact. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor het opzetten en uitvoeren van de deelstudies binnen jouw promotietraject. Je werkt nauw samen met de andere REMARK-promovendi, met de onderzoekers van de universiteiten en met de consortiumpartners.

Je combineert verschillende methoden, zoals documentanalyse van wet- en regelgeving en beleid, ketenanalyses, interviews en expertsessies met bijvoorbeeld apothekers, zorgprofessionals, toezichthouders, zorgkantoren en zorgverzekeraars, en de evaluatie van praktijkpilots. Je vertaalt je onderzoeksbevindingen naar wetenschappelijke publicaties, die uiteindelijk samenkomen in een proefschrift. Daarnaast draag je bij aan kennisverspreiding naar de praktijk en het beleid, en presenteer je jouw resultaten op nationale en internationale congressen.

Je standplaats is Tilburg. De betrokken organisaties zitten op verschillende plekken in Nederland, waardoor je regelmatig op locatie werkt. Dat maakt de functie afwisselend en dynamisch.

Tranzo verzorgt de mastertrack Health, Wellbeing & Society en de mastertrack Sociaal Werk, in de Sociologie master. Er wordt van alle Tranzo medewerkers verwacht dat men een bijdrage levert aan het onderwijs, bijvoorbeeld in de vorm van verzorgen werkgroepen/colleges of nakijkwerk. Afspraken hierover worden met de leidinggevende gemaakt.

jobs.title: PhD Position: Biodiversity for Nature-Inclusive Dairy Farming
jobs.description_html:
In this PhD position, you will develop integrated and innovative biodiversity monitoring and data analysis techniques to aid in the decision-making of businesses within the dairy sector for the benefit of biodiversity.

Biodiversity recovery is essential to sustain resilient food systems, robust businesses and healthy societies. A transition to a more nature-inclusive dairy sector in the Netherlands would be pivotal to biodiversity recovery, because of its influence in shaping landscapes through land use and management, and because of its socio-economic relevance.

To properly assess the suitability and effectiveness of key performance indicators and the effects of management practices on local biodiversity, it is crucial to monitor, for example, breeding birds, bats, insect communities and soil life (depending on the KPI).

By adapting and developing biomonitoring techniques programmes at dairy farms that are in line with long-running or recently developed monitoring schemes, you will utilise the full potential of datasets and methods to quantify biodiversity gains resulting from nature-inclusive farming as well as the potential for further biodiversity recovery. Novel instruments such as DIOPSIS smart insect cameras, LED buckets and bat loggers generate huge amounts of biodiversity data from across the Netherlands and can be used to detect and identify biodiversity automatically.

National schemes like the breeding bird monitoring project, the butterfly monitoring scheme and the dragon fly monitoring scheme (standardised and coordinated by NGOs such as Sovon and Dutch Butterfly Conservation, and powered by thousands of citizen scientists) generate standardised long-term trends based on thousands of plots around the country. You will design novel, integrated analyses to quantify the effects on biodiversity from existing and new data while accounting for factors such as observers' bias, weather and surrounding landscape configuration.

In this project you will:
  1. Bring coherence across the diverse monitoring systems and KPI developed so far and adapt sets of KPI's suited to peat soils.
  2. Document the relationships between different nature-inclusive measures taken by heterogeneous farm types, and the different aspects of biodiversity and ecosystem services considered. The precise type of monitoring and the number and locations of monitoring points will be decided in collaboration with stakeholders.
  3. Further develop effective and integrated monitoring to guide decision-making in businesses and develop reward schemes.

Your teaching load may be up to 10% of your working time.

Would you like to learn more about what it’s like to pursue a PhD at Radboud University? Visit the page about working as a PhD candidate.

jobs.title: PhD Candidate: Psychosocial, Environmental and Economical Impact in Non-Ischemic Cardiomyopathies
jobs.description_html:
Welcome to Maastricht University!

How does cardiomyopathy (heart failure in young adults) affect patients beyond their physical health? And how can we better understand how psychosocial and environmental factors, such as stress, obesity and physical activity, influence the disease process and patients’ quality of life and mental well-being? As a PhD candidate, you will use Health Technology Assessment (HTA) methods to study the psychosocial and economic impact of cardiomyopathy-related complications as well as the role of psychosocial and environmental factors in the disease process, and contribute to evidence on the value and cost-effectiveness of healthcare strategies.

PhD Candidate: Psychosocial, Environmental and Related Economical Impact in Non-Ischemic Cardiomyopathies (Heart Failure in Young Adults)
  • Our goal: The goal of this research is to understand how psychosocial and environmental factors influence the cardiomyopathy disease process and related biological changes in the heart, as well as their impact on quality of life, mental well-being and societal burden in young patients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. By combining clinical phenotyping, questionnaires, patient-reported outcomes, healthcare use, employment and cost data, the project aims to link these factors and biological and clinical findings to better understand, detect, prevent or treat cardiomyopathy complications.
  • Your colleagues & research context: You will join the Heart Failure Research team of Prof. dr. Stephane Heymans at CARIM and Maastricht UMC+ and work within a large Dutch research consortium. You will collaborate with the team of Prof. dr. Jan Y. Verbakel at KU Leuven, Department of Public Health and Primary Care, and work closely with the HTA and health economics group at KU Leuven. The research uses a prospective cohort, biobank and omics of more than 1,300 cardiomyopathy patients. You will be based in Maastricht (CARIM / Maastricht UMC+) and make regular working visits to Leuven. Supervision will take place by both Dr. Stephane Heymans and dr. Verbakel.

The project focuses on Health Technology Assessment (HTA) and on understanding the psychosocial and economic impact of cardiomyopathy-related complications. An important part of the research is to examine how psychosocial and environmental factors, including factors such as stress, obesity and physical activity, are related to the cardiomyopathy disease process and biological changes in the heart. Using a prospective cohort, biobank and omics, you will integrate clinical phenotyping, questionnaires, patient-reported outcomes, biosamples and multi-omics to study cardiomyopathy and associated psychosocial, economical, environmental and behaviourial conditions.

You will link these data to healthcare use, cost, work, quality of life, mental well-being, patient preferences and societal burden to generate evidence for HTA and cost-effectiveness analyses.You will have the freedom to identify their original projects, e.g. where biological findings in the heart (e.g. RNA/protein data) can be linked to psychosocial and environmental factors, as part of the gene-environmental interactions paradigm.

What you do
  • Quantify the psychosocial and economic impact of cardiomyopathy complications using questionnaires, patient-reported outcomes, healthcare use, employment and cost data.
  • Investigate how psychosocial and environmental factors, such as stress, obesity and physical activity, may influence the cardiomyopathy disease process and related biological changes in the heart.
  • Evaluate the value and cost-effectiveness of strategies to detect, prevent or treat cardiomyopathy-related complications in patients with cardiomyopathy, incorporating patient preferences and societal impact.
  • Where relevant and if time allows, and in close collaboration with the molecular research team, translate selected cohort findings into patient-derived iPSC or experimental animal models.

Are you ready to set the course for the years ahead? Then we’d love to meet you.

What you bring
We’re not looking for checkboxes; we’re interested in who you are and what you bring. Do you recognize yourself in this?

You bring strong analytical and communication skills and enjoy working in a multidisciplinary team. You are motivated to contribute to research at the intersection of clinical, psychosocial and economic perspectives.

  • You have an interest in and/or experience with Health Technology Assessment (HTA), with focus on psychosocial and related economic impact of cardiomyopathy on patients’ lives, including quality of life and patient-reported outcomes.
  • You are familiar with the Northern European and/or Dutch healthcare system.
  • You have experience with, or are willing to learn, statistical software such as R or Stata.
  • You have an excellent command of English and Dutch, both written and spoken, at minimum C1 level (CEFR).

  • A gross monthly salary between € 3.204 and € 4.051 (based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week). 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus.

jobs.title: PhD in Physics-informed generative AI for dynamic cardiac MRI
jobs.description_html:
Do you want to make cardiac MRI safer for patients and the environment? Join PRIMA-CMR, a EuroTech Universities Alliance project between TU/e and the Technical University of Munich (TUM) and help to develop trustworthy generative AI that makes it possible to scan with far less contrast agent.

Information
Cardiac MRI gives unmatched insight into heart disease, but some of its most important exams depend on gadolinium-based contrast agents. Gadolinium can build up in the body, cannot be given to all patients, and is now an environmental pollutant. A large reduction in the dose would make cardiac MRI safer and available to more patients. At low doses, however, the images no longer contain enough signal for a reliable diagnosis. Current AI methods can make images that look realistic, but they cannot guarantee that what they show is real.

We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate to develop new generative AI methods that recover diagnostic information from low-dose cardiac MRI in a reliable and trustworthy way. Your work will combine knowledge of MR imaging physics, patient-specific clinical information, and uncertainty quantification. The aim is a model whose outputs clinicians can trust, and which tells them when it is not certain. You will validate the methods on real clinical data together with our clinical partners.

This PhD position is part of PRIMA-CMR, a collaborative project within the EuroTech Universities Alliance programme. You will be based at TU/e and spend six months at TUM in the group of prof. Julia Schnabel, which is a world leader in generative and multimodal AI. You will also work with international clinical and academic partners across Europe. This position is embedded in the Medical Image Analysis group, Department of Biomedical Engineering, TU/e. You will be supervised by dr. Cian Scannell, and co-supervised by prof. Julia Schnabel (TUM).

jobs.title: PhD Candidate in Complex Networks
jobs.description_html:
The Mathematical Institute (MI) of Leiden University and the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science (LIACS) are looking for a PhD Candidate in Complex Networks to commence at the earliest possible date and no later than April 2027.

The project investigates how structural properties observed in complex networks can be understood and modeled using mathematically tractable network models. The research will combine theoretical modeling with computational and data-driven investigation of real-world networks, with a particular emphasis on understanding how features such as spatial structure, clustering, heterogeneity, and connectivity shape network behavior.

Possible research directions include, but are not limited to, network science, spatial network modeling, random graph models, and data-driven methods for network analysis. We welcome candidates with an interest in real-world network data as well as in developing and analyzing mathematical models of complex networks. The precise balance between theoretical, computational, and data-driven work will depend on the candidate’s background and interests.

The position will be co-supervised by dr. Moritz Otto (MI) and dr. Akrati Saxena (LIACS). Michel Mandjes (MI) will act as promotor. Academic excellence is the main selection criterion.

What you will do
  • Conducting complex networks research at the intersection of mathematics and computer science.
  • Writing a publication-based PhD thesis.
  • Engaging in a limited number of teaching and supervision activities.

Where you will work
The PhD candidate will be employed at the Mathematical Institute and also be affiliated with the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science and AI (LIACS). In particular, the candidate will become part of the Leiden AlFa (Algorithmic Fairness: https://alfa.liacs.nl) group and the Probability research group, and collaborate closely with the Network Science group.
Both the research groups and the institutes are highly international and feature a mix of disciplinary and cultural backgrounds. There are plenty of additional opportunities for other types of interaction and collaboration, for example, at the Faculty of Science through the Leiden Complex Networks Network (LCN2) and nationally through the Dutch Network Science Society.

The Mathematical Institute focuses on four key research themes: Algebra, Geometry, and Number Theory; Analysis and Dynamical Systems; Probability; and Statistics and Data Science. There is extensive collaboration between these themes. For more information about the Mathematical Institute, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science/mathematics.
LIACS is one of the leading computer science departments in the Netherlands. We strive for excellence in a supportive institute where academic achievement, enjoyment, and diversity go hand in hand. For more information about LIACS, visit our website: http://www.cs.leiden.edu

What you bring
  • A university degree* in mathematics, computer science or a closely related field.

  • Programming experience, preferably in Python, and willingness to develop strong computational skills (please mention your level of proficiency and knowledge of other programming languages in your CV).
  • Strong motivation for academic research.
  • Good English communication skills.

jobs.title: PhD position: Bacterial packaging of biocatalytic nanofactories
jobs.description_html:
What you will do
With the recent rapid progress in synthetic cells, sometimes known as artificial cells, the toolbox for liposome-encapsulated biocatalyst has massively expanded, creating complex systems that can act as ‘chemical nanofactories’ for biocatalytic cascade reactions. In this PhD project, you will optimise, apply and exploit a new technology in which biocatalysts are ‘packaged’ and confined in lipid vesicles during bacterial expression, which not only massively enriches biocatalyst yields, but also creates a ready-to-go liposome-encapsulated systems.

About the project
This project is a good match if:
  • you are interested in the expression, characterisation and engineering of biocatalysts.
  • you like working in a multidisciplinary team.
  • you are interested in contributing to the field of Synthetic Cells and biotechnology.

What you bring

  • has a Master’s degree in Life Sciences and Technology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, or a related discipline
  • has experience in cloning, expression, purification and characterisation of biocatalysts, and preferably also in the preparation and analysis of lipid vesicles.
  • has a strong interest in structure-function relationship of enzymes, with proven excellent technical experimental and analytical skills and ability to work independently.
  • has a good proficiency in (scientific) English, and excellent communication skills.
  • feels comfortable working in a collaborative environment.
