jobs.title: PhD Position Energy Data Sharing for City-Level Policy Making Using Digital Twins
jobs.description_html:
Job description

The Delft University of Technology is hiring a doctoral candidate on the subject of "Energy data sharing for city-level policy making using digital twins". The PhD position is a part of the FEDERATE NWO project.

Municipal policy makers are making city decarbonization and sustainability policies using digital twins that rely on fragmented, partial and incomplete data. The data mostly comes from public sources, such as CBS (Central Bureau for Statistics) and through time consuming and costly data collection initiatives initiated by municipalities. However, this is insufficient to provide a high-resolution picture that the policy makers need. In 2026, a new Energy Law enacted in the Netherlands that provisions easier energy data sharing among different parties including municipalities and their citizens and local companies. Although it unlocks new possibilities of data sharing among these actors, this law is yet to become operationalized in the data sharing processes of municipalities.

This PhD research project will investigate data sharing architectures for energy data sharing between citizens, local companies and municipalities, compatible with digital twins that municipalities use. The work involves designing of ontologies and knowledge graphs and their integration with digital twins of municipalities and other tools that could be used for data collection from citizens and companies. This is a four-year doctoral appointment. You will be supervised by Dr. Milos Cvetkovic. You will be a member of the section Intelligent Electrical Power Grids in the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, and Computer Science. The project will offer opportunities to collaborate with industrial partners but also with academics from other disciplines. Within the team, we strive to develop methods that are mathematically rigorous and have near-term application potential. We are strong supporters of open science (publishing, source code, data). You will also be expected to assist in teaching activities (student supervision, labs) related to your subject area.

About the department

The research in the Department of Electrical Sustainable Energy is inspired by the technical, scientific, and societal challenges originating from the transition toward a more sustainable society and focuses on three areas:
  • DC Systems, Energy Conversion and Storage (DCE&S)
  • Photovoltaic Materials and Devices (PVMD)
  • Intelligent Electrical Power Grids (IEPG)
  • High Voltage Technologies (HVT)

The department provides expertise across the entire energy system chain and hosts extensive research facilities, including high-voltage testing laboratories, DC grids testing environments, and large-scale RTDS infrastructure for real-time simulation of future electrical power systems, AC/DC protection, and wide-area monitoring and protection.

The Intelligent Electrical Power Grids (IEPG) group, headed by Prof. Peter Palensky, focuses on the future evolution of electrical power systems. The group develops advanced power technologies and intelligent control approaches to enable reliable, efficient, stable, affordable, and sustainable energy systems with increasing levels of distributed and renewable generation.

Job requirements
We are looking for a candidate that already has an MSc degree in Computer Science, Electricical Engineering, Mathematics, or a similar field. They have demonstrated working proficiency in programming. They have excellent analytical skills and solid basis in one or more of the following: knowledge graphs, knowledge representation, data engineering, model-driven software engineering, data space architectures, etc. Idealy, they have already demonstrated high inclination towards modeling of socio-technical systems and processes, and they have worked in large projects with many partners. The ideal candidate is open minded, curious and creative.

The PhD will develop new science, write scientific papers and publish them in journals and conferences, work on deliverables of the FEDERATE project, attend project meetings and work alongside project partners, complete the graduate school requirements of TU Delft and write the PhD dissertation by the end of the project.

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Delft University of Technology is built on strong foundations. As creators of the world-famous Dutch waterworks and pioneers in biotech, TU Delft is a top international university combining science, engineering and design. It delivers world class results in education, research and innovation to address challenges in the areas of energy, climate, mobility, health and digital society. For generations, our engineers have proven to be entrepreneurial problem-solvers, both in business and in a social context.

At TU Delft we embrace diversity as one of our core values and we actively engage to be a university where you feel at home and can flourish. We value different perspectives and qualities. We believe this makes our work more innovative, the TU Delft community more vibrant and the world more just. Together, we imagine, invent and create solutions using technology to have a positive impact on a global scale. That is why we invite you to apply. Your application will receive fair consideration.

Challenge. Change. Impact!

Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science
The Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) brings together three scientific disciplines. Combined, they reinforce each other and are the driving force behind the technology we all use in our daily lives. Technology such as the electricity grid, which our faculty is helping to make completely sustainable and future-proof. At the same time, we are developing the chips and sensors of the future, whilst also setting the foundations for the software technologies to run on this new generation of equipment – which of course includes AI. Meanwhile we are pushing the limits of applied mathematics, for example mapping out disease processes using single cell data, and using mathematics to simulate gigantic ash plumes after a volcanic eruption. In other words: there is plenty of room at the faculty for ground-breaking research. We educate innovative engineers and have excellent labs and facilities that underline our strong international position. In total, more than 1000 employees and 4,000 students work and study in this innovative environment.

Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science.

Conditions of employment
Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met.

Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%.

As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills.

The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged.

Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands.

Additional information
If you would like more information about this vacancy or the selection procedure, please contact Dr. Milos Cvetkovic, via m.cvetkovic@tudelft.nl. For information about the selection procedure, please contact Carla Jager, Management Assistant, email: c.p.jager@tudelft.nl.     

Application procedure
Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 20 November 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents:
  • CV
  • Motivational letter that details your motivation and fit to the job requirements. Incomplete applications will not be considered
  • A list of grades of your qualifying degrees (BSc, MSc)

You can address your application to Dr. Milos Cvetkovic.

Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements.

Please note:
  • You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post.
  • As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security.
  • Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

jobs.title: PhD kandidaat Ondernemers op de loonlijst: Hoe Employeneurship individuele, organisatorische en klantgerichte waarde beïnvloedt
jobs.description_html:
Ben je gefascineerd door wat sommige organisaties beter laat presteren dan hun concurrenten? Wil je werken aan onderzoek dat direct invloed heeft op hoe bedrijven functioneren? Streef je ernaar bij te dragen aan het wetenschappelijke debat binnen een gespecialiseerd onderzoeksveld? Ons team Strategie en Ondernemerschap is op zoek naar talent dat promotieonderzoek wil doen.

Beschrijving van het project
Sommige bedrijven maken medewerkers mede-eigenaar; anderen belonen op basis van prestaties, in plaats van op senioriteit gebaseerde salarisschalen. In tijden van personeelsschaarste wordt het nog belangrijker voor ondernemers en werkgevers om de juiste talenten aan te nemen en aan zich te binden. Logisch dus dat personeelsbeleid en de inrichting van de organisatie van strategisch belang zijn. Zeker in tijden van schaarste op de arbeidsmarkt zal aantrekkelijk werkgeverschap van strategische waarde blijken, zowel om talent aan te trekken als te behouden. Toch is er nog veel onduidelijk over het strategisch management van de interne talentpool.

Om die duidelijkheid te scheppen, zoeken wij een bedrijfskundige die onderzoekt hoe werkgeverschap kan worden ingezet om strategische waarde te creëren. Je werkt samen met andere onderzoekers om inzichtelijk te maken hoe werkgeverschap medewerkers in staat kan stellen om als ondernemende professionals het verschil te maken.

Het project zal drie onderling verbonden onderzoeksvragen beantwoorden:

  1. Hoe kunnen we employeneurship definiëren, en hoe verhoudt het zich tot soortgelijke concepten in de bestaande literatuur?
  2. Hoe kunnen we employeneurship meten en daarmee (toekomstige) employeneurs binnen organisaties identificeren?
  3. Hoe beïnvloedt employeneurship relevante uitkomsten op het niveau van de werkgever (individueel), het niveau van werkgeversbedrijven (organisatie) en het niveau van het klantbedrijf?

Het lijkt je interessant om je resultaten en inzichten te publiceren ten behoeve van het internationale wetenschappelijke debat en de praktijk. Binnen het project zul je kwantitatieve en kwalitatieve onderzoeksmethoden combineren. Je werkt samen met werkgevers en werknemers om de impact van ondernemendheid van individuele medewerkers op henzelf, de onderneming en de maatschappij te kunnen verklaren.

Jouw functie
Taken en verantwoordelijkheden:

  • Opzetten, uitvoeren en analyseren van onderzoek, waaronder literatuurstudie, interviews, focusgroepen en dataverzameling met behulp van vragenlijsten en/of experimenten.
  • Plannen, opzetten en uitvoeren van wetenschappelijk onderzoek, in nauwe samenwerking met regionale bedrijven. Dit op basis van principes van open science en team science.
  • Vertalen van onderzoeksbevindingen naar praktische aanbevelingen voor werknemers, en werkgevers.
  • Binnen het departement Strategy & Entrepreneurship verzorg je bedrijfskundig onderwijs op het gebied van (intern) ondernemerschap in de bachelor- en/of masterfase en verricht je coördinerende taken. Daarnaast help je mee met de begeleiding van afstuderende studenten en met het nakijken van tentamens en/of opdrachten (max. 20% van je tijd).
  • Presenteren van projectresultaten op (inter)nationale conferenties en het publiceren van je onderzoeksresultaten in wetenschappelijke tijdschriften.

jobs.title: PhD in Process-Aware Information Systems for Circular Care Pathways
jobs.description_html:
Are you excited about designing digital innovations for sustainable healthcare and eager to support Dutch care organizations in reducing medication waste while ensuring safe and compliant care? Join us as a PhD candidate on the NWO project REMARK.

Information
Healthcare organizations are under increasing pressure to become more sustainable while continuing to deliver safe, high-quality, and compliant care. Circular care pathways offer opportunities to reduce waste and improve resource utilization, but they also introduce new challenges. Healthcare organizations need to track resources across organizational boundaries, ensure compliance with regulations and quality standards, and monitor increasingly complex processes involving multiple stakeholders.

Existing healthcare information systems provide only limited support for monitoring circular processes and demonstrating compliance throughout the care pathway. As healthcare systems transition from linear to circular models, new methods are needed to continuously monitor processes, detect deviations, assess compliance risks, and provide actionable insights to healthcare professionals and managers.

In this PhD project, you will investigate how process-aware information systems can support the monitoring and governance of circular care pathways. You will develop novel methods that use event data and healthcare process information to provide visibility into the execution of care pathways and identify opportunities for improving compliance, transparency, and sustainability. A central goal is to understand how organizations can continuously monitor circular healthcare processes and ensure that circular interventions remain safe and compliant with regulatory requirements.

You will become member of the Information Systems group within the Department of Industrial Engineering & Innovation Sciences at Eindhoven University of Technology. Your work is embedded in the NWO KIC funded REMARK project, in which a multidisciplinary consortium investigates how circular healthcare pathways can be designed and implemented in practice. For this project, you will collaborate with researchers from multiple universities, Dutch healthcare organizations and industry partners, giving you a unique opportunity to achieve both scientific and societal impact.

jobs.title: Promovendus 'Verbeterde diagnostiek en kennisdeling voor Multipele Systeem Atrofie'
jobs.description_html:
Functie
Multiple systeematrofie (MSA) is een zeldzame en ernstige hersenziekte die zich vaak uit met Parkinsonverschijnselen, maar meestal veel sneller verloopt dan de ziekte van Parkinson. Dit onderzoeksproject probeert in een tweetal samenhangende deelprojecten oplossingen te bieden voor twee problemen rondom de ziekte MSA. Ten eerste: de slechte verspreiding van (nieuwe) kennis omtrent MSA onder professionals; ten tweede: de lange tijd tot aan een diagnose die mensen met MSA ervaren.

Deelproject 1 ‘MSA-Kennisradar’
De meeste neurologen krijgen MSA maar weinig te zien. Daardoor bereiken nieuwe inzichten over het herkennen en vaststellen van MSA hen vaak niet of pas laat. Ook voor neurologen en wetenschappers die gespecialiseerd zijn in bewegingsstoornissen is het moeilijk om alle nieuwe wetenschappelijke informatie bij te houden. De hoeveelheid onderzoek naar MSA groeit snel en de kennis is verspreid over veel verschillende wetenschappelijke publicaties. Met kunstmatige intelligentie (AI) systemen gaan we in dit project op een verantwoorde en veilige manier kennisoverdracht en scholing ontwikkelen omtrent MSA. De kern van dit MSA-kennisradar project is het ontwikkelen van een doorlopend en grotendeels geautomatiseerd proces dat nieuwe wetenschappelijke kennis over MSA omzet in betrouwbare en praktisch bruikbare informatie voor neurologen en wetenschappers op het gebied van MSA.

Deelproject 2: ‘MAESTRO’
In het begin van de ziekte kunnen de klachten van MSA en Parkinson sterk op elkaar lijken. Daardoor is het vaak moeilijk om in een vroeg stadium met zekerheid vast te stellen om welke ziekte het gaat. Het onderscheid is heel belangrijk, omdat mensen met MSA meestal minder goed reageren op de medicijnen die bij Parkinson worden gebruikt. Deze medicijnen kunnen bij mensen met MSA bovendien bijwerkingen veroorzaken. Daarnaast is het zo dat met mensen met MSA hun diagnose vaak pas na vele jaren krijgen. Zij ervaren dit als een van de meest frustrerende aspecten van hun ziekte.

Het doel van de MAESTRO-studie is om biomarkers te vinden waarmee MSA al in een vroeg stadium zo betrouwbaar mogelijk kan worden vastgesteld. We onderzoeken of een combinatie van verschillende meetbare biomarkers hierbij kan helpen, zoals bijvoorbeeld biomarkers in hersenvocht of bloed, zichtbare afwijkingen op een MRI of oogbewegingsstoornissen. We onderzoeken mensen bij wie neurologen denken aan MSA, maar bij wie tijdens het eerste bezoek nog niet met zekerheid kan worden vastgesteld welke aandoening zij hebben. Juist bij deze mensen is in de dagelijkse praktijk behoefte aan aanvullende onderzoeken die de arts kunnen helpen om sneller tot een betrouwbare diagnose te komen. Tijdens het eerste onderzoek bezoek worden verschillende mogelijke biomarkers onderzocht. Daarna volgen we de deelnemers gedurende drie jaar, waarna de klinische diagnose wordt vastgesteld. In de MAESTRO studie onderzoeken we welke biomarkers deze klinische diagnose het beste voorspellen.

Het strekt tot aanbeveling als je naast jouw onderzoek als promovendus bereid bent om gemiddeld één dag in de week als trialarts te werken voor meerdere studies binnen het onderzoekteam. Je beoordeelt of patiënten veilig kunnen deelnemen aan onderzoek en verricht studie-specifieke medische handelingen. Het biedt dus een mooie gelegenheid om je klinische vaardigheden op peil te houden.

jobs.title: PhD position: Optical metasurfaces controlling quantum electron wavepackets
jobs.description_html:
Work Activities
In this project, you will study the fundamental interactions between high-energy electrons and extreme light fields in a scanning electron microscope (SEM). Gaining control over these interactions may lead to new forms of electron microscopy that exploit the quantum-mechanical nature of electron wavepackets. The project uses an emerging technique, photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM), in which electrons in a 1-ps-pulsed electron beam exchange energy with a strongly confined optical near field generated by intense laser pulses. This interaction changes the electrons' energy, which in turn modifies the electron wavepacket in space and time, creating, for example, attosecond electron pulse trains. You will develop specially designed non-local optical metasurfaces to control the interaction of the electrons with the strong light fields. Structured 2D dielectrics integrated with nanometer-thin transition-metal dichalcogenide layers, exhibiting strong optical resonances, will be designed to enhance and control the coupling in an ultrafast 1-30 keV SEM.

Your research will include:
  • PINEM and metasurface design (years 1): learn to operate the ultrafast SEM at AMOLF, study PINEM theory and modeling, and design and fabricate metasurfaces in the Amsterdam NanoCenter cleanroom.
  • PINEM-metasurface integration (year 2): measure the electron-light interaction of optimized metasurfaces and tailor electron wavepackets by design, including through two subsequent coherent PINEM interactions.
  • Coherence and entanglement (year 3-4): investigate correlations between electron energy loss and cathodoluminescence, and test a quantum-eraser geometry in which the which-path information is erased.

The project combines the ultrafast electron-light-matter interaction and cathodoluminescence expertise of Prof. Albert Polman (AMOLF) with metasurface design, fabrication and optical characterization expertise of Dr. Jorik van de Groep (University of Amsterdam). You will be based in the Photonic Materials group of Prof. Polman at AMOLF, with close interaction with the 2D Nanophotonics group of Dr. van de Groep at the University of Amsterdam.

Qualifications
We invite applications from highly motivated candidates with a strong background in physics and a keen interest in nanophotonics, quantum physics, nanofabrication and electron microscopy. We especially encourage individuals from underrepresented groups to apply. Prospective PhD candidates must hold an MSc degree in physics or equivalent qualification.

Work environment
Work environment The Photonic Materials group (www.erbium.nl), led by Prof. Albert Polman, studies light-matter interactions at the nanoscale. The group is composed of an international team of PhD students, postdocs and master students that work in a collaborative atmosphere with many social group activities. Every week we hold a group meeting and departmental colloquium and poster sessions. We also regularly organize an international group labtour.

AMOLF provides state-of-the-art ultrafast electron microscopy systems for time-, angle- and polarization-resolved cathodoluminescence spectroscopy and PINEM, and a shared cleanroom for nanofabrication and characterization (Amsterdam NanoCenter). We offer a highly collaborative and supportive environment, fostering strong connections both within the group and with our national and international partners. PhD students benefit from a variety of courses designed to enhance their research skills.

AMOLF is a part of NWO-I and initiates and performs leading fundamental research on the physics of complex forms of matter, and creates new functional materials, in partnership with academia and industry. The institute is located at Amsterdam Science Park and currently employs about 140 researchers and 80 support employees. www.amolf.nl The 2D Nanophotonics lab (https://vandegroeplab.com), led by Dr. Jorik van de Groep, studies nanophotonic metasurfaces that enable active control over light by harnessing the highly tunable optical properties of two-dimensional quantum materials. By combining resonant metallic and semiconductor nanostructures with exciton resonances in 2D semiconductors, we create dynamic metasurfaces that actively tune light emission, scattering, and absorption at the nanoscale. Our group is part of the Institute of Physics at the University of Amsterdam (https://iop.uva.nl) and works in a collaborative atmosphere with other researchers within the department and (inter)national collaborators.

Working conditions
  • The working atmosphere at the institute is largely determined by young, enthusiastic, mostly non-Dutch employees. Communication is informal and runs through short lines of communication.
  • The position is intended as full-time (40 hours / week, 12 months / year) appointment for the duration of four years. The planned start date is December 1, 2026. · The starting salary is 3.115 Euros gross per month and a range of employment benefits.
  • After successful completion of the PhD research a PhD degree will be granted at the University of Amsterdam.
  • Several courses are offered, specially developed for PhD-students.
  • AMOLF assists any new foreign PhD-student with housing and visa applications and compensates their transport costs and furnishing expenses.

More information?
For further information about the position, please contact Albert Polman: a.polman@amolf.nl and Jorik van de Groep: j.vandegroep@uva.nl

Application
You can respond to this vacancy online via the button below.

Online screening may be part of the selection.

Diversity code
AMOLF is highly committed to an inclusive and diverse work environment: we want to develop talent and creativity by bringing together people from different backgrounds and cultures. We recruit and select on the basis of competencies and talents. We strongly encourage anyone with the right qualifications to apply for the vacancy, regardless of age, gender, origin, sexual orientation or physical ability.

AMOLF has won the NNV Diversity Award 2022, which is awarded every two years by the Netherlands Physical Society for demonstrating the most successful implementation of equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI).

jobs.title: PhD Position in Cloud-Native and AI-Native 6G Networks
jobs.description_html:
Are you passionate about shaping next-generation mobile networks? If so, please continue reading!

Join us!
Software-defined and programmable networking is a key enabling technology for cloud-native and AI-native 6G networks, supporting greater scalability, flexibility, automation, and efficient resource utilization. Cross-layer and cross-domain programmability, across the control and data planes and from RAN to core, is expected to be a defining characteristic of 6G systems, which are currently being developed and standardized. In this context, data plane programming capabilities in next-generation mobile networks can bring significant benefits with regards to network slicing and multi-tenancy, dynamic traffic engineering, offloading network functions to hardware accelerators, etc.

Specifically, this PhD project, conducted in collaboration with Ericsson, the leading mobile communications equipment manufacturer, will investigate data-plane programmability in next-generation mobile networks, with a particular focus on cloud-native and AI-native Radio Access Networks (RAN). The candidate will investigate research challenges including, but not limited to, the specification and implementation of common abstraction layers for heterogeneous programmable data planes, mechanisms for data-plane multitenancy and modularization, and programmable radio resource management, with an emphasis on intelligent and adaptive control.

The research is conducted within the scope of the Future Network Services (FNS): the 6G flagship project for the Netherlands where 60 leading ICT businesses, mobile operators, semiconductor manufacturers and research institutions, have united to spearhead the development of specific aspects of 6G: Software antennas, AI-driven networking, and groundbreaking 6G applications.

You will be embedded in the MNS group. The group focuses its research on the fundamental architectural problems that arise from the interconnection of systems and of data flows. We look at the emerging architectures that can support the operations of the future Internet. More information can be found at: https://mns-research.nl/

Within Ericsson Hungary, your work will be anchored to the team in Ericsson's Research Area Networks, which drives innovations towards 6G and the future network platform. Our local competence and expertise are in Radio Network (RAN) and Packet Core architectures and protocols, programmable networks, and network automation. More information is available at https://www.ericsson.com/en/about-us/company-facts/ericsson-worldwide/hungary/research-ericsson-hungary

Tasks and responsibilities:
  • focus on the development and evaluation of and end-to-end programmable data plane, supporting multitenancy and modularity, through the definition and implementation of a generic hardware abstraction layer, supporting heterogeneous systems e.g., GPUs, TPUs, FPGAs, SOCs.

What we ask of you
Your experience and profile:
  • Master's degree or equivalent program (completed or near completion: see below) in a relevant discipline, such as computer science, electrical and computer engineering, security and network engineering etc.;
  • excellent programming skills (python, C/C++);
  • experience with cloud-native platforms, particularly Kubernetes, is an advantage.
  • experience in programmable networking technologies and DSLs such as eBPF and P4 is a plus;
  • knowledge in mobile network architectures and protocols is a plus;
  • the willingness to be part of an international research team;
  • fluency in oral and written English and good presentation skills;

This is what we offer you
A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is as soon as possible. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000, as well as 1,800 members of staff working in education, research or support services. Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, be it elementary particles, the birth of the universe or the functioning of the brain.

jobs.title: PhD in Early Modern Religious Debates. The use of AI in analysing sources
jobs.description_html:
In the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, in the Low Countries many public religious debates were organized between, for example, Calvinists and Mennonites, or Catholics and Lutherans. Their written reports constitute an underexplored treasure of information about the religious dynamics following the Reformation and the development of a public sphere.

A PhD position is available within the NWO-funded project “In Search of the Truth, in Search of Adherents”. This interdisciplinary project investigates early modern religious debates in the Dutch language.

As a PhD candidate, you will investigate early modern religious debates using digital humanities methods and tools. You will analyse how participants drew on classical and ecclesiastical traditions, examining how different religious groups appropriated and used these traditions to support their arguments and distinguish themselves from their opponents. In addition to conducting your own research, you will contribute to the preparation of a critical edition of early modern Dutch-language debates. You will also help develop and refine methods and tools for producing digital critical editions, making them more effective and widely applicable.

You will work closely with a second PhD candidate in the project, whose research focuses on the rhetorical and argumentative strategies employed by participants in religious debates and the role of these debates in the emergence of a public sphere. Together, the two PhD projects will offer complementary perspectives on the practices, intellectual traditions, and wider cultural significance of early modern religious debate. This position offers an opportunity to work at the intersection of digital humanities and religious history, combining historical research with the development and application of digital methods. A full description of the project is available upon request.

Duties and Responsibilities
  • Conduct independent research and write a PhD dissertation, as well as academic articles.
  • Contribute to knowledge exchange and public engagement activities.
  • Contribute to the preparation of a critical edition of early modern Dutch-language religious debates.
  • Help develop, refine, and improve methods and tools for producing digital critical editions.
  • Contribute to the activities of the research group, research section, and department.
  • Participate in relevant courses and training offered by the Graduate School and NOSTER.

jobs.title: PhD: viral manipulation of caterpillar behaviour in a multidimensional context
jobs.description_html:
Many parasites, including viruses, manipulate the behaviour of host organisms to increase their own transmission, linking to the concept of the ‘extended phenotype’. Fascinating examples include behavioural manipulation of caterpillars by baculoviruses, with infected caterpillars expressing hyperactivity as well as climbing to elevated positions on plants just prior to death. These behavioural alterations have a crucial evolutionary benefit to the virus, enhancing its transmission. Until now, parasitic manipulation of host behaviour has been investigated as a bidirectional interaction between the manipulative parasite and the host.

While the possible influence of the host or parasite microbiome on host behavioural manipulation is starting to be recognized, the influence of the host’s resident virome has so far been ignored. The past decades, evidence has accumulated that insects harbour a wide range of covert virus infections that do not cause any signs of disease. In this project, you will study manipulative parasite-host interactions in a multidimensional context, by investigating how covert virus infections modulate crosstalk between manipulative baculoviruses and their caterpillar host.

You will start with analysing the phenotype of baculovirus-induced behavioural manipulation across several closely and more distantly related baculoviruses and lepidopteran hosts, and determine the impact of the insect’s virome on the manipulation. Next, you will investigate in detail the molecular mechanisms underlying the manipulation, especially focusing on changes induced in the lepidopteran central nervous system (CNS). You will specifically perform an in-depth analysis of viral CNS invasion and determine localisation of baculoviruses as well as covert virus infections.

Furthermore, you will validate putative mechanisms by functional analyses of candidate genes and proteins, using a range of techniques including RNAi and CRISPR/Cas9 technology. This research will aid in identifying how virus-induced manipulation has evolved across lepidopterans and identify commonalities and differences in underlying mechanisms, and will also reveal how the behavioural outcome of manipulation is dependent on the context of resident viruses present in the host.

This PhD project is part of a larger Vici project, funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO). As such, you will closely collaborate with another PhD student and a postdoc in this project, working on related questions.

As a PhD candidate you will contribute to fundamental science in the context of insect virology. In addition, you will participate in cursory teaching of the chair group. You will be embedded in the Laboratory of Virology. In addition, you will collaborate with (inter)national colleagues from both in- and outside Wageningen University & Research.

Your duties and responsibilities include:
  • Designing and executing experiments with insects and viruses, measuring behavioural manipulation;
  • Investigating the molecular mechanisms underlying behavioural manipulation using dissections, transcriptome, proteome and small RNA profiling;
  • Studying virus invasion of the lepidopteran central nervous system, using GFP-labelled viruses, hybridisation techniques, antibody labelling and microscopy;
  • Teaching in courses and supervise BSc and MSc students;
  • Writing and presenting research at/in internationally renowned conferences/journals.

You will work here
You will work with in the Insect Virology group, as part of the NWO Vici project ‘Invisible influencers: How hidden virus infections shape insect life’ led by Dr. Vera Ros. The project is aimed at disentangling how the insect’s virome (i.e. the assemblage of viruses) impacts insect immune responses, fitness and behaviour, and thereby influences interactions with and effects of incoming virus infections.

The Insect Virology group is part of the chair group Laboratory of Virology, and research in Insect Virology focuses on multiple aspects of insect-virus interactions including mechanisms behind viral manipulation of insect behaviour, virus discovery, covert virus infections (i.e. infections without clear symptoms) in insects and the use of viruses for biological control of insect pests. You will be supervised by Dr. Vera Ros (WUR Laboratory of Virology) and Prof. Monique van Oers (chair of the WUR Laboratory of Virology). In addition, you will also be embedded in the PE&RC graduate school (Home | PE&RC), which will allow you to follow a wide variety of training courses and will provide support during your academic journey.

The Laboratory of Virology is part of the Plant Sciences Group of Wageningen University. It is located at the Wageningen Campus in the Radix building. We provide virology teaching at Wageningen University within BSc and MSc programs across various disciplines. The Virology chair group comprises around 35 members, including research/teaching staff, technicians, PhD candidates, postdocs and visiting researchers. Each year, an average of 25 BSc and MSc students undertake their final-year thesis research within Virology. The Virology group conducts fundamental research into plant viruses, insect viruses and arboviruses. Where possible, the knowledge generated is translated into applications aimed at improving food production and human and animal health.

jobs.title: PhD Insect Virology: impact of the insect’s virome on insect immunity & fitness
jobs.description_html:
Insects are exposed to a diverse range of infectious viruses throughout their lives. In recent years, advances in largescale sequencing technologies have accelerated virus discovery, revealing a rich and diverse resident assemblage of viruses or 'virome' in insects, including covert viral infections that appear asymptomatic. To date it is unclear how such a virome impacts insect life.

In this project you will investigate how the resident virome impacts insect immune responses and fitness and thereby influences interactions with and effects of incoming virus infections. First, you will define the virome in several lepidopteran species and determine how the virome impacts insect life history traits and responses to incoming infections. In a next step, you will study in detail vertical transmission of the virome and investigate how the virome affects transgenerational immune priming (TgIP), a process whereby incoming infections lead to immune protection against secondary infections in the next generation.

By integrating virome sequencing and experimental infections with -omics approaches, microscopy, and gene editing tools, you will reveal fundamental mechanisms of insect immunity and virus-induced TgIP and the impact of the virome thereon.

jobs.title: PhD Position in AI for Software Reuse and Agentic Development
jobs.description_html:
How can AI agents build on existing software instead of reinventing it? Join this collaboration between TU Delft and ING to research more reliable agentic software development.

Job description
Software intensive organizations rely on increasingly large and complex software ecosystems consisting of services, libraries, APIs, frameworks, documentation, and other shared engineering knowledge. Recent advances in generative AI and software engineering agents are changing how software is developed and how developers interact with these ecosystems. TU Delft is collaborating with ING to investigate how we can make enterprise software development more sustainable and reliable in this changing landscape.

We will develop new techniques and tools that help developers and AI agents make better use of existing software and developer knowledge. Our research will combine AI with software repository mining, program and architecture analysis, empirical software engineering, and studies with practitioners. The research will focus on real-world software engineering challenges at ING, while contributing scientific insights and open research results that can benefit the broader software engineering community.

Within this collaboration, we explore two main research directions:

Direction 1: Software Reuse in Enterprise Software Ecosystems

Large organizations invest substantially in reusable software assets. However, as a consequence similar functionality can be implemented independently across teams, increasing fragmentation and long-term maintenance costs. AI-assisted software development makes this challenge even more important: software engineering agents can rapidly generate new code, but may reproduce functionality that already exists elsewhere in an organization.

This direction investigates how software assets are discovered, consumed, adapted, and evolved across large software ecosystems. We will study where opportunities for reuse exist, how software can successfully be adapted across teams, how reusable assets evolve over time, and how developers and AI agents can be guided towards suitable existing software. Ultimately, we aim to develop intelligent techniques that help organizations maximize reuse while reducing unnecessary duplication and maintenance effort.

Direction 2: Reliable Agentic Software Development

AI software engineering agents can increasingly perform tasks such as implementing features, fixing bugs, testing, and refactoring software. Their success, however, depends not only on the underlying AI models, but also on the engineering context available to them. In enterprise environments, relevant knowledge is distributed across source code, documentation, architecture descriptions, requirements, APIs, development history, and organizational practices.

This direction investigates the engineering foundations required for reliable agentic software development. We will study what context agents need for different software engineering tasks, what makes specifications sufficiently complete and precise, how stale or incomplete context and software complexity affect agent performance, and how organizations can determine when tasks can be reliably delegated to AI agents. The goal is to develop techniques and safeguards that enable organizations to integrate increasingly autonomous software engineering agents while maintaining software quality and human oversight.

We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive research environment and encourage applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of their background or experience. We believe that diversity contributes to a more innovative and creative research community. If you do not meet some of the optional requirements listed, we encourage you to still apply and explain how your unique experience and skills can contribute to our research.

Job requirements
Required
  • Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field
  • Proficiency in the English language

Additional requirements:
  • Research focus, characterized by curiosity, data fluency, and critical thinking
  • Engineering mindset, including ability to create experimental prototypes and demonstrators
  • Team player, good listener, and ready to help

To thrive as a PhD candidate, it’s crucial to have a strong research mindset driven by curiosity and passion for your topic. Reflecting on your motivation for pursuing a PhD trajectory is essential, as this path involves unique challenges and uncertainties inherent to scientific exploration. Success requires dedication, adaptability, the ability to analyze complex problems, manage your time effectively, innovate and stay resilient under pressure. Combined with the ability and willingness to work independently and collaborate well, these qualities are indispensable for a fulfilling PhD journey. These experiences will build you as an independent researcher, expand your professional network, and pave the way for diverse career pave the way for diverse career paths, inside or outside academia.

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Delft University of Technology is built on strong foundations. As creators of the world-famous Dutch waterworks and pioneers in biotech, TU Delft is a top international university combining science, engineering and design. It delivers world class results in education, research and innovation to address challenges in the areas of energy, climate, mobility, health and digital society. For generations, our engineers have proven to be entrepreneurial problem-solvers, both in business and in a social context.

At TU Delft we embrace diversity as one of our core values and we actively engage to be a university where you feel at home and can flourish. We value different perspectives and qualities. We believe this makes our work more innovative, the TU Delft community more vibrant and the world more just. Together, we imagine, invent and create solutions using technology to have a positive impact on a global scale. That is why we invite you to apply. Your application will receive fair consideration.

Challenge. Change. Impact!

Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science
The Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) brings together three scientific disciplines. Combined, they reinforce each other and are the driving force behind the technology we all use in our daily lives. Technology such as the electricity grid, which our faculty is helping to make completely sustainable and future-proof. At the same time, we are developing the chips and sensors of the future, whilst also setting the foundations for the software technologies to run on this new generation of equipment – which of course includes AI. Meanwhile we are pushing the limits of applied mathematics, for example mapping out disease processes using single cell data, and using mathematics to simulate gigantic ash plumes after a volcanic eruption. In other words: there is plenty of room at the faculty for ground-breaking research. We educate innovative engineers and have excellent labs and facilities that underline our strong international position. In total, more than 1000 employees and 4,000 students work and study in this innovative environment.

Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science.

Conditions of employment
Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met.

Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%.

As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills.

The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged.

Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. Additional information

Application procedure
Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 1 December 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents:

  • Motivational letter. In your motivation letter, please include your preference for one of the two research directions you are most interested in.

You can address your application to Andy Zaidman. The PhD position will be fully at TU Delft, with strong collaboration with ING. Please include a brief statement in your application indicating whether and, if so, how you used AI tools to prepare your application documents.

Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements.
