jobs.title: PhD Candidate 'AI-Driven Handheld Ultrasound for Military Trauma Care'
jobs.description_html:
Job description
Do you want to develop artificial intelligence for medical imaging to improve care for injured military personnel?

Military trauma care takes place under challenging conditions. During military operations, medical resources may be limited, specialist expertise may not always be available, and evacuation to a hospital may take hours or even days. Under these circumstances, healthcare providers must be able to rapidly and reliably identify a patient’s injuries and determine the treatment required. Rapid diagnostics can be lifesaving.

Ultrasound offers significant opportunities in this regard. Portable ultrasound equipment enables healthcare providers to examine patients at the point of care, without relying on extensive diagnostic facilities. One important application is the Extended Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma (EFAST), which can be used to detect signs of internal bleeding and pneumothorax, among other conditions. However, performing and interpreting ultrasound examinations requires specific knowledge and experience, which may not be readily accessible in forward-deployed medical treatment facilities.

Can artificial intelligence make ultrasound more accessible and effective for military healthcare providers in operational environments?

This is the central challenge of this PhD research project. Ultrasound offers valuable opportunities for rapid, portable diagnostics in military trauma care, particularly in forward-deployed settings where access to advanced diagnostic equipment and specialised expertise may be limited.

You will investigate how artificial intelligence can support military healthcare providers in acquiring and interpreting ultrasound images. The research will start by exploring existing AI-assisted ultrasound technologies, identifying unmet operational needs and determining where further technological development could provide the greatest benefit to military healthcare.

Applications such as Extended Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma (EFAST), used to identify potentially life-threatening injuries, provide a relevant starting point. However, the research will also explore other promising applications of ultrasound and AI across military trauma care.

Beyond developing and evaluating AI algorithms, the project will investigate how these technologies can be effectively integrated into military medical practice, taking into account the capabilities of healthcare providers and the specific challenges of operational environments.

Although military healthcare is the primary focus, the resulting knowledge and technologies may also benefit civilian emergency care, including ambulance services and emergency departments.

jobs.title: PhD in Synthesis of Sustainable PFAS-Free Polymers for High-Performance Applications
jobs.description_html:
Fluorinated polymers and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely used in high-performance applications because of their exceptional thermal stability, chemical resistance and low surface energy. These properties make them essential in demanding applications, including automotive and aerospace components, sealing systems, and chemical processing equipment. However, growing environmental concerns and increasing regulatory pressure, particularly in Europe, are driving the need to replace PFAS with safer and more sustainable alternatives. Developing innovative PFAS-free materials that combine environmental sustainability with outstanding performance under demanding operating conditions represents an important scientific and technological challenge.

Research challenge
In this project, the research challenge will be to design, synthesize, and characterize novel fluorine-free thermoplastic materials that combine the outstanding surface and bulk properties of fluorinated polymers. The project will explore how molecular architecture and surface segregation can be used to achieve low surface energy while maintaining high thermal stability, chemical resistance, and robust thermomechanical properties. By combining molecular design with surface thermodynamics, the research will establish fundamental structure–property relationships linking polymer architecture and interfacial organization to macroscopic material performance. The research activities will involve the synthesis of novel polymer architectures and their comprehensive characterization using chemical, structural, thermal, rheological, and mechanical techniques, complemented by the investigation of surface and interfacial properties. The ultimate goal is to establish rational design principles for sustainable, high-performance thermoplastics suitable for demanding industrial applications, including sealing systems and high-durability components.

An interdisciplinary and international environment
The PhD research will be carried out under the supervision of Prof. Željko Tomović and Dr. Catarina Esteves in the Department of Chemical Engineering and Chemistry at Eindhoven University of Technology. You will join the Polymer Performance Materials research group, which focuses on sustainable polymer chemistry. You will also become part of the interdisciplinary Institute for Complex Molecular Systems, which connects TU/e researchers working across polymer science and related fields.

The PhD project will be carried out within the HARFF project, funded by the Dutch Polymer Institute (DPI), which promotes research collaboration between industry and leading universities across Europe. The industrial partners involved in this project are Envalior, SKF, Teijin Aramid, and SABIC Specialties. Through this collaborative network, you will develop new skills, build valuable academic and industrial connections, and explore how your research can contribute to developing future sustainable technologies.

Working at TU/e
At TU/e, you will work in an environment that combines scientific curiosity with a hands-on mentality. You will receive personal guidance while having room to develop your own ideas, ambitions, and talents. Together with supportive colleagues from different disciplines and backgrounds, you will push the boundaries of sustainable polymer chemistry and contribute to research with clear societal relevance.

Ideal start date: January 01 2027

jobs.title: PhD in Fair Distributed Optimization and Control of Large-Scale Networked Systems
jobs.description_html:
Can thousands of autonomous agents, each with only local information, reach decisions that are optimal, stable and provably fair? In this PhD you will build the distributed optimization and control theory that answers this question. You will design scalable multi-agent algorithms with fairness built in, handle uncertainty with stochastic and robust methods, and prove convergence, stability and fairness guarantees. Your testbed will be one of the largest and most demanding networked systems there is: the electricity distribution grid, where thousands of solar panels, heat pumps and electric vehicles compete for limited network capacity. If you enjoy turning hard real-world problems into elegant mathematics, this position is for you.

Note to applicants: No background in energy systems is required; you will pick up the domain knowledge during the project, together with our energy experts. We are looking for candidates with a strong background in control systems, optimization or applied mathematics.

Information
At its core, this project tackles a fundamental problem in networked control: how to allocate a scarce shared resource among many agents in a way that is efficient, scalable and fair, using only local computation and limited communication. The motivating application is congestion management in electricity distribution networks. As rooftop photovoltaics, heat pumps and electric vehicles spread, local networks increasingly hit their capacity limits, and operators must decide how much power each prosumer may inject or consume. The core idea is to embed clear and interpretable notions of fairness directly into distributed control and optimization algorithms, as constraints or objectives with provable guarantees.

The project advances fundamental science at the intersection of distributed optimization, control theory, multi-agent systems and machine learning. It seeks to redefine how societal objectives such as fairness are formalized mathematically and enforced in intelligent control systems.

You will be embedded in the Control Systems group at TU/e, contributing to its research program on intelligent and responsible control of networked systems.

You will work closely with experts in distributed control, responsible AI and power systems across departments, who provide the domain knowledge and real-world data to test your methods.

Beyond the theory, your algorithms will help distribution system operators manage congestion transparently and equitably, speeding up the integration of renewable energy and strengthening public trust in the energy transition.

As a PhD candidate, you will:
  • Formulate fair resource allocation problems: Cast congestion management as a large-scale, constrained multi-agent optimization problem, and formalize interpretable fairness notions (e.g., proportional, max-min or probabilistic fairness) as mathematical constraints or objectives.
  • Design distributed optimization algorithms: Develop and analyze consensus-based, primal-dual, ADMM-type and game-theoretic algorithms that coordinate thousands of agents using only local information and limited communication.
  • Develop fairness-aware feedback controllers: Design distributed controllers (e.g., distributed MPC, online feedback optimization) that enforce fairness while guaranteeing scalability, stability and constraint satisfaction.
  • Analyze probabilistic allocation policies: Study randomized and weighted allocation schemes, such as raffle-based curtailment, and characterize their fairness and efficiency over time.
  • Handle uncertainty: Incorporate stochastic models of generation and demand using tools from stochastic, robust and learning-based control.
  • Prove theoretical guarantees: Establish convergence, stability, robustness and fairness guarantees, including under forecasting errors, model mismatch and communication delays.
  • Validate on realistic large-scale networks: Test your algorithms in simulations of realistic distribution networks and on real-world data from Dutch distribution system operators.
  • Publish and collaborate: Publish in leading control and optimization venues (e.g., IEEE TAC, Automatica, CDC) and work with colleagues in control, AI and electrical engineering.

This PhD position is part of the project "Responsible AI for Fair and Efficient Control of Energy Systems (RAICES)“ (https://www.tue.nl/en/research/institutes/eindhoven-artificial-intelligence-systems-institute/ai-research/eaisi-emdair-program)

jobs.title: PhD Candidate on Responsible AI for Online Safety (1.0 FTE)
jobs.description_html:
Artificial intelligence, and generative AI in particular, is reshaping digital ecosystems and the way people access information, make decisions, and stay safe, creating new opportunities and new risks for society. This PhD project sits at the intersection of AI, cybersecurity, and computational social science, and focuses on responsible AI, developing trustworthy and accountable methods that remain reliable when people or AI systems actively try to manipulate them. You will contribute to this area through methodological and empirical research, collaborating with colleagues at LIACS and international partners. Potential research topics include, but are not limited to, modeling and detecting AI-driven manipulation such as coordinated influence campaigns and social bots, building early warning systems for online harms such as fraud and scams, and studying how humans and AI systems can jointly recognize and counter manipulation.

What you will do
The PhD student will be embedded in the System and security cluster at the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science, supervised by Dr. Valerio La Gatta and Dr. Olga Gadyastkaya from the Leiden Organizational Cyber Security Group. The successful candidate will conduct original research on responsible AI methods for online safety, publish and present scientific articles at leading venues in AI, computational social science, and cybersecurity, contribute to educational activities as a (head) teaching assistant and finally write a PhD thesis detailing the outcome of the research activities.

Where you will work
The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. Our people are driven by curiosity to expand fundamental knowledge and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline. The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is diverse, ranging from mathematics, artificial intelligence, computer science, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences

The faculty is home to more than 2,700 staff members and over 6,000 students enrolled in nine bachelor's and fifteen master's programs. We are located at the heart of the Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s largest science parks, where academia and industry come together.
For more information, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science.

You will be part of the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science (LIACS). LIACS offers the bachelor's programs in Computer Science and Data Science/Artificial Intelligence, as well as master's programs in Computer Science, ICT in Business and the Public Sector, Media Technology, and Science Based Business. According to an independent research assessment, LIACS is one of the leading computer science departments in the Netherlands. We strive for excellence in a supportive institute where academic achievement, enjoyment, and diversity go hand in hand. We offer a clear and welcoming career path for young and talented scientists with the ambition to grow. For more information about LIACS, visit our website: https://www.cs.leiden.edu.

What you bring
  • A Master’s (or equivalent) degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, or a closely related quantitative field (e.g., Mathematics, Physics, or Computational Social Science);
  • Solid background in machine learning; familiarity with natural language processing, large language models, or network analysis is a plus;
  • Strong programming skills (e.g., Python and deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch) and experience working with real-world data;
  • Genuine interest in the societal impact of AI and in interdisciplinary research bridging computer science and the social sciences;
  • Prior research experience, such as a research-oriented thesis or a scientific publication, is a plus;
  • Ability to work independently as well as in a team, and to communicate research findings clearly in writing and in oral presentations;
  • Proficiency in English, both spoken and written (Dutch is not required, but LIACS does subsidize optional Dutch language courses).

What we offer
  • An employment contract for the duration of initially one year. After a positive evaluation of the progress of the thesis, personal capabilities and compatibility, the appointment will be extended by a further three years.
    This contract falls under the CLA of Dutch Universities;
  • A salary between € 3.204,= and € 4.051,= gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours, Payscale P);
  • A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP;
  • Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel;
  • Flexible working hours: as a standard, you are entitled to a minimum of 29 leave days on the basis of a full-time working week of 38 hours; you can also save for extra leave, for example by working 40 hours a week, and in this way accrue an extra 96 leave hours, or exchange 96 leave hours for a 36-hour week.
  • Lots of options when it comes to secondary employment conditions; we can, for example, discuss options for a sabbatical or paid parental leave. Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme;
  • If your work allows it, hybrid working is possible within the Netherlands;
  • A home-working allowance (day and internet allowance) and attention for good workplaces. The University will also provide you with a laptop.


The expected starting date is March 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter

What we value
Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent.

Want to apply or find out more?

Information

Enquiries can be made to Dr. Valerio La Gatta, who will be the daily supervisor for this position, email: v.la.gatta@liacs.leidenuniv.nl. If you have If you have any questions about the application, please sent an email to: jobs@liacs.leidenuniv.nl.


Applications

To apply for this position, please submit your application online via the blue button in the vacancy on the university website. Please ensure that you attach the following additional documents:
  • Cover letter (1–2 pages) explaining your motivation for this position, how your background fits the project, and which research directions within the project interest you most;
  • Curriculum vitae (CV);
  • MSc (or equivalent) degree (or expected graduation date);
  • Transcripts of records for both your bachelor’s and master’s degrees;
  • If available, one example of your scientific writing (e.g., master’s thesis or a draft of it, a scientific publication);
  • If available, links to code repositories (e.g., GitHub) or other software projects you have developed;
  • Names and contact details of up two references (e.g., your thesis supervisor or other academic collaborators). References will only be contacted for shortlisted candidates.

Only applications received before Dec 13, 2026, 23:59 CET can be considered. Early applications are welcome, since this will help speed up the recruitment process, but all applications submitted before the deadline will be given equal consideration. Your application will be treated confidentially and will be assessed by researchers from the System and Security Cluster at LIACS, Leiden University.

jobs.title: Promovendus Strafrecht en Criminologie (1,0 fte)
jobs.description_html:
Bij het Instituut voor Strafrecht en Criminologie is per 1 februari 2027 een vacature voor de functie van promovendus die promotieonderzoek verricht naar financiële kwetsbaarheid en strafrechtelijke boetes in Nederland.

Dit ga je doen
Als promovendus zal je zowel sociaalwetenschappelijk als juridisch onderzoek uitvoeren naar de rol van financiële kwetsbaarheid bij strafrechtelijke boetes in Nederland. Jaarlijks worden in Nederland tienduizenden strafrechtelijke geldboetes opgelegd maar inzicht in de manier waarop financiële kwetsbaarheid een rol speelt bij de boeteoplegging is schaars. Aan de hand van zowel juridisch als sociaalwetenschappelijk onderzoek wordt binnen dit PhD-project de rol van financiële kwetsbaarheid onderzocht bij de oplegging en tenuitvoerlegging van geldboetes, onderzocht wat de effecten van geldboetes zijn en nagegaan hoe dit zich verhoudt tot juridische uitgangspunten en beginselen.

Het promotieonderzoek wordt verricht binnen het Instituut voor Strafrecht en Criminologie. Het onderzoek zal worden verricht onder begeleiding van prof. mr. L.A. (Marloes) van Noorloos (strafrecht), dr. R.M. (Rosa) Koenraadt (criminologie) en prof. Mr. S. (Sigrid) van Wingerden (criminologie). Het onderzoek mondt aan het eind van de aanstellingsperiode uit in een dissertatie. Het gaat om een fulltime functie als PhD-kandidaat (38 uur per week) voor de periode van vier jaar.

Naast inhoudelijke onderzoekstaken zul je ook onderwijs verzorgen, word je betrokken bij de organisatie van wetenschappelijke activiteiten en neem je deel aan het opleidingstraject voor promovendi.

Jouw werkzaamheden:
  • Uitvoeren van sociaalwetenschappelijk en juridisch onderzoek naar financiële kwetsbaarheid en boetes, onder andere door middel van interviews, statistische analyses via R en analyse van rechtspraak.
  • Je neemt deel aan het opleidingstraject voor promovendi van de Faculteit der Rechtsgeleerdheid.
  • Ongeveer 10% van de tijd verzorg je onderwijs op het gebied van de criminologie of straf(proces)recht en verricht je ondersteunende taken binnen het onderzoeksprogramma Criminal Justice: Maatschappelijk effectieve strafrechtspleging;
  • Je neemt deel aan en draagt bij aan de organisatie van wetenschappelijke activiteiten die door het Instituut voor Strafrecht en Criminologie worden georganiseerd (lezingen, conferenties, symposia);

Het promotietraject zal begin 2027 van start gaan.

Hier ga je werken
De Faculteit der Rechtsgeleerdheid is gevestigd in Leiden en Den Haag en is met ruim 7000 studenten en ongeveer 600 medewerkers een van de grootste faculteiten van Nederland. De faculteit richt zich op innovatief multidisciplinair onderzoek en een steeds vernieuwend onderwijsaanbod aan de hand van maatschappelijke vraagstukken. Onze faculteit is groot genoeg om nationaal en internationaal het verschil te maken en klein genoeg om persoonlijk onderwijs te bieden. Zo leveren we dagelijks een bijdrage aan een veilige en duurzame wereld. Impact met recht! Zie voor meer informatie https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/rechtsgeleerdheid.

Je gaat werken bij zowel de Afdeling Criminologie als Straf- en strafprocesrecht, die samen het Instituut voor Strafrecht & Criminologie in Leiden vormen. Bij de afdeling Criminologie werken ongeveer 50 medewerkers en bij de afdeling Straf- en strafprocesrecht ongeveer 20 medewerkers, waarvan de meesten onderzoek verrichten en met elkaar onderwijs verzorgen in de bachelor- en masteropleidingen Criminologie, Rechtsgeleerdheid en Strafrecht. Het (inter)nationale onderzoek is voor een belangrijk deel ingebed in het facultaire onderzoeksprogramma Criminal Justice: Maatschappelijk effectieve strafrechtspleging: zie

https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/onderzoek/onderzoeksprojecten/rechtsgeleerdheid/criminal-justice-legitimacy-accountability-and-effectivity .

Dit breng je mee
  • Je hebt een afgeronde masteropleiding Criminologie, Sociologie, Psychologie, Sociale Wetenschappen of gerelateerde opleidingen, in combinatie met een afgeronde juridische opleiding, bij voorkeur met specialisatie Strafrecht.
  • Aantoonbare belangstelling en vaardigheden voor het verrichten van wetenschappelijk onderzoek, bij voorkeur blijkend uit een goede afstudeerscriptie, papers en/of publicaties;
  • Je hebt affiniteit met en aantoonbare kwalitatieve en geavanceerde kwantitatieve onderzoeksvaardigheden en bij voorkeur reeds ervaring met het interviewen en analyseren van kwalitatieve onderzoeksgegevens (bijv. in Atlas.ti) en het werken met statistische software (bijv. SPSS/Stata/R).
  • Sterke analytische vaardigheden;
  • Uitstekende beheersing van de Nederlandse en Engelse taal in woord en geschrift;
  • Je kunt goed samenwerken in teamverband, maar bent ook in staat om zelfstandig je weg te vinden binnen en buiten onze organisatie;

Dit bieden we je
We streven ernaar om met elkaar een transparante, inclusieve werkomgeving te creëren, waarin iedereen zich welkom en gewaardeerd voelt. Onze organisatie is volop in beweging en met jouw ideeën voor verbetering en vernieuwing komen we verder. We besteden graag met jou aandacht aan je persoonlijke ontwikkeling.

Je kunt rekenen op een leuke maatschappelijk relevante baan binnen de wereld van onderwijs en onderzoek. De uitdagende en internationale werkomgeving van de universiteit bevindt zich op een steenworp afstand van de levendige Leidse binnenstad of in het bruisende stadscentrum in Den Haag. Ook hebben we – samen met jou – aandacht voor gezondheid en vitaliteit. Vanuit Healthy University organiseren we leuke activiteiten die hieraan bijdragen.

Daarnaast bieden we je:
  • Aanstelling als promovendus conform de cao Nederlandse Universiteiten. In eerste instantie krijg je een dienstverband van een jaar. Daarna kan het dienstverband met drie jaar verlengd worden; met het oog op die verlenging vindt aan het einde van het eerste jaar een evaluatie plaats waarin gekeken wordt naar de promovendi-opleiding, naar de haalbaarheid van het proefschrift, en naar de progressie in didactische kwaliteiten;
  • Een salaris tussen €3204 - €4051,- bruto per maand bij een fulltime (38 uur) aanstelling (Promovendus);
  • Daarnaast kent de Universiteit Leiden goede arbeidsvoorwaarden. Zo is er sprake van een eindejaarsuitkering (8,3%), vakantietoeslag (8%), uitstekende opleidingsfaciliteiten, betaald ouderschapsverlof en de mogelijkheid om via een keuzemodel arbeidsvoorwaarden op maat te kiezen;
  • Volledige vergoeding van reiskosten met OV voor woon-werkreizen.
  • Samenwerking in een enthousiast en professioneel team aan een gefinancierd onderzoeksproject met grote maatschappelijke relevantie;;
  • Veel vrijheid, flexibiliteit en verantwoordelijkheid: je krijgt alle ruimte om je talent verder te ontwikkelen;;
  • Deelname aan het opleidingsprogramma voor promovendi.

Meer informatie over arbeidsvoorwaarden lees je hier: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/werken-bij/sollicitatieprocedure-en-arbeidsvoorwaarden

Dit vinden wij belangrijk
Het bevorderen van een inclusieve gemeenschap staat centraal in de waarden en visie van de Universiteit Leiden. We streven ernaar om een open gemeenschap te zijn waar alle studenten en medewerkers zich gewaardeerd en gerespecteerd voelen en zich volop kunnen ontplooien. Diversiteit in ervaringen en perspectieven verrijkt ons onderwijs en versterkt ons onderzoek. Een inclusieve academische omgeving waarin studenten en medewerkers hun ervaringen en opvattingen kunnen delen, zien we als essentieel voor de ontwikkeling van talenten.

Solliciteren of meer weten?
Solliciteren kan via ons sollicitatiesysteem. Sollicitaties voorzien van het vacaturenummer en vergezeld van een motivatiebrief en cv kunnen tot uiterlijk 3 december worden ingediend, gericht aan mw. S. Mattheus. De gesprekken zullen worden gevoerd op 8 en 9 december 2026.

Wil je eerst nog meer informatie over de inhoud van deze functie? Neem contact op met R.M. (Rosa) Koenraadt, r.m.koenraadt@law.leidenuniv.nl.

Om elkaar goed te leren kennen, volgen we een aantal stappen in de sollicitatieprocedure. Meer informatie lees je hier: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/werken-bij/sollicitatieprocedure-en-arbeidsvoorwaarden

jobs.title: PhD positie, Policy Lab Justitie en Veiligheid (1,0 fte, vier jaar)
jobs.description_html:
PhD positie, Policy Lab Justitie en Veiligheid: Intermediair tussen Kennis en Sanctiebeleid binnen het NWA-onderzoeksproject Cocreating Research to Improve Science for Policy (CRISP) (1,0 fte, vier jaar)
Het instituut Strafrecht en Criminologie van de Universiteit Leiden zoekt een promovendus/promovenda voor een onderzoekproject in het consortium Cocreating Research to Improve Science for Policy (CRISP), gefinancierd in het kader van de Nationale Wetenschapsagenda (NWA). De promovendus zal onderzoek uitvoeren in het deelproject Justitie en Veiligheid: Intermediair tussen Kennis en Sanctiebeleid.


Het overkoepelende project
Kennis uit onderzoek vormt een belangrijke bouwsteen voor effectief beleid. De praktijk leert echter dat de systematische benutting van kennis uit onderzoek voor beleid niet vanzelfsprekend is. Het consortium ‘Cocreating Research to Improve Science for Policy’ (CRISP) wil door onderzoek bijdragen aan een verbeterde aansluiting van de werelden van kennis en beleid. Daarmee kunnen complexe maatschappelijke opgaven beter worden begrepen en effectiever en efficiënter aangepakt worden. In het CRISP-consortium nemen verschillende kennisinstellingen en ministeries deel en zullen 8 promovendi en 3 postdocs in deelprojecten onderzoek doen. In het onderzoek staat het versterken van samenwerkingsvormen tussen kennis en beleid centraal die leiden tot beter bruikbare kennis en betere kennisbenutting. Het CRISP-onderzoek vindt plaats in co-creatie met ministeries en andere stakeholders en richt zich op actuele publieke vraagstukken.

Voor een beschrijving van het CRISP-consortium en de deelprojecten: zie www.scienceforpolicy.nl

Dit ga je doen

Het promotieonderzoek
Als promovendus/promovenda voer je zelfstandig onderzoek uit binnen een van de deelprojecten van CRISP: Policy Lab Justitie en Veiligheid: Intermediair tussen Kennis en Sanctiebeleid.

In dit deelproject onderzoeken we welke kennis beleidsmakers nodig hebben om evidence-based te werken bij de vormgeving, uitvoering en evaluatie van sanctiebeleid, en welke belemmeringen zij daarbij ervaren. Meer specifiek bestuderen we of en hoe een intermediair tussen kennis en (sanctie)beleid hierin een verschil kan maken, en onder welke voorwaarden dit het geval is. Samen met beleidsmedewerkers van het ministerie van Justitie en Veiligheid geef je vorm aan de intermediaire functie. In het project toetsen en evalueren we de meerwaarde ervan. Op basis van de resultaten formuleer je lessen en aanbevelingen.

Het onderzoek wordt uitgevoerd onder begeleiding van Prof. mr. dr. Miranda Boone (promotor), en Prof. dr. René Torenvlied (promotor)


Kerntaken
Als promovendus ben je, samen met jouw begeleiders, verantwoordelijk voor:
  • het uitwerken van het onderzoeksvoorstel tot een samenhangend en uitvoerbaar promotieplan, dat aansluit bij het overkoepelende CRISP-project;
  • Het uitvoeren van literatuuronderzoek, het inventariseren van bestaande praktijkdocumenten en het verzamelen en analyseren van empirische gegevens;
  • het samen met praktijkpartners vormgeven van het onderzoek door hen actief te betrekken bij het onderzoeksproces en het vertalen van resultaten naar praktijkgerichte aanbevelingen en producten;
  • het succesvol afronden van een Engelstalig proefschrift binnen de vastgestelde periode;
  • het publiceren in internationale peer-reviewed tijdschriften, bijdragen aan Open Access-publicaties en professionele publicaties;
  • het presenteren van resultaten op nationale en internationale wetenschappelijke en praktijkgerichte conferenties;
  • actieve deelname aan bijeenkomsten en onderzoeksactiviteiten van de eigen onderzoeksgroep en instituut, het deelproject en het CRISP-consortium;
  • Een beperkte bijdrage aan onderwijs of andere academische taken

Hier ga je werken
De Faculteit der Rechtsgeleerdheid is gevestigd in Leiden en Den Haag en is met ruim 7000 studenten en ongeveer 600 medewerkers een van de grootste faculteiten van Nederland. De faculteit richt zich op innovatief multidisciplinair onderzoek en een steeds vernieuwend onderwijsaanbod aan de hand van maatschappelijke vraagstukken. Onze faculteit is groot genoeg om nationaal en internationaal het verschil te maken en klein genoeg om persoonlijk onderwijs te bieden. Zo leveren we dagelijks een bijdrage aan een veilige en duurzame wereld. Impact met recht! Zie voor meer informatie https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/rechtsgeleerdheid.

Je wordt aangesteld bij het Instituut voor Strafrecht en Criminologie van de Faculteit Rechtsgeleerdheid van de Universiteit Leiden. Het Instituut bevindt zich in hartje Leiden. De Faculteit der Rechtsgeleerdheid is gevestigd in Leiden en Den Haag en is met ruim 7000 studenten en ongeveer 600 medewerkers een van de grootste faculteiten van Nederland. De faculteit richt zich op innovatief multidisciplinair onderzoek en een steeds vernieuwend onderwijsaanbod aan de hand van maatschappelijke vraagstukken.

De afdeling De afdeling Criminologie van het Instituut Strafrecht & Criminologie aan de Universiteit Leiden verzorgt onderwijs in de bacheloropleidingen Criminologie, Rechtsgeleerdheid en Cybercrime, in de masteropleidingen Forensische Criminologie en Veiligheidsbeleid en in de Engelstalige masteropleiding Criminal Justice. Het (inter)nationale onderzoek is voor een belangrijk deel ingebed in het facultaire onderzoeksprogramma Criminal Justice: Maatschappelijk effectieve strafrechtspleging 2023-2029 Universiteit Leiden)

Dit breng je mee
We zoeken iemand die zelfstandig aan de slag kan. Elke functie is anders dus er is in het begin aandacht voor inwerken. Mochten bepaalde werkzaamheden nieuw zijn voor je, dan kijken we samen wat je nodig hebt en stellen hiervoor een ontwikkelplan op. Deze functie past bij jou als je je herkent in de volgende punten:
  • Je hebt een afgeronde masteropleiding in bestuurskunde, politicologie, beleidswetenschappen, criminologie, organisatiewetenschappen, science and technology studies, (wetenschaps)communicatie of een relevante interdisciplinaire opleiding, Je hebt belangstelling voor evidence-informed policymaking, kennisgebruik, beleidsprocessen of publieke organisaties

jobs.title: PhD Candidate: Museums, Collections and Society - Indigenous Heritage (1.0 FTE)
jobs.description_html:
PhD Candidate
The Department of Archaeological Heritage and Society, Faculty of Archaeology, Leiden University, is looking for a PhD Candidate in the field of Museums, Collections and Society - Indigenous Heritage to join a project funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO) and carried out at the Faculty of Archaeology, Leiden University.

Project Description
The Faculty of Archaeology, Leiden University, seeks to appoint a full-time PhD candidate to carry out research in Museums, Collections and Society - Indigenous Heritage. The successful candidate will join the Department of Archaeological Heritage and Society of our Faculty. The research should lead you to obtain a PhD within a four-year timeframe (1.0 FTE).

jobs.title: PhD in Efficient Online Optimization
jobs.description_html:
How do you optimize a system you can’t fully model, where the operational objectives vary over time, and where safety is a major concern? Drones flying in cluttered changing environment, buildings that manage their own climate, and supply chains under changing market conditions and global events all face this problem. We are looking for a curious, mathematically minded PhD candidate to help build the theory that lets such systems learn on the fly, safely and efficiently and without a central coordinator. If you like elegant algorithms, mathematical challenges and seeing your theory tested on real drones and a real building, we’d like to hear from you.

Information
Bayesian optimization is a data-efficient way to optimize controllers and systems without explicit models, because it learns surrogate models and comes with built-in uncertainty estimates. Its theory still has major gaps when the system is large-scale, distributed and safety-critical, and when the reward and safety constraints change over time. In this project you will develop a new framework that combines safe Bayesian optimization, online learning and distributed estimation, with a strong focus on provable guarantees. This is primarily theoretical research. Your main contributions will be new algorithms and convergence and safety guarantees. Experimental validation will be done together with our partners in the drone lab of the Control Systems group at TU Eindhoven and at the NEST building in Dübendorf, Switzerland.

You will be embedded in the Control Systems group at TU/e, contributing to its research program on intelligent and responsible control of networked systems.

As a PhD candidate, you will:
  • Develop safe Bayesian optimization algorithms for time-varying settings, including adaptive sampling strategies that track moving optima while keeping constraints satisfied at every step.
  • Design distributed learning and optimization schemes in which multiple agents, each with only partial information, cooperate without central coordination.
  • Study how surrogate models and the optimization process can be broken down in time and space to stay tractable in high dimensions and over long horizons.
  • Derive rigorous convergence, regret and safety guarantees for constrained large-scale optimization in non-stationary, safety-critical environments.
  • Use tools from online learning, Gaussian processes, distributed estimation and control theory, and connect them in new ways.
  • Turn your theory into algorithms that can be validated on UAV reference tracking and obstacle avoidance, and on temperature control in a real residential building in Dübendorf, Switzerland.
  • Publish in leading venues in control, optimization and machine learning (e.g., CDC, TAC, NeurIPS, ICML), present your work internationally and work with our academic partners.

This PhD position is in collaboration with Dr. Marta Zagorowska from TU Delft and other collaboration partners in Switzerland.

jobs.title: PhD in Labour Migration in Digital Industrial Policy
jobs.description_html:
This fully funded four-year PhD position is part of an ERC Starting Grant ‘Migrant Labor in EU’s Pivot to Digital Autonomy’ funded by the European Research Council and led by Dr. Julia Rone at the Department of Political Science and Public Administration, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam.

The broader ERC project develops new explanations of how the EU (and individual member states) change labour migration policies to further their digital industrial policy ambitions. The project will offer a novel theorization of how the governance of labour migration intersects with digital capitalism, positioning the EU and its member states as active “catching-up” actors.

The project is structured around four interlinked objectives:
  1. to conceptualize and map migrant labour across the digital stack in the EU, with a focus on flagship EU projects on networks, semiconductor chips, cloud, and AI.
  2. to analyse the strategic interactions between firms, trade unions, and policy makers in shaping digital labour migration regimes
  3. to analyse how migrant workers themselves experience, assess and (fail to) shape labour policies and workplace conditions in digital industry across the stack
  4. to advance a meso- and macro-level theorization of the (re)configuration of labour migration regimes in service of digital capitalism.

The PhD project
The PhD project will primarily contribute to Objectives 2 and 4. Your research will examine specifically how policy makers, employers and trade unions interact to decide who counts as a high-skilled, mid-skilled and low-skilled migrant in the digital industrial sector, what rules apply to them, and what rights they have. The main sectors analysed will be strategic priority sectors in EU digital industrial policy, including networks, semiconductor chips, cloud, and AI.

The project will involve a cross-national comparative policy analysis, process tracing, and qualitative interviews. Experience with survey methods will be a plus but is not essential.

Your duties
As a PhD candidate, you will complete a cumulative PhD dissertation within four years, consisting of four publishable journal articles. Working closely with your supervisory team, led by Dr. Julia Rone, and in collaboration with the ERC research team, which includes two other postdoctoral researchers, you will play an integral role in advancing Objectives 2 and 4 of the ERC project.

As part of your PhD, you will conduct comparative cross-national analyses on labour migration policies in the service of industrial policy, followed by a process tracing to explain the differences in the relative influence of various actors (such as employers or trade unions) in different national contexts and the EU more broadly. Your research will contribute to a broader theorization of the relation between infrastructural labour and digital capitalism in the current AI boom.

You will actively participate in the intellectual life of the Department of Political Science and Public Administration at the VU, present your work at international conferences and workshops, contribute to collaborative research activities within the project, and have the opportunity to undertake research stays abroad within the project’s international network of collaborators.

jobs.title: PhD Position Efficient Online Optimization for Time-Varying Systems
jobs.description_html:
How to avoid learning too much - safe and efficient learning for control

Job description
Inefficient operation of industrial systems, electricity production, and heating systems in buildings is currently responsible for over 50% of overall greenhouse gases emissions. Improving energy efficiency of energy-intensive sectors by implementing advanced control systems has the potential to both improve efficiency and reduce the costs, all while continuing to meet safety requirements. The flexibility of safe and adaptive learning control methods makes them crucial for safety-critical applications. A key difficulty in these learning-based approaches lies in the fact that the algorithm must simultaneously learn the model and guarantee safety. This dual requirement significantly impacts the computational cost of the learning algorithm, particularly in situations where the optimal decision evolves over time. We now aim to develop computationally efficient safe learning methods for time-varying optimal control problems.

Existing safe learning algorithms usually assume that they have unlimited access to the experiments and thus unlimited new data. Approaches using limited data sets have been restricted to Bayesian optimization without safety constraints. Moreover, the algorithms typically rely on the repetitive nature of the experiments, for instance in robotics or precision manufacturing. The unlimited data combined with repetitiveness limit the applicability of safe learning algorithms in problems evolving over time, such as residential buildings. This PhD project will explore the connection between the dynamics of the optimized system with numerical properties of optimization algorithms to provide a framework for safe learning with minimal interactions over time. Sitting at the intersection of theory and applications, the project includes experimental validation of the developed algorithms in collaboration with Dr Giulia de Pasquale from TU Eindhoven (laboratory tests) and partners in Switzerland (Next Evolution in Sustainable Building Technologies (NEST) residential building).

The PhD would join the group of Dr Marta Zagorowska at Delft Center for Systems and Control (DCSC).

jobs.title: PhD Position in Physical Modelling of Backward Erosion Piping
jobs.description_html:
Challenge: Predicting how backward erosion piping develops beneath dikes.

Change: Using physical models to reveal pipe progression and meandering.

Impact: Improving dike safety and enabling more reliable flood protection.

Job description
The Netherlands relies heavily on its dikes for flood protection. However, current models cannot fully predict how dikes may fail when seepage flows erode the sand beneath them. This process is known as backward erosion piping (BEP). The NWO-funded Digital Dikes project aims to improve these predictions by developing advanced digital models that combine monitoring data with probabilistic assessments of pipe progression and its severity. The resulting open-source platform will support more accurate risk assessments and targeted dike reinforcement. Its capabilities will be tested through real-world case studies, co-designed with industry, government and international partners.

In this PhD position you will push the boundaries of experimental BEP modelling by developing new experimental setups, incorporating novel measurement techniques, and exploring mechanisms that remain only marginally understood, such as the 3D meandering behaviour of pipe networks. You will study the driving interactions at the grain-scale and investigate the influence of a non-uniform blanket layer in the propagation stage of BEP. You will also analyse 3D patterns of BEP in a small setup using image analysis and spatial statistics. Your findings will contribute to a better understanding of pipe progression and provide insights that can support the development of improved predictive models.

Your home base will be the Geoscience and Engineering (GSE) department at TU Delft's Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences. The project will be carried out jointly between TU Delft and Deltares and is part of the NWO-funded Digital Dikes consortium. Led by the University of Twente, the consortium brings together Utrecht University, Eindhoven University of Technology, the University of Bologna, Deltares and TU Delft. It is supported by water authorities, Rijkswaterstaat, STOWA, the Dutch Flood Protection Programme and international organisations.

Working in a rich multi-institutional research environment, you will also benefit from opportunities for secondments and short visits to partners in the Digital Dikes network, e.g., Waterschap Drents Overijsselse Delta, Waterschap Hollandse Delta, Fugro, University of Sheffield, and a close collaboration with the PhD project on a fully-resolved simulation of BEP (supervised by University of Twente and University of Lyon). Moreover, the project involves a wide range of training activities, workshops, dedicated sessions at international meetings, to foster scientific and transferable skills for the Jobs of Tomorrow.

jobs.title: Promovendus glucoseregulatie bij vrouwen met diabetes type 1
jobs.description_html:
Twee op de drie vrouwen met diabetes type 1 ervaren een verslechtering van hun glucoseregulatie tijdens de overgang. Deze levensfase kan vijf tot tien jaar duren en vraagt om een meer persoonlijke aanpak.

Binnen het DAME-APersonal-project werk je als onderzoeker van Amsterdam UMC samen met Inreda Diabetic, TNO en AIKON Health. Samen ontwikkelen jullie het eerste geautomatiseerde insulinetoedieningssysteem dat specifiek is ontworpen voor vrouwen rondom en na de overgang.

Je onderzoekt hoe overgangsspecifieke factoren, zoals opvliegers en veranderingen in hartslag, de glucosewaarden beïnvloeden bij vrouwen met en zonder diabetes. Met deze inzichten optimaliseer en test je een gepersonaliseerd glucoseregulatie-algoritme voor de artificiële pancreas (AP) van Inreda Diabetic. Zo draag je bij aan betere zorg op maat voor vrouwen met diabetes type 1 tijdens deze levensfase.

Wil je alvast meer weten over de verschillende fases binnen het PhD-traject? Op deze pagina lees je hierover meer informatie.

Je brengt eerst de bestaande wetenschappelijke literatuur en beschikbare klinische data in kaart. Vervolgens pas je deze kennis toe in twee klinische studies met vrouwen met en zonder diabetes. Je verzamelt en analyseert gegevens van glucosesensoren en gebruikt het digitale biomarkerplatform van TNO om data van wearables te onderzoeken.

Op basis van deze gegevens beoordeel je welke factoren het algoritme kunnen verbeteren. Daarna test je het geoptimaliseerde algoritme in een kleinschalig klinisch onderzoek onder de doelgroep.

Het onderzoek wordt gefinancierd door een beurs van Health Holland. Er is budget voor vier jaar fulltime onderzoek, met als doel om binnen deze periode te promoveren in de Geneeskunde.

jobs.title: PhD Position in Computational Nano-Electrochemistry
jobs.description_html:
Are you fascinated by how electrochemical processes unfold at the nanoscale, and do you want to use advanced computer simulations to help drive the clean energy transition? Are you eager to develop and apply quantum chemical and machine-learning methods to model complex solid-liquid interfaces? Then join the Computational Chemistry Group at the University of Amsterdam!

Join our team!
The Computational Chemistry Group at the Van 't Hoff Institute for Molecular Sciences (HIMS) is looking for a motivated PhD candidate in Computational Nano-Electrochemistry. Controlling electrochemical reactions at the nanoscale is essential for next-generation energy conversion and storage technologies, such as green hydrogen production, CO2 electroreduction, and advanced batteries. In this project, you will bridge the gap between fundamental atomistic physics and real-world electrocatalysis by modeling electric double layers, charge transfer, and catalytic reactivity under operating conditions. You will work in an international, collaborative team of theoretical and computational chemists at Amsterdam Science Park, closely interacting with experimental partners within the Advanced Nano-electrochemistry Institute of the Netherlands (ANION consortium) e.g. AMOLF, University of Twente etc.

This is what you are going to do
  • Develop and apply multi-scale simulation workflows, combining Density Functional Theory (DFT), ab initio molecular dynamics, and machine learning interatomic potentials, to model electrochemical interfaces at the nanoscale.
  • Investigate reaction mechanisms, solvent dynamics, and electric double-layer effects in nano-confined electrochemical systems.
  • Collaborate closely with experimental electrochemists and catalysis researchers to validate theoretical models and guide material design.
  • Publish your research findings in peer-reviewed journals and present your work at national and international scientific conferences.
  • Complete a PhD thesis within four years and assist in teaching undergraduate and master’s chemistry courses and supervising student projects.

This is what we ask of you
  • You hold (or are about to obtain) a Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Chemistry, Physics, Computational Science, Materials Science, or Chemical Engineering.
  • You have a solid background in quantum mechanics, statistical mechanics, machine-learning or atomistic simulations (such as DFT, molecular dynamics, or scientific programming in Python/Linux or C++).
  • When tackling complex scientific problems, you take initiative, think critically, and enjoy exploring creative solutions.
  • You communicate your ideas clearly in English, both in writing and in discussions with colleagues from diverse scientific backgrounds.
  • You enjoy working collaboratively in an international team and actively share code, methods, and insights with fellow group members.

This is what we offer you
You will work in a supportive, open, and well-equipped research environment with access to national and local high-performance computing (HPC) facilities, regular group seminars, and hands-on mentorship tailored to your academic and career growth.

A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is ultimately January 2027 (or early 2027) however, for exceptional candidates this is negotiable. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students.

The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week and ranges between €3,204 (1st year) to €4,051 (last year), scale P. This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile Promovendus is applicable. A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants. The Collective Labour Agreement of Dutch Universities is applicable.

Besides the salary and a vibrant and challenging environment at Science Park we offer you multiple fringe benefits:
  • 232 holiday hours per year (based on fulltime) and extra holidays between Christmas and 1 January;
  • multiple courses to follow from our Teaching and Learning Centre;

This is where you will work

jobs.title: PhD in Free-Space Optical and Radio Communications for Tropospheric Future Networks (ANCHOR)
jobs.description_html:
Are you passionate about working on next-generation wireless communications? We foresee a future where lasers light up the sky and provide seamless connectivity for space and tropospheric networks, together with radio communications. In this PhD research you will study fundamental limits in free-space optical (FSO) communications, turn ideas into experiments, and help shape future networks with a focus on high-throughput and photon-efficiency. Join the European doctoral network with extensive training programs, welcome at the Information and Communication Theory Lab at TU/e, and enjoy a secondment at the Instituto de Telecomunicações, Aveiro in Portugal.

Information
How can we use laser links to connect tropospheric nodes beyond the reach of optical fiber and overcoming the bandwidth limitations of radio? In this PhD, you will study the fundamentals of FSO wireless links for flexible networks on the ground, in the air and in space. The challenge is to combine the capacity of free-space optical communications with the complementary strengths of radio and fiber, creating links that are reliable, use the least amount of photons-per-bit, are adaptive to varying link conditions and approach fundamental limits. Your work will be part of ANCHOR, a European doctoral network exploring optical, THz and radio technologies for future communication networks, including 6G.

Your research will put free-space optical communications at the heart of hybrid FSO–RF–fiber links for terrestrial and airborne networks. You will move between theory, simulation and experiments: develop channel models that capture the essential impairments, explore how modulation, coding and low-level protocols can work together across these links, and design link architectures for experimental evaluation. The goal is to create ultra-high capacity links with high photon efficiency, as needed for tropospheric 6G NTN networks, future data centers in space and as a backup for the high-capacity fiber connections.

You will not be doing this alone. Through ANCHOR, you will join a research community spanning international partners from academia, research institutions and industry, with training that brings together theory and practical skills. You will be enrolled in the PhD program at TU/e, and your project includes a secondment at Instituto de Telecomunicações, Aveiro, Portugal. This is an opportunity to experience another research environment, exchange ideas with international collaborators and build your network beyond Eindhoven.

Throughout this PhD program you will be embedded in the ICT Lab of Signal Processing Systems group of the Department of Electrical Engineering at TU/e. Within the ICT Lab you will work within a dynamic team of approximately twenty researchers under the esteemed leadership of prof. Alex Alvarado and prof. Frans Willems (winner of the Shannon Award 2026). At the ICT Lab, we study information processing in a broad sense. We focus on finding fundamental limits, data processing techniques and architectures that aim at approaching these limits. Main areas of interest are free space optical communications, fiber communications, source coding, channel coding, (multi-user) information theory, security, and machine learning. You will have the opportunity to work with and in the extensive laboratory facilities of the TU/e’s Centre for Wireless Technology (CWTe) and you may use the 4.7 km FSO testbed in Eindhoven for high-throughput experiments. You will work closely with the second ANCHOR PhD at TU/e within the Quantum & Terahertz Systems (QTS) team in the Electro-Optical Communications (ECO) group.

jobs.title: PhD on worker-augmenting technology implementation
jobs.description_html:
Are you eager to study how workers can shape the AI and robotic systems they use, so that technology helps them to improve their quality of working life and their performance? We are looking for a PhD candidate to become part of a multidisciplinary research programme on digital technology and work.

The project
AI and robotics can help workers handle demanding tasks, yet their actual benefits depend on how technologies are selected, introduced and adapted in everyday work. Workers may have too little say in those choices or face an overwhelming number of decisions without adequate support. The Design work package of the NWA-project AUGMENT therefore asks when, how and to what extent workers themselves should be able to decide how technology supports their work. Its goal is to develop evidence-based guidance for worker-augmenting technology implementation across small and large organizations and among workers with different educational backgrounds. Thus, your work will directly contribute to a future of work wherein technology augments rather than replaces human work.

Your research will connect work and organizational psychology, work design, human-technology interaction and participatory design. You will examine which forms of assistance workers need, which technologies can meet those needs, and which job decision opportunities allow workers to adjust technology while sustaining their job quality, well-being and performance. The precise research questions and studies will be refined with the supervisory team and consortium partners.

Your role in this project
Within this project, you will:
  • Conduct fieldwork and collaborate with practical and knowledge workers in small and medium-sized and large organizations, by - among others - performing task and capacity analyses and interviews about their experience of work and desired support.
  • Review relevant AI and robotic applications, interview technology integrators, and help assess their potential to support workers using an available human-machine synergy scoring approach.
  • Develop and use a transportable laboratory setting at TU/e to study simulated work activities and decisions about AI and robotics
  • Design a longitudinal field study of how workers use decision opportunities over time and their implications for labour productivity and meaningful work.
  • Analyse qualitative and quantitative data, develop practical guidance for job redesign with partner organizations, and communicate findings to workers, organizations and other stakeholders.
  • Publish scientific papers, present at international conferences, and complete a doctoral dissertation.

Your research will be embedded in the Human Performance Management (HPM) group of the School of Industrial Engineering at TU/e. HPM develops scientific knowledge and tests theories that uncover and explain (psychological) processes contributing to performance at the organizational, team, and individual level. By examining the ‘people factor’ in operational and innovation processes, HPM aims to ensure that employees can help in bringing organizational strategies to fruition in the most rewarding and efficient way possible. See: https://www.tue.nl/en/research/research-groups/industrial-engineering/human-performance-management for more information about HPM research.

Prof. Dr Pascale Le Blanc (TU/e) is the assigned promotor; your co-promotors are Dr. Anna-Sophie Ulfert-Blank (daily supervisor, TU/e) and Dr. Milan Wolffgramm (daily supervisor, Saxion). Dr. Paul Preenen (Saxion) will serve as scientific advisor. You will closely collaborate with partner organizations and theoretical and practical workers involved in the NWA-project AUGMENT.

The wider AUGMENT consortium connects research on changing work, worker agency, technology design and implementation. Thus, this PhD position offers ample opportunities to work across disciplines, collaborate actively with organizations and researchers from different institutes, and translate research into meaningful guidance and tools for practice.

jobs.title: PhD in cell therapy for hereditary eye diseases: A vision for the future
jobs.description_html:
Developing new treatments starts with models that accurately reflect the disease in the patient. In this four-year PhD project, you will develop and characterize new patient-based preclinical models, both in vitro and in vivo, for inherited retinal diseases, including gyrate atrophy and retinitis pigmentosa. Using these models, you will investigate disease mechanisms and evaluate the potential of cell therapy.

You will work with patient-derived stem cells and develop and optimize differentiation protocols for relevant retinal cell types and tissue models. You will characterize how patients' genetic and clinical characteristics are reflected in the morphology, molecular properties and function of these models. In addition, you will work on the development and characterization of patient-based in vivo models. By connecting findings from cell and tissue models, in vivo models and clinical practice, you will investigate which models and outcome measures are suitable for evaluating new treatments.

These model systems will subsequently form the basis for preclinical cell therapy research. You will investigate how stem cell-derived cells and biomaterials can be combined to create transplantable cell constructs and evaluate their survival, integration and function after transplantation.

The project connects Platform A: Model systems and Pillar 3: Cell-based therapy of the Lifelong VISION consortium. The development of relevant disease models and the development of cell therapy therefore go hand in hand. Through the Emma Center for Personalized Medicine (Emma CPM), the research aligns with the broader ambition of connecting diagnostics and therapy development for rare hereditary diseases.

Lifelong VISION, a Gravitation project funded by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science (2024-2033), will develop new treatments against blindness.

Blindness is among the top 15 most disabling conditions and can manifest in many different ways. In young people, a hereditary retinal condition is the main cause, while in the elderly, age-related macular degeneration is a prominent reason. The Lifelong VISION program is developing a new generation of treatment strategies to prevent blindness: genetic therapies, treatments that target the disease pathways, and cell therapies. State of the art cell and animal models will be developed to test these new therapies in vitro and in vivo. The suitability of each patient group, and the optimal timing for therapeutic intervention is predicted using artificial intelligence, so that the right patient receives the right treatment at the right time. The innovative technologies and strategies developed for eye diseases within our project may serve as blueprints for other diseases and organs.

Ten research institutions participate in the Lifelong Vision project. The project is led by prof. dr. Caroline Klaver from Radboudumc and Erasmus MC; other institutions include Amsterdam UMC, University of Twente, Hubrecht Institute, Eindhoven University of Technology, University of Amsterdam, Utrecht University, Tilburg University, and Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience.

Would you like to know more about the different phases within the PhD trajectory? You can read more about this on this page.

Your main responsibility will be to develop, characterize and apply patient-based preclinical models. In doing so, you will work closely with researchers from Human genetics and clinicians from the Emma Children's Hospital and the department of Ophthalmology at Amsterdam UMC. Together, you will translate clinical questions into experiments and discuss what the results mean for understanding disease mechanisms and developing new treatments.

Your tasks will include:
  • culturing patient-derived stem cells and developing and optimizing differentiation protocols for retinal cell and tissue models.
  • characterizing new in vitro models at the molecular, cellular and functional levels and investigating the extent to which they reflect characteristics of the disease;
  • contributing to the development and characterization of patient-based in vivo models and establishing relevant outcome measures for disease progression and treatment;
  • applying the models to investigate cell therapy, including combining stem cell-derived cells with biomaterials and performing and evaluating preclinical transplantations;
  • integrating experimental findings with genetic and clinical patient data, in collaboration with researchers and clinicians;
  • presenting your results within Lifelong VISION, Emma CPM and at scientific meetings, and incorporating them into scientific publications and a PhD thesis.

jobs.title: PhD position DISKS-ROCK - planet forming disks with JWST and ALMA
jobs.description_html:
PhD position in the group of Prof. Inga Kamp working on planet forming disks 

What are you going to do?

The James Webb Space Telescope shows an intriguing difference between the mid-IR spectra of disks around Solar mass stars and Very Low Mass Stars, the former being oxygen-rich, the latter carbon-rich. Within my ERC project DISKS-ROCK, we will decipher these JWST spectra and characterize the current birth environment of planets forming there. The PhD candidate will perform forward modeling using an existing thermo-chemical disk code. The project comprises applying the code to JWST and ALMA data and investigating physical scenarios that shape mid-IR molecular spectra of the warm inner disks.

jobs.title: PhD Position in Computational Platforms for Advanced Motion Control
jobs.description_html:
Are you excited about pushing the limits of real-time computing for next-generation high-tech systems?

Join Us!
The Informatics Institute at the University of Amsterdam (UvA) is looking for an ambitious PhD candidate to join the Parallel Computing Systems (PCS) group. This position is part of the NWO-funded iCARe project, a collaboration between leading academic institutions and industrial partners.

In this role, you will work at the intersection of real-time systems, control theory, and computational architecture, contributing to the design of next-generation motion control platforms. You will be supervised by Andy Pimentel (UvA) and Benny Akesson (TNO-ESI & UvA). The research is carried out in close collaboration with Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) and ASML, where you will contribute to the development of motion control platforms for semiconductor lithography machines. The position involves close collaboration with industry, and you may be asked to spend part of your time (on average up to one day per week) working on ASML premises in Eindhoven.

This is what you will do
As a PhD candidate, you will work on the design of next-generation computational platforms for advanced industrial motion control systems, with a particular focus on semiconductor lithography.

These systems impose extreme requirements on timing predictability, computational performance, and scalability. Control performance in such systems depends not only on the control algorithms themselves, but also on how they are executed on complex multi-core computing platforms.

Your research will address key questions such as:
  • How do timing effects (e.g. latency, jitter, and resource contention) in computing platforms impact motion control performance and stability?
  • How can computational platforms be designed and configured to explicitly optimize control performance?
  • How can we co-design control algorithms, scheduling strategies, and computing architectures to improve overall system performance?

Concretely, you will:
  • Model and analyze the interaction between control algorithms and computational platforms, including task execution behavior, timing characteristics, and data dependencies;
  • Quantify the effect of timing variations (such as delays and jitter) on motion control performance using realistic system models and industrial use cases;
  • Develop novel scheduling strategies for real-time control workloads, taking into account both computational constraints and control requirements;
  • Design and evaluate computational architectures (e.g. multi-core and heterogeneous platforms) tailored to high-performance motion control systems;
  • Develop design-space exploration methods and tools to analyze trade-offs between performance, scalability, and cost;
  • Validate your methods in an industrial context, in close collaboration with ASML and TU/e, using realistic motion control scenarios.

Your work will directly contribute to the development of next-generation motion control platforms for lithography systems, ensuring both strong scientific contributions and real industrial impact.

What we ask of you
You are motivated to work at the interface of multiple disciplines and enjoy tackling complex system-level challenges.

Your experience and profile:
  • a Master’s degree in Control Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related field;
  • experience with control systems and at least one of the following areas: 1) real-time systems and scheduling, or 2) computer architecture or embedded systems
  • familiarity with optimization, distributed/parallel systems, or system modeling is an advantage;
  • strong analytical and programming skills;
  • ability to work independently as well as in an interdisciplinary team;
  • excellent command of written and spoken English.

This is what we offer you
A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is as soon as possible. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students.

The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week and dependent on relevant experience, ranges between € 3,204 to € 4,051 (scale P). This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile promovendus / PhD student is applicable. A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants. The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable.

Curious about our extensive secondary benefits package? You can read more about it here.

You will work in this team
The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000 and 1,800 staff members working in education, research, and support services.

You will be based at the Institute for Informatics within the Parallel Computing Systems (PCS) group at the University of Amsterdam. The PCS group is internationally recognized for its work in system-level modeling, simulation, and design-space exploration of complex computing systems.

Within the iCARe project, you will collaborate closely with:
  • researchers from TU/e specializing in control systems and system engineering;
  • engineers from ASML working on cutting-edge semiconductor equipment.

This position offers a unique opportunity to combine fundamental research with direct impact on real-world high-tech systems.

jobs.title: PhD Student Biophysics of Cellular Immunity
jobs.description_html:
Mechanical forces have emerged as key regulators of immune functions. In the Vorselen Lab, we develop new technologies to tune the physical information that cells receive and to measure cellular forces. We combine this approach with high-resolution microscopy and molecular biology approaches. Together, this combination provides a very detailed readout of immune cell behavior and helps us understand the regulation of immune processes by physical forces in health and disease.

In this project, you will focus especially on developing new analysis pipelines to allow increased throughput analysis of cellular forces during phagocytosis and by therapeutic cytotoxic T cells. You will conduct experiments combining immune assays and high-resolution fluorescence imaging to obtain the required data. The balance of experiments and analysis is expected to be 25% and 75% respectively. Together, this approach is expected to reveal new insights into the regulation and functional role of biophysical forces by immune cells. The new tools and insights from this research will be a step towards assessing the potential of biophysical parameters as biomarkers.

jobs.title: PhD Position in Data Systems Education
jobs.description_html:
Do you have passion for students and education, and a drive to explore the Data Systems Education landscape? Do you enjoy solving both technical and educational challenges? The Intelligent Data Engineering lab (INDElab) is looking for a PhD candidate.

Join Us!
We are looking for a highly motivated candidate to continue our exploration of the Data Systems Education (DSE) landscape. We approach Data Systems broadly, from query languages to modelling and dependencies, and from Big Data to individual spreadsheets. The education side is also broadly construed and can focus from K-12 all the way through to life-long learning. Our aim is to build theory on the principles behind DSE, and discover in what ways it is similar to, or different from, other disciplines within Computing Education. At this moment, we are less interested in applications such as learning analytics and LLM-supported education.

As this is an open-ended vacancy, please share which aspect of DSE research you are most passionate about in your application materials, and how it connects to our current work in this space.

This is what you will do
Here are some of your responsibilities:
  • conducting independent research resulting in academic publications in peer-reviewed international conferences or journals;
